summary.en: Germanic tribes led by Arminius ambushed and destroyed three Roman legions under Publius Quinctilius Varus. The defeat ended Augustus's plans to push the frontier to the Elbe, leaving the Rhine as the lasting boundary of Roman power.
summary.zh: 阿米尼乌斯率领的日耳曼部落伏击并全歼瓦卢斯统率的三个罗马军团。此役使奥古斯都放弃将边界推进至易北河的计划，莱茵河由此成为罗马势力的长期边界。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of the Teutoburg Forest

note: Month (September 9 CE) is known but not the exact days; the battlefield is identified with the Kalkriese archaeological site (Wikidata coordinates), which most but not all scholars accept.

story.en:
Arminius was a prince of the Cherusci who had served Rome as an auxiliary commander and held Roman citizenship, so Publius Quinctilius Varus, governor of the new province between Rhine and Elbe, trusted him. In 9 CE, probably in September, Arminius lured Varus and three legions, the XVII, XVIII and XIX, off their route with news of a distant revolt.

Cassius Dio describes the column strung out along forest tracks in driving rain while tribesmen attacked it again and again over several days. Varus and his senior officers took their own lives; perhaps 15,000 to 20,000 soldiers and camp followers died. Suetonius reports that Augustus, for months afterwards, would beat his head on a door and cry for Varus to give him back his legions.

When Germanicus reached the site six years later, Tacitus says, he found bleached bones and skulls nailed to trees and buried the dead. Rome never again tried to rule east of the Rhine. Since 1987 finds of coins, weapons and a turf rampart at Kalkriese near Osnabrück have identified the most likely battlefield.
story.zh:
阿米尼乌斯是切鲁西部落的王子，曾在罗马军中担任辅助部队指挥官并取得罗马公民权，因此深得莱茵河与易北河之间新设行省的总督普布利乌斯·昆克蒂利乌斯·瓦卢斯的信任。公元9年（大概在9月），阿米尼乌斯谎报远处有部落叛乱，诱使瓦卢斯率第十七、十八、十九三个军团偏离行军路线。

据卡西乌斯·狄奥记载，罗马纵队在大雨中沿林间小道绵延拉长，日耳曼战士连续数日反复袭击。瓦卢斯和高级军官相继自尽，约一万五千至两万名士兵和随军人员丧生。苏埃托尼乌斯写道，此后数月，奥古斯都常以头撞门，高呼“瓦卢斯，还我军团！”

据塔西佗记载，六年后日耳曼尼库斯来到战场，只见白骨遍地，头骨被钉在树上，他下令掩埋死者。此后罗马再未尝试统治莱茵河以东。1987年以来，在奥斯纳布吕克附近的卡尔克里泽出土了钱币、兵器和草皮壁垒，这里被认为是最可能的战场。

summary.en: Mount Vesuvius erupted and buried Pompeii, Herculaneum and neighbouring towns under ash and pyroclastic flows. Pliny the Younger's letters describe the disaster, in which his uncle Pliny the Elder died; the buried cities became key archaeological sites.
summary.zh: 维苏威火山喷发，火山灰和火山碎屑流掩埋了庞贝、赫库兰尼姆及周边城镇。小普林尼的书信记录了这场灾难，其舅父老普林尼在救援中遇难；被掩埋的城市后来成为重要的考古遗址。

sources.title: Pliny the Younger, Letters VI.16 and VI.20

note: Wikidata gives 24 October 79, supported by a charcoal inscription found at Pompeii in 2018; the manuscript tradition of Pliny's letter gives 24 August. The year is undisputed.

story.en:
Pompeii had still not finished repairing the damage of a severe earthquake in 62 CE when Vesuvius woke in 79. Early in the afternoon a column of ash and pumice rose so high that Pliny the Younger, then seventeen and watching from Misenum across the bay, compared its shape to an umbrella pine. Pumice rained on Pompeii for hours; overnight and next morning, surges of scalding gas and ash swept down the slopes and killed those who remained in Herculaneum and Pompeii.

His uncle Pliny the Elder, admiral of the fleet at Misenum, set out with warships to help people on the shore. He landed at Stabiae and died there on the beach, apparently overcome by fumes. Decades later his nephew described both days in two letters to the historian Tacitus, the earliest detailed eyewitness account of a volcanic eruption to survive.

Excavation began at Herculaneum in 1738 and at Pompeii in 1748. In the 1860s Giuseppe Fiorelli poured plaster into the hollows left by bodies in the ash, and in the 1980s hundreds of skeletons were found in Herculaneum's boat sheds, where people had waited for rescue.
story.zh:
公元62年的一场强烈地震给庞贝造成的破坏尚未完全修复，79年维苏威火山便爆发了。午后不久，火山灰与浮石形成的烟柱直冲云霄，当时十七岁、在海湾对岸米塞努姆观望的小普林尼把它比作一棵伞松。浮石连续数小时落在庞贝城中；当夜至次日清晨，灼热的气体与火山灰形成的火山碎屑涌流冲下山坡，留在赫库兰尼姆和庞贝的人无一幸免。

他的舅父老普林尼是驻米塞努姆的舰队司令，率战舰前去救助岸上的民众。他在斯塔比伊登岸，最终死在海滩上，似乎是被毒烟窒息。数十年后，小普林尼在写给史学家塔西佗的两封信中记述了这两天的经过，这是现存最早的火山喷发详细目击记录。

赫库兰尼姆和庞贝分别于1738年和1748年开始发掘。19世纪60年代，朱塞佩·菲奥雷利把石膏灌入遗体在火山灰中留下的空腔，制成人体模型；20世纪80年代，人们又在赫库兰尼姆的船库里发现了数百具骸骨，他们当时正在那里等待救援。

summary.en: On Emperor Hadrian's orders, Roman legions began building a stone and turf barrier about 118 km long across northern Britain, from the Tyne to the Solway Firth. It marked and controlled the empire's north-western frontier for most of the next three centuries.
summary.zh: 罗马军团奉哈德良皇帝之命，在不列颠北部自泰恩河至索尔威湾修筑长约118公里的石土城墙。此后近三百年间，它大体标志并管控着帝国的西北边疆。

sources.title: UNESCO: Frontiers of the Roman Empire

note: Construction began c. 122 and the main work was completed c. 128; both dates are approximate.

summary.en: Meeting in Milan, the emperors Constantine I and Licinius agreed to grant religious freedom throughout the empire and to restore confiscated property to Christians. The policy ended state persecution and opened the way for Christianity's rise to imperial favour.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世与李锡尼在米兰会晤，同意在帝国境内给予宗教自由，并归还被没收的基督徒财产。这一政策终结了官方迫害，为基督教获得帝国青睐铺平了道路。

note: The agreement was reached at Milan in February 313; the surviving text is a rescript issued by Licinius at Nicomedia in June 313.

story.en:
In October 312 Constantine defeated his rival Maxentius at the Milvian Bridge outside Rome. Christian writers tied the victory to the Christian God: Lactantius says Constantine was told in a dream to put a sign of Christ on his soldiers' shields, while Eusebius later recorded the emperor's own story of a cross of light seen in the sky. A few months later, in February 313, Constantine met Licinius, ruler of the Balkan provinces, at Milan, where Licinius married Constantine's half-sister Constantia.

There the two emperors agreed that Christians and everyone else should be free to follow the religion of their choice, and that churches, cemeteries and other property seized in the Great Persecution should be returned. No edict from Milan survives: what we have is a letter Licinius sent to provincial governors from Nicomedia in June 313, after he had defeated Maximinus Daia, the last persecuting emperor.

The settlement made Christianity a lawful, protected religion. Constantine went on to defeat Licinius in 324, to summon the Council of Nicaea in 325 and to pour imperial money into church building.
story.zh:
312年10月，君士坦丁在罗马城外的米尔维安桥击败对手马克森提乌斯。基督教作家把这场胜利归功于基督教的上帝：拉克坦提乌斯说君士坦丁在梦中受命把基督的符号画在士兵盾牌上；优西比乌后来则记下了皇帝亲口讲述的故事，说他曾看见天空中出现光的十字架。数月后的313年2月，君士坦丁与统治巴尔干诸行省的李锡尼在米兰会晤，李锡尼在此迎娶了君士坦丁的异母妹妹君士坦提娅。

两位皇帝议定：基督徒和其他所有人都可以自由信奉自己选择的宗教；在“大迫害”中被没收的教堂、墓地和其他财产一律归还。米兰并没有留下任何敕令原文，今天所见的是313年6月李锡尼击败最后一位迫害基督徒的皇帝马克西米努斯·代亚之后，从尼科米底亚发给各行省总督的一封信。

这一安排使基督教成为合法并受保护的宗教。此后君士坦丁于324年击败李锡尼，325年召开尼西亚公会议，并以帝国财力大规模兴建教堂。

summary.en: Constantine I formally dedicated his rebuilt city on the site of Byzantium as a new imperial residence, Constantinople. It became the capital of the eastern Roman, later Byzantine, empire for more than eleven centuries.
summary.zh: 君士坦丁一世在拜占庭旧址上重建城市，并正式将其奉献为新的帝国驻地——君士坦丁堡。此后一千一百余年，它一直是东罗马即拜占庭帝国的首都。

note: QID is the historical city of Constantinople, whose inception Wikidata gives as 330.

summary.en: Gothic forces, mainly Tervingi under Fritigern joined by Greuthungi cavalry, destroyed an eastern Roman army near Adrianople; Emperor Valens was killed. The disaster left the Goths settled inside the empire and is often seen as a turning point in the late Roman crisis.
summary.zh: 以弗里提格伦为首的哥特人（主要为特尔温吉部，并有格鲁森尼骑兵增援）在阿德里安堡附近歼灭东罗马军队，瓦伦斯皇帝阵亡。此役使哥特人得以定居帝国境内，常被视为罗马晚期危机的转折点。

note: Date is secure; the exact battlefield, some kilometres north of Adrianople (Edirne), is unknown—coordinates follow Wikidata's approximation.

story.en:
In 376 tens of thousands of Goths, driven west by the Huns, begged to be let across the Danube, and Emperor Valens agreed. Ammianus Marcellinus says corrupt Roman officers then starved the refugees and sold them dogs for food in exchange for their children as slaves. The Goths under Fritigern rose in revolt and ravaged Thrace for two years.

Valens came west from Antioch. His nephew Gratian, the western emperor, was hurrying to join him, but Valens, told that the enemy numbered only about 10,000, chose not to wait. On 9 August 378 his army marched for hours in the summer heat and found the Goths drawn up around their wagon circle. While envoys were still talking, Roman units attacked without orders; then the Greuthungi cavalry under Alatheus and Saphrax returned from foraging and struck the Roman flank. Ammianus says two-thirds of the army perished. Valens's body was never found; one report had him burned to death in a farmhouse.

His successor Theodosius could not expel the Goths. A treaty in 382 let them settle south of the Danube under their own leaders as allies, a precedent for the later Germanic kingdoms.
story.zh:
376年，数以万计的哥特人被匈人驱赶西迁，恳求渡过多瑙河，瓦伦斯皇帝予以准许。据阿米阿努斯·马塞利努斯记载，腐败的罗马军官随后让难民忍饥挨饿，用狗肉换取他们的孩子作奴隶。弗里提格伦率哥特人起兵反抗，蹂躏色雷斯达两年之久。

瓦伦斯从安条克西进。他的侄子、西部皇帝格拉提安正赶来会师，但瓦伦斯听信敌军只有约一万人，决定不再等待。378年8月9日，罗马军在盛夏烈日下行军数小时，发现哥特人已围绕车阵列好阵势。双方使者尚在谈判，部分罗马部队便擅自出击；这时阿拉塞乌斯和萨弗拉克斯率领的格鲁森尼骑兵觅粮归来，直扑罗马军侧翼。阿米阿努斯称全军三分之二覆没。瓦伦斯的遗体始终未被找到，一说他被困在一座农舍中被烧死。

继任者狄奥多西无力驱逐哥特人。382年的和约允许他们作为同盟者在多瑙河以南定居，由本族首领统率，这成为后来日耳曼诸王国的先例。

name.en: Sack of Rome by the Visigoths

summary.en: Visigoths under Alaric I entered Rome and plundered it for three days, the first time in about 800 years that the city had fallen to a foreign enemy. The shock across the Roman world prompted Augustine to write The City of God.
summary.zh: 阿拉里克一世率领的西哥特人攻入罗马城并劫掠三日，这是近八百年来罗马首次落入外敌之手。此事震动整个罗马世界，促使奥古斯丁写下《上帝之城》。

sources.title: Orosius, Seven Books of History against the Pagans VII.39
Augustine, De civitate Dei, Book I
Procopius, History of the Wars III.2

story.en:
Alaric, a Gothic commander who wanted land for his people and a high Roman command for himself, besieged Rome three times in two years. The emperor Honorius, safe behind the marshes of Ravenna, refused every deal. On the night of 24 August 410 the Goths entered through the Salarian Gate.

For three days they looted the city and burned some buildings near the Senate house, but Orosius stresses that Alaric, himself a Christian, ordered the basilicas of St Peter and St Paul to be treated as sanctuaries, and that Goths escorted fugitives there. Among the captives was the emperor's half-sister Galla Placidia. Procopius tells a story, almost certainly invented, that Honorius was horrified to hear Rome had perished until he learned it was the city, not his pet rooster named Roma.

In Bethlehem, Jerome wrote that the city that had captured the world had itself been captured. Pagans blamed the abandonment of the old gods, and Augustine answered them in The City of God, begun around 413. Alaric marched south hoping to reach Africa but died within months; according to Jordanes he was buried beneath the diverted bed of the river Busento.
story.zh:
阿拉里克是一位哥特统帅，他想为族人争得土地，也为自己谋求罗马的高级军职，两年内三次围攻罗马。躲在拉文纳沼泽之后的霍诺留皇帝拒绝了一切交易。410年8月24日夜，哥特人从萨拉里亚门攻入城中。

他们劫掠了三天，并焚毁元老院附近的一些建筑。但奥罗修斯强调，本身信奉基督教的阿拉里克下令把圣彼得与圣保罗两座大教堂作为庇护所，还有哥特士兵护送难民前往。皇帝的异母妹妹加拉·普拉西提阿也成了俘虏。普罗柯比讲过一个几乎可以肯定是虚构的故事：霍诺留听说“罗马完了”时大惊失色，后来才明白指的是城市，而不是他那只名叫“罗马”的宠物公鸡。

远在伯利恒的哲罗姆写道，征服了世界的城市自己也被征服了。异教徒归咎于抛弃古老神祇，奥古斯丁约于413年开始写作《上帝之城》予以回应。阿拉里克挥师南下，希望渡海前往非洲，却在数月内去世；据约达尼斯记载，他被葬在布森托河被改道后的河床之下。

summary.en: A coalition of Romans under Flavius Aetius and Visigoths under Theodoric I fought Attila's Hunnic army in north-eastern Gaul. Theodoric fell, but Attila withdrew, ending his invasion of Gaul.
summary.zh: 罗马统帅埃提乌斯与西哥特国王狄奥多里克一世的联军，在高卢东北部迎战阿提拉的匈人大军。狄奥多里克阵亡，但阿提拉被迫撤退，其入侵高卢的行动就此终止。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of the Catalaunian Plains

note: The site is unknown—proposals range from near Châlons-en-Champagne to near Troyes; the coordinates (Wikidata) lie by the traditional 'Camp d'Attila' at La Cheppe, north-east of Châlons. The day (20 June, per Wikidata) is a modern reconstruction. Wikidata's English label is 'Battle of the Maureaco Fields'.

story.en:
In spring 451 Attila led Huns, Ostrogoths, Gepids and other subject peoples across the Rhine into Gaul. He was besieging Orléans when Flavius Aetius, the Western Empire's leading general, arrived with an army joined by the Visigothic king Theodoric I, the Alans and other allies. Attila withdrew east, and the armies met on open plains somewhere in Champagne.

Jordanes, writing a century later, says Attila's soothsayers foretold defeat for the Huns but the death of an enemy commander, and Attila accepted battle late in the day. Theodoric was killed in the fighting, but his Visigoths, led by his son Thorismund, drove the Huns back to their wagon laager. There, Jordanes claims, Attila heaped up a pyre of horse saddles, ready to burn himself rather than be taken. Instead the coalition let him go: Thorismund hurried home to secure his crown, and Aetius may have preferred to keep the Huns as a counterweight to the Goths. Jordanes's 165,000 dead is not credible.

Attila invaded Italy the next year and sacked Aquileia, but turned back after meeting envoys including Pope Leo I. He died in 453, and his empire soon broke apart.
story.zh:
451年春，阿提拉率匈人以及东哥特人、格皮德人等附属民族越过莱茵河进入高卢。他正在围攻奥尔良时，西罗马帝国首席统帅弗拉维乌斯·埃提乌斯率军赶到，同来的有西哥特国王狄奥多里克一世、阿兰人和其他盟军。阿提拉向东撤退，双方在香槟某处的开阔平原上相遇。

一个世纪后写作的约达尼斯说，阿提拉的占卜者预言匈人将战败，但敌方一位统帅会阵亡，于是阿提拉直到傍晚才接战。狄奥多里克战死，但他的儿子托里斯蒙德率西哥特人把匈人逼回车阵。据约达尼斯称，阿提拉在那里用马鞍堆起火堆，准备在被俘前自焚。然而联军放走了他：托里斯蒙德急于回国稳固王位，埃提乌斯或许也想留着匈人牵制哥特人。约达尼斯所说的十六万五千名死者并不可信。

次年阿提拉入侵意大利，洗劫阿奎莱亚，但在会见包括教宗利奥一世在内的使团后退兵。他于453年去世，其帝国随即瓦解。

name.zh: 罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯被废黜

summary.en: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus at Ravenna and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople. The date conventionally marks the end of the Western Roman Empire, though its decline had been long and gradual.
summary.zh: 日耳曼将领奥多亚克在拉文纳废黜少年皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯，并将帝国徽章送往君士坦丁堡。这一年通常被视为西罗马帝国灭亡的标志，尽管其衰落是一个漫长渐进的过程。

sources.title: Peter Heather, The Fall of the Roman Empire (2005)

story.en:
By the 470s the Western Empire held little more than Italy, and its emperors were made and unmade by generals. In 475 Orestes, who had once been Attila's secretary, drove out the emperor Julius Nepos and put his own young son Romulus on the throne; people mocked the boy as Augustulus, "little Augustus".

The barbarian soldiers of the army in Italy demanded a third of the land to settle on. Orestes refused, and they rallied to Odoacer, an officer of Germanic origin. Orestes was captured and executed at Piacenza in August 476, and on 4 September Odoacer entered Ravenna. According to the Anonymus Valesianus he pitied Romulus for his youth and good looks, spared him, and sent him to live in Campania on a pension of 6,000 solidi a year.

Odoacer took no imperial title. Instead he had the Senate send the imperial regalia to the emperor Zeno in Constantinople with the message that one emperor was enough, and he ruled Italy as king until Theodoric the Ostrogoth killed him in 493. Contemporaries saw little break; only in the next century did writers treat 476 as the end of the Western Empire.
story.zh:
到5世纪70年代，西罗马帝国已几乎只剩下意大利，皇帝的废立全由将领操纵。475年，曾任阿提拉秘书的欧瑞斯特斯赶走了皇帝尤利乌斯·尼波斯，把自己年幼的儿子罗慕路斯扶上皇位；人们戏称这孩子为“奥古斯都路斯”，即“小奥古斯都”。

驻意大利军队中的蛮族士兵要求分得三分之一的土地定居。欧瑞斯特斯拒绝后，他们转而拥戴日耳曼裔军官奥多亚克。476年8月，欧瑞斯特斯在皮亚琴察被俘处死；9月4日，奥多亚克进入拉文纳。据《瓦莱西亚努斯佚名残篇》记载，他怜惜罗慕路斯年少俊秀，饶他不死，把他送往坎帕尼亚居住，每年给予六千索利都斯的年金。

奥多亚克没有称帝，而是让元老院把皇帝徽章送给君士坦丁堡的芝诺皇帝，并传话说一位皇帝已经足够。他以国王身份统治意大利，直到493年被东哥特人狄奥多里克杀死。当时的人并不觉得这是一次断裂，直到下一个世纪，史家才把476年当作西罗马帝国的终结。

summary.en: Clovis I, king of the Franks, was baptised a Catholic Christian by Bishop Remigius at Reims. Choosing Nicene Christianity rather than the Arianism of other Germanic kings won him the support of the Gallo-Roman church and population.
summary.zh: 法兰克国王克洛维一世在兰斯由主教雷米吉乌斯施洗，皈依天主教。他选择尼西亚派而非其他日耳曼诸王所信奉的阿里乌派，因而赢得高卢—罗马教会与民众的支持。

sources.title: Gregory of Tours, History of the Franks II.31

note: Gregory of Tours' chronology implies c. 496; modern historians place the baptism anywhere between 496 and 508. Wikidata has no date.

summary.en: Justinian I dedicated the rebuilt church of Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, designed by Anthemius of Tralles and Isidore of Miletus. Its vast dome made it the largest church in Christendom for nearly a thousand years.
summary.zh: 查士丁尼一世为君士坦丁堡重建的圣索菲亚大教堂举行献堂礼，该教堂由特拉勒斯的安提米乌斯和米利都的伊西多尔设计。其巨大的穹顶使之在近千年间都是基督教世界最大的教堂。

note: Wikidata's start date (23 February 532) is when rebuilding began; this record marks the dedication of 27 December 537.

summary.en: Bubonic plague, caused by Yersinia pestis, reached the Mediterranean through Egypt in 541 and struck Constantinople in 542, killing a large share of its population. Recurring waves until the mid-8th century weakened the Byzantine Empire and its neighbours.
summary.zh: 由鼠疫杆菌引起的腺鼠疫于541年经埃及传入地中海世界，542年侵袭君士坦丁堡，造成大量人口死亡。此后直至8世纪中叶的反复流行，削弱了拜占庭帝国及其邻邦。

sources.title: Procopius, History of the Wars II.22–23
Lester K. Little (ed.), Plague and the End of Antiquity: The Pandemic of 541–750 (2007)

note: Wikidata spans all waves (541–750); endYear here marks the first wave. Placed at Constantinople, the best-documented outbreak (542).

name.zh: 倭马亚王朝征服伊比利亚

summary.en: Berber and Arab forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad crossed from North Africa, defeated King Roderic at the Guadalete in 711 and within a few years overran most of the Visigothic kingdom. The conquest created al-Andalus, Muslim-ruled Iberia, which survived in part until 1492.
summary.zh: 塔里克·伊本·齐亚德率领柏柏尔人和阿拉伯人从北非渡海，711年在瓜达莱特河击败国王罗德里克，数年内攻占西哥特王国大部。这次征服建立了安达卢斯，穆斯林在伊比利亚的统治部分延续至1492年。

sources.title: Roger Collins, The Arab Conquest of Spain, 710–797 (1989)

note: Coordinates and date are those of the opening Battle of Guadalete (Wikidata Q504172); the span 711–726 follows Wikidata.

story.en:
Visigothic Spain in 711 was divided by a disputed succession: Roderic had taken the throne, but rival nobles did not accept him. That spring Tariq ibn Ziyad, a Berber commander serving Musa ibn Nusayr, the Umayyad governor of North Africa, crossed the strait with an army made up mostly of Berbers and landed beneath the rock that still bears his name, Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq). Later legend blamed the invasion on Count Julian of Ceuta, avenging Roderic's seduction of his daughter, but the story first appears in Arabic accounts written well over a century later.

Roderic hurried south from campaigning in the north and was defeated near the Guadalete in July; he vanished in the battle. Tariq pressed on to the capital, Toledo, and in 712 Musa followed with a largely Arab army, taking Seville and Mérida. Some towns were won by agreement: the treaty of 713 with the Gothic lord Theodemir in Murcia survives, granting his people their churches in exchange for tribute.

Within a few years only the mountains of the far north lay outside Muslim rule. There a noble named Pelayo defeated a Muslim force at Covadonga, traditionally around 722, founding the kingdom of Asturias, from which later Christian kingdoms grew.
story.zh:
711年的西哥特西班牙因王位之争而分裂：罗德里克登上王位，但对立的贵族并不承认他。这年春天，倭马亚王朝北非总督穆萨·伊本·努赛尔麾下的柏柏尔将领塔里克·伊本·齐亚德率领一支以柏柏尔人为主的军队渡过海峡，在至今仍以他命名的岩山——直布罗陀（意为“塔里克山”）脚下登陆。后世传说把这次入侵归咎于休达的朱利安伯爵，称他为报复罗德里克诱奸其女儿而引狼入室，但这一说法最早见于一个多世纪后成书的阿拉伯文献。

罗德里克从北方战场匆忙南下，7月在瓜达莱特河附近战败，在战斗中下落不明。塔里克乘胜直取首都托莱多；712年，穆萨又率一支以阿拉伯人为主的军队渡海，攻占塞维利亚和梅里达。有些城镇是通过协议归附的：713年与穆尔西亚的哥特领主狄奥德米尔订立的条约保存至今，条约以缴纳贡赋为条件，保障其臣民保留教堂。

数年之内，只有极北的山区仍在穆斯林统治之外。在那里，一位名叫佩拉约的贵族在科瓦东加击败一支穆斯林军队（传统上定在约722年），建立阿斯图里亚斯王国，后来的基督教诸王国即由此发展而来。

summary.en: Frankish forces under Charles Martel defeated an Umayyad army led by Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, governor of al-Andalus, between Poitiers and Tours. The victory checked Muslim raids north of the Pyrenees and strengthened the Carolingian family's power.
summary.zh: 查理·马特率领的法兰克军队在普瓦捷与图尔之间击败安达卢斯总督阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·加菲基率领的倭马亚军队。此役遏制了穆斯林越过比利牛斯山向北的袭扰，并巩固了加洛林家族的权势。

sources.title: Continuations of the Chronicle of Fredegar
Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, ch. 52

note: Traditionally 10 October 732 (Wikidata); a minority argue for 733. The site between Tours and Poitiers is uncertain; placed at Moussais-la-Bataille (Vouneuil-sur-Vienne), the most often proposed site. Wikidata's point (46.99, 0.53) is roughly the midpoint of the two cities.

story.en:
In 732 Abd al-Rahman al-Ghafiqi, governor of al-Andalus, led a large raiding army over the western Pyrenees. He crushed Duke Odo of Aquitaine near Bordeaux and pushed north towards Tours, whose abbey of St Martin was one of the richest shrines in Gaul. Odo, long Charles Martel's rival, had to ask him for help.

Charles, mayor of the palace and real ruler of the Frankish kingdom, brought an army of mostly foot soldiers to meet the invaders between Poitiers and Tours. After days of skirmishing, the Arab and Berber cavalry charged the Frankish line. The Mozarabic Chronicle of 754 says the northerners stood firm like a wall, as if frozen together like ice, and cut the attackers down. Abd al-Rahman was killed, and in the night his army slipped away, leaving its tents behind.

Edward Gibbon later imagined that, but for this victory, the Qur'an might be taught at Oxford. Most historians now see a halt to one major raid rather than the saving of Christendom: Muslim forces held Narbonne until 759. But the battle made Charles, later nicknamed Martel, "the Hammer", the unrivalled master of Francia, and his grandson was Charlemagne.
story.zh:
732年，安达卢斯总督阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼·加菲基率大军越过比利牛斯山西段劫掠。他在波尔多附近击溃阿基坦公爵厄德，挥师北上直指图尔，那里的圣马丁修道院是高卢最富有的圣地之一。长期与查理·马特对立的厄德只得向他求援。

查理身为宫相，是法兰克王国的实际统治者。他率领一支以步兵为主的军队，在普瓦捷与图尔之间迎击来犯者。经过数日对峙与小规模交锋，阿拉伯和柏柏尔骑兵向法兰克阵线发起冲锋。据754年的《莫札拉布编年史》记载，北方人像一堵墙般岿然不动，如冰块般紧紧凝结在一起，将来敌砍倒。阿卜杜勒·拉赫曼阵亡，其军队趁夜撤走，连营帐都弃之不顾。

爱德华·吉本后来设想，若没有这场胜利，牛津大学讲授的也许就是《古兰经》了。如今多数史家认为，此役只是挡住了一次大规模劫掠，并非拯救了基督教世界：穆斯林直到759年仍据有纳博讷。但这一仗使查理——后来被称为“马特”，即“铁锤”——成为法兰克无可匹敌的主宰，而他的孙子就是查理曼。

summary.en: From the raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne in 793 until the mid-11th century, Scandinavian seafarers raided, traded and settled from Ireland to the Volga. They founded the Kingdom of Jórvík, Normandy and the settlement of Iceland, and helped shape the early Rus' state.
summary.zh: 自793年袭击林迪斯法恩修道院起至11世纪中叶，斯堪的纳维亚航海者从爱尔兰到伏尔加河一带劫掠、贸易与定居。他们建立了约克维京王国和诺曼底，定居冰岛，并参与塑造了早期罗斯国家。

label.zh: 罗斯人袭击君士坦丁堡
留里克入主诺夫哥罗德（传说）

label.en: Harald Hardrada falls at Stamford Bridge
label.zh: 哈拉尔德·哈德拉达战死斯坦福桥

sources.title: Russian Primary Chronicle (Povest' vremennykh let), entry for 862
Alcuin, letter to King Æthelred of Northumbria (793)

note: 793–1066 is a conventional span; Wikidata gives no dates. Several route dates (Novgorod 862, Iceland 874) are traditional.

story.en:
In 793 raiders from the sea plundered the monastery of Lindisfarne off the Northumbrian coast. The scholar Alcuin, writing from Charlemagne's court, lamented that such terror had never before appeared in Britain. It was the start of more than two centuries in which Scandinavians, in fast, shallow-draught ships, reached almost every coast and river of Europe.

At first they raided; then they stayed. A great army that landed in England in 865 seized York in 866 and settled much of the north and east, the later Danelaw. Norse raiders founded Dublin as a fortified base in 841; in 911 the Frankish king Charles the Simple granted the chieftain Rollo land on the lower Seine that became Normandy. Settlers reached Iceland from about 870 and Greenland in the 980s, and around 1000 Leif Erikson's voyages touched North America, where a Norse site survives at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland. In the east, Swedes called Rus' traded down the Dnieper and Volga to Constantinople and the markets of the Islamic world; the Primary Chronicle says the Rus' leader Rurik was invited to rule Novgorod in 862.

The age is conventionally closed in 1066, when Harald Hardrada of Norway fell at Stamford Bridge. By then Scandinavia itself had become Christian kingdoms.
story.zh:
793年，海上来的劫掠者洗劫了诺森布里亚海岸外的林迪斯法恩修道院。身在查理曼宫廷的学者阿尔昆悲叹，不列颠从未出现过如此恐怖之事。此后两百多年间，斯堪的纳维亚人驾驶轻快、吃水浅的船只，几乎抵达欧洲的每一处海岸和河流。

他们起初只是劫掠，后来便定居下来。865年登陆英格兰的“异教徒大军”于866年攻占约克，并在北部和东部大片土地上定居，即后来的“丹麦法区”。841年挪威劫掠者建立了据点都柏林；911年，法兰克国王“糊涂者”查理把塞纳河下游的土地封给首领罗洛，这里后来成为诺曼底。约870年起移民抵达冰岛，980年代到达格陵兰；约1000年，莱夫·埃里克松的航行到达北美，纽芬兰的兰塞奥兹牧草地至今保留着一处维京人遗址。在东方，被称为“罗斯”的瑞典人沿第聂伯河和伏尔加河而下，与君士坦丁堡和伊斯兰世界的市场通商；据《往年纪事》记载，罗斯首领留里克于862年应邀统治诺夫哥罗德。

按惯例，这个时代以1066年挪威国王哈拉尔·哈德拉达在斯坦福桥阵亡为终点。那时斯堪的纳维亚本身也已成为基督教王国。

summary.en: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Charlemagne emperor of the Romans in St Peter's Basilica on Christmas Day. The act revived a western imperial title, deepened the alliance between the papacy and the Franks, and strained relations with Byzantium.
summary.zh: 圣诞节当天，教宗利奥三世在圣伯多禄大殿为法兰克国王查理曼加冕为“罗马人的皇帝”。此举复兴了西方的帝号，加深了教廷与法兰克人的同盟，也使与拜占庭的关系趋于紧张。

sources.title: Royal Frankish Annals, entry for 801 (year reckoned from Christmas)

story.en:
In April 799 enemies of Pope Leo III ambushed him during a procession in Rome and tried to blind him and cut out his tongue. Leo escaped and fled across the Alps to Charlemagne at Paderborn. The Frankish king, who already ruled most of western Christendom, came to Rome in late 800; on 23 December Leo publicly swore an oath clearing himself of the charges his accusers had made.

Two days later, at the Christmas mass in St Peter's, Leo placed a crown on Charlemagne's head as he rose from prayer, and the crowd acclaimed him emperor of the Romans. Einhard, his biographer, claims Charlemagne said that he would not have entered the church that day had he known what the pope intended. Historians still argue whether this was modesty, irritation at the pope taking the lead, or worry about Constantinople.

Byzantium was then ruled by the empress Irene, and some in the West argued that the imperial throne was in effect vacant. The Byzantines saw a usurpation and only in 812 recognised Charlemagne as an emperor, not as emperor of the Romans. The idea of a western empire crowned by the pope lasted, in the Holy Roman Empire, until 1806.
story.zh:
799年4月，教宗利奥三世在罗马参加游行时遭政敌伏击，对方企图弄瞎他的眼睛、割掉他的舌头。利奥逃脱后翻越阿尔卑斯山，投奔在帕德博恩的查理曼。这位法兰克国王当时已统治西方基督教世界的大部分地区，他于800年末来到罗马；12月23日，利奥公开宣誓，洗清控告者加在他身上的罪名。

两天后，在圣伯多禄大殿的圣诞弥撒上，查理曼祈祷完毕起身时，利奥把一顶皇冠戴在他头上，众人高呼他为“罗马人的皇帝”。传记作者艾因哈德称，查理曼曾说，若事先知道教宗的打算，那天他根本不会进教堂。史家至今仍在争论，这究竟是谦逊，还是不满教宗抢占主动，抑或是顾虑君士坦丁堡的反应。

当时拜占庭由女皇伊琳娜统治，西方有人认为皇位实际上空缺。拜占庭人视之为僭越，直到812年才承认查理曼是一位“皇帝”，但不承认他是“罗马人的皇帝”。由教宗加冕的西方帝国这一观念，在神圣罗马帝国一直延续到1806年。

summary.en: The three surviving sons of Louis the Pious divided the Carolingian Empire: Charles the Bald took West Francia, Louis the German East Francia, and Lothair I a middle kingdom with the imperial title. The partition foreshadowed the later division between France and Germany.
summary.zh: 虔诚者路易的三个儿子瓜分加洛林帝国：秃头查理得西法兰克，日耳曼人路易得东法兰克，洛泰尔一世得中法兰克并保有皇帝称号。这次分割预示了日后法兰西与德意志的分野。

story.en:
Louis the Pious, Charlemagne's son, had spent much of his reign fighting his own sons over how the empire would be shared. After his death in 840 the eldest, Lothair, claimed authority over the whole as emperor. His brothers Louis the German and Charles the Bald joined forces and defeated him at Fontenoy in June 841, one of the bloodiest battles of the age.

In February 842 the two younger brothers renewed their alliance at Strasbourg. Their cousin Nithard, who fought at Fontenoy and wrote a history of the war, recorded the oaths: Louis swore in an early form of French so that Charles's army could understand, and Charles in Old High German for Louis's men. They are among the oldest surviving texts in either language.

After more than a year of surveys and bargaining, the brothers met at Verdun in August 843. Charles took the west, Louis the lands east of the Rhine, and Lothair a long middle strip from Frisia through Aachen and Burgundy to Italy, with the imperial title. The middle kingdom soon broke up; its northern part, named Lotharingia after Lothair's son, became a borderland that France and Germany fought over for a thousand years.
story.zh:
查理曼之子虔诚者路易在位期间，大部分时间都在与自己的儿子们争夺帝国如何分配。840年他去世后，长子洛泰尔以皇帝身份要求统辖全境。两个弟弟日耳曼人路易和秃头查理联手，于841年6月在丰特努瓦击败他，这是那个时代最血腥的战役之一。

842年2月，两个弟弟在斯特拉斯堡重申盟约。他们的堂兄弟尼特哈德亲历丰特努瓦之战，并写了一部战争史，记下了誓词：路易用早期法语宣誓，以便查理的军队听懂；查理则用古高地德语向路易的部下宣誓。这些誓词是两种语言现存最古老的文本之一。

经过一年多的勘查与讨价还价，兄弟三人于843年8月在凡尔登会面。查理得到西部，路易得到莱茵河以东，洛泰尔得到从弗里斯兰经亚琛、勃艮第直至意大利的狭长中部地带，并保有皇帝称号。中法兰克王国很快解体，其北部以洛泰尔之子的名字命名为洛林，此后一千年间一直是法德两国争夺的边疆。

summary.en: Grand Prince Vladimir I of Kyiv accepted Byzantine Christianity, was baptised and had the people of Kyiv baptised in the Dnieper. The conversion tied the Rus' to the church and culture of Constantinople, shaping the later Orthodox identity of Ukraine, Belarus and Russia.
summary.zh: 基辅大公弗拉基米尔一世接受拜占庭基督教并受洗，随后令基辅民众在第聂伯河中受洗。这次皈依使罗斯与君士坦丁堡的教会和文化紧密相连，塑造了日后乌克兰、白俄罗斯和俄罗斯的东正教认同。

note: 988 is the Primary Chronicle's date; Vladimir's own baptism may have taken place at Chersonesos in Crimea, and some historians date it 987–989.

summary.en: Papal legates led by Cardinal Humbert laid a bull excommunicating Patriarch Michael Cerularius on the altar of Hagia Sophia, and the patriarch replied in kind. The mutual excommunications came to symbolise the lasting split between the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox churches.
summary.zh: 以枢机主教洪贝尔为首的教宗使节将绝罚君士坦丁堡宗主教米海尔·色路拉里乌斯的诏书置于圣索菲亚大教堂祭坛上，宗主教随即予以反绝罚。这次相互绝罚成为罗马天主教与东正教长期分裂的象征。

sources.title: Henry Chadwick, East and West: The Making of a Rift in the Church (2003)

note: The rupture was a long process; 1054 is its conventional symbolic date.

story.en:
Rome and Constantinople had been drifting apart for centuries, divided by language, by the Latin addition of the filioque ("and the Son") to the Nicene Creed, by the use of unleavened bread in the Eucharist, and above all by the pope's claim to authority over the whole Church. Around 1053 Patriarch Michael Cerularius closed the Latin churches in Constantinople, and Pope Leo IX sent three legates, led by the combative Cardinal Humbert of Silva Candida, to settle matters.

Talks went badly. Leo died in April 1054, which arguably ended the legates' authority, but on 16 July Humbert walked into Hagia Sophia during the afternoon liturgy and laid a bull of excommunication against Cerularius on the altar. The legates then left the city. Days later a synod in Constantinople excommunicated the legates in turn.

At the time this looked like one more quarrel, and contacts continued; the crusades, and above all the sack of Constantinople by the Fourth Crusade in 1204, made the rift permanent. In 1965 Pope Paul VI and Patriarch Athenagoras I lifted the mutual excommunications of 1054, though the churches remain separate.
story.zh:
罗马与君士坦丁堡数百年来渐行渐远：语言不同；拉丁教会在《尼西亚信经》中加入了“和子”句；圣餐使用无酵饼；最根本的是教宗主张对整个教会拥有最高权威。约1053年，宗主教米海尔·色路拉里乌斯关闭了君士坦丁堡的拉丁教堂，教宗利奥九世派出以好斗的席尔瓦·坎迪达枢机主教洪贝尔为首的三名使节前去解决争端。

谈判很不顺利。1054年4月利奥九世去世，按理说使节的授权随之失效，但7月16日洪贝尔仍在下午礼仪进行时走进圣索菲亚大教堂，把绝罚色路拉里乌斯的诏书放在祭坛上，随后使节们离开了这座城市。几天后，君士坦丁堡的主教会议也绝罚了这些使节。

当时这看上去只是又一次争吵，双方往来并未中断；是十字军东征，尤其是1204年第四次十字军攻陷并洗劫君士坦丁堡，使裂痕再难弥合。1965年，教宗保禄六世与普世牧首阿特纳哥拉一世撤销了1054年的相互绝罚，但两教会至今仍未合一。

summary.en: Duke William of Normandy defeated and killed King Harold II near Hastings, opening the Norman conquest of England. William was crowned at Westminster on Christmas Day 1066, and a new French-speaking aristocracy transformed English government, language and architecture.
summary.zh: 诺曼底公爵威廉在黑斯廷斯附近击败并杀死英格兰国王哈罗德二世，开启诺曼征服。威廉于1066年圣诞节在威斯敏斯特加冕，说法语的新贵族阶层由此深刻改变了英格兰的政治、语言和建筑。

sources.title: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (MSS D and E), entry for 1066

story.en:
England had three claimants in 1066. Harold Godwinson was crowned the day after Edward the Confessor died; Harald Hardrada of Norway invaded in the north; William of Normandy said Edward had promised him the throne. Harold crushed the Norwegians at Stamford Bridge on 25 September, and three days later William landed at Pevensey.

Harold marched south and drew up his shield wall on Senlac Hill. For most of a day the Norman cavalry and archers could not break it. Feigned retreats seem to have lured parts of the English line downhill, and late in the afternoon Harold fell (the Bayeux Tapestry famously shows a man struck near the eye, though which figure is Harold is debated).

William was crowned in Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day. Within twenty years almost every great English estate had passed to Norman lords, as the Domesday Book of 1086 records, and Anglo-Norman French reshaped the English language.
story.zh:
1066年英格兰王位有三位争夺者：忏悔者爱德华去世次日，哈罗德·葛温森加冕；挪威国王哈拉尔·哈德拉达从北方入侵；诺曼底公爵威廉则声称爱德华曾许诺把王位传给他。9月25日，哈罗德在斯坦福桥大败挪威军，三天后威廉在佩文西登陆。

哈罗德挥师南下，在森拉克山上列起盾墙。诺曼骑兵与弓箭手整整一天未能突破。诺曼人的佯退似乎诱使部分英军冲下山坡，傍晚时分哈罗德阵亡（贝叶挂毯上那位眼部中箭的人物最为著名，但究竟哪一位是哈罗德仍有争议）。

威廉于圣诞节在威斯敏斯特修道院加冕。不到二十年，英格兰几乎所有大地产都落入诺曼领主之手（见1086年《末日审判书》），盎格鲁-诺曼法语也深刻改变了英语。

summary.en: Answering Pope Urban II's call at Clermont in 1095, armies of western knights marched through Constantinople and Anatolia, took Antioch in 1098 and captured Jerusalem in July 1099. The crusade founded Latin states in the Levant.
summary.zh: 响应教宗乌尔班二世1095年在克莱蒙发出的号召，西欧骑士大军经君士坦丁堡、穿越安纳托利亚，于1098年攻占安条克，1099年7月攻陷耶路撒冷，并在黎凡特建立了一系列拉丁国家。

label.zh: 十字军集结莱茵兰（科隆）
大军经君士坦丁堡渡海

sources.title: Robert the Monk, Historia Iherosolimitana, Book I

note: Wikidata's 'point in time' of 1090 appears erroneous; its start/end (1096–1099) are used. Event placed at Clermont, where the crusade was preached.

story.en:
In 1095 envoys of the Byzantine emperor Alexios I Komnenos asked Pope Urban II for soldiers against the Seljuk Turks. On 27 November, in a field outside Clermont, Urban called on western knights to free the Christians of the East and Jerusalem itself, promising remission of sins; according to one chronicler the crowd answered "God wills it!" The response far exceeded what anyone expected.

Popular bands led by preachers such as Peter the Hermit set off first; some massacred Jewish communities in the Rhineland, and most were destroyed by the Turks in Anatolia. The princes' armies, under leaders including Godfrey of Bouillon, Raymond of Toulouse and Bohemond of Taranto, gathered at Constantinople in 1097, helped take Nicaea and won at Dorylaeum. The siege of Antioch dragged on for eight months; after it fell in June 1098 the crusaders were themselves besieged, until the claimed discovery of the Holy Lance, doubted even then, lifted their spirits and they routed the relief army.

On 15 July 1099 they stormed Jerusalem, recently taken by the Fatimids, and slaughtered many of its inhabitants. Godfrey became its ruler, refusing the title of king. Four crusader states, Edessa, Antioch, Jerusalem and Tripoli, would endure for up to two centuries.
story.zh:
1095年，拜占庭皇帝阿历克塞一世·科穆宁的使节请求教宗乌尔班二世派兵对抗塞尔柱突厥人。11月27日，乌尔班在克莱蒙城外的一片原野上号召西方骑士解救东方的基督徒和耶路撒冷，并许诺赦免罪罚；据一位编年史家记载，群众高呼“这是上帝的旨意！”响应之热烈远远超出了所有人的预料。

隐士彼得等布道者率领的民众队伍最先出发，其中一些人在莱茵兰屠杀了犹太社群，大部分人后来在安纳托利亚被突厥人消灭。由布永的戈弗雷、图卢兹的雷蒙、塔兰托的博希蒙德等人率领的诸侯大军于1097年在君士坦丁堡会合，协助攻下尼西亚，又在多里莱乌姆获胜。安条克之围持续了八个月；1098年6月城破后，十字军反遭围困，直到有人声称找到了“圣枪”（当时就有人怀疑其真伪），士气大振，才击溃了援军。

1099年7月15日，十字军攻破不久前被法蒂玛王朝夺回的耶路撒冷，屠杀了大量居民。戈弗雷成为该城统治者，但拒绝称王。埃德萨、安条克、耶路撒冷和的黎波里四个十字军国家，有的延续了近两个世纪。

summary.en: Facing baronial rebellion, King John of England agreed at Runnymede to a charter limiting royal power and guaranteeing certain legal rights. Though annulled within months, its reissued versions became a foundation of English law and a symbol of constitutional government.
summary.zh: 面对贵族叛乱，英格兰国王约翰在兰尼米德同意颁布一份限制王权、保障若干法律权利的特许状。该文件数月后即被废止，但其后的重订版本成为英格兰法律的基石和宪政的象征。

sources.title: J. C. Holt, Magna Carta (3rd ed., 2015)

story.en:
King John lost Normandy to Philip II of France in 1204, and his expensive attempt to win it back ended in defeat at Bouvines in 1214. Barons angry at his heavy taxes, arbitrary fines and seizures renounced their allegiance, and in May 1215 they took London. John agreed to negotiate, and on the meadow of Runnymede beside the Thames, between Windsor and Staines, a charter dated 15 June was sealed (not signed) and copies were sent across the kingdom.

Most of its clauses dealt with feudal grievances such as inheritance payments, widows' rights and fish weirs. But two promised that no free man would be imprisoned or dispossessed except by the lawful judgement of his peers or the law of the land, and that justice would not be sold, denied or delayed. Another set up a council of twenty-five barons to enforce the deal.

Neither side kept it. Pope Innocent III annulled the charter in August and civil war followed. After John died in 1216, his son's regents reissued it, and the 1225 version became part of English law. Four originals of 1215 survive, and later readers, from 17th-century parliamentarians to American revolutionaries, made it a symbol of government under law.
story.zh:
1204年，约翰王把诺曼底丢给了法王腓力二世；他耗费巨资试图夺回，结果1214年在布汶战役中失败。贵族们早已不满他的重税、任意罚款和没收财产，于是宣布不再效忠，并于1215年5月攻占伦敦。约翰同意谈判。在泰晤士河畔、温莎与斯坦斯之间的兰尼米德草地上，一份署期6月15日的特许状加盖了国王印玺（并非签名），抄本被送往全国各地。

其中大多数条款涉及封建权益方面的不满，如继承税、寡妇权利和河中捕鱼堰等。但有两条承诺：非经同侪的合法裁决或依据国法，任何自由人不得被监禁或剥夺财产；国王不出卖、不拒绝、不拖延正义。另有一条规定由二十五名贵族组成委员会监督执行。

双方都没有遵守。教宗英诺森三世于8月宣布特许状无效，内战随之爆发。1216年约翰死后，其子的摄政者重新颁布了它，1225年的版本成为英格兰法律的一部分。1215年的原件有四份传世。后来从17世纪的议会派到美国革命者，都把它奉为法治政府的象征。

summary.en: A Mongol army under Batu Khan besieged and stormed Kyiv, the old capital of the Rus', destroying much of the city. Its fall completed the Mongol conquest of the Rus' principalities, which became tributaries of the Golden Horde.
summary.zh: 拔都率领的蒙古军队围攻并攻陷罗斯旧都基辅，城市大部被毁。基辅的陷落标志着蒙古对罗斯诸公国征服的完成，此后诸公国沦为金帐汗国的附庸。

note: Wikidata gives 28 Nov–6 Dec 1240; Rus' chronicles give differing days (some 19 Nov) for the fall.

summary.en: A series of wars between the Plantagenet kings of England and the Valois kings of France over the French crown and English lands in France. English victories such as Crécy and Agincourt were reversed after Joan of Arc helped relieve Orléans in 1429; by 1453 England held only Calais.
summary.zh: 英格兰金雀花王朝与法兰西瓦卢瓦王朝围绕法国王位及英格兰在法领地展开的一系列战争。英军虽有克雷西、阿金库尔等大捷，但1429年贞德助解奥尔良之围后局势逆转；至1453年英格兰仅保有加来。

sources.title: Jonathan Sumption, The Hundred Years War (5 vols., 1990–2023)

note: Placed at Orléans, the war's turning point (1429).

story.en:
When Charles IV of France died in 1328 without a son, his nephew Edward III of England had a claim through his mother, but the French nobility chose Philip of Valois. Edward did homage for his duchy of Aquitaine, yet tensions grew, and in May 1337 Philip VI declared the duchy confiscated. Edward answered by claiming the French crown.

The war came in bursts separated by truces and plague. English longbowmen won at Crécy in 1346, and after an eleven-month siege Calais fell. Froissart tells how six leading citizens came out with nooses round their necks to offer their lives for the town, and were spared when Queen Philippa begged Edward for mercy. At Poitiers in 1356 the Black Prince captured King John II. After a long French recovery, Henry V's victory at Agincourt in 1415 and the Treaty of Troyes of 1420 made him heir to France.

The tide turned in 1429, when Joan of Arc helped lift the siege of Orléans and saw Charles VII crowned at Reims. She was burned at Rouen in 1431, but French armies, newly strong in artillery, took Normandy and then Gascony, winning the last battle at Castillon in 1453. England kept only Calais, lost in 1558.
story.zh:
1328年法王查理四世去世，没有留下儿子。英王爱德华三世通过母亲享有继承权，但法国贵族推举了瓦卢瓦的腓力。爱德华为其阿基坦公国向法王行了臣服礼，但矛盾日益加深；1337年5月，腓力六世宣布没收该公国，爱德华则以要求法国王位作为回应。

战争时断时续，其间夹杂着休战和瘟疫。1346年英格兰长弓手在克雷西获胜，经过十一个月的围困，加来陷落。据傅华萨记载，六位城中显要脖套绞索出城，愿以性命换取全城平安，后因王后菲莉帕向爱德华求情而获赦免。1356年，黑太子在普瓦捷俘虏了法王约翰二世。法国经过长期恢复后，亨利五世又于1415年在阿金库尔大胜，1420年的《特鲁瓦条约》使他成为法国王位继承人。

1429年局势逆转：贞德助解奥尔良之围，并护送查理七世在兰斯加冕。她于1431年在鲁昂被处以火刑，但炮兵日益强大的法军先后收复诺曼底和加斯科涅，1453年在卡斯蒂永赢得最后一战。英格兰只保住了加来，而加来也在1558年失守。

summary.en: Plague carried on Genoese ships from the Black Sea reached Sicily in October 1347 and swept across Europe within four years, killing perhaps a third to a half of the population. The catastrophe reshaped labour, religion and society across the continent.
summary.zh: 随热那亚船只从黑海传来的鼠疫于1347年10月抵达西西里，四年内席卷欧洲，可能造成三分之一至一半人口死亡。这场浩劫深刻改变了整个欧洲的劳动力、宗教与社会。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Decameron, Introduction to the First Day
Ole J. Benedictow, The Black Death 1346–1353: The Complete History (2004)
Gabriele de' Mussi, Historia de morbo (c. 1348)
K. I. Bos et al., "A draft genome of Yersinia pestis from victims of the Black Death", Nature 478 (2011)

note: Wikidata dates the pandemic 1346–1352, starting in the Golden Horde; 1347 marks its arrival in Europe (Messina), and it reached Moscow in 1353, so endYear follows Benedictow.

story.en:
Plague reached the Black Sea in the mid-1340s, apparently out of Central Asia. The notary Gabriele de' Mussi wrote that Mongol besiegers of the Genoese port of Caffa catapulted plague corpses over the walls, a story often repeated but of uncertain reliability. In October 1347 Genoese galleys brought the disease to Messina, and within months it was in Genoa, Venice and Marseille.

It crossed France and Italy in 1348, England in 1348–49 and Germany in 1349, and Scandinavia and Russia by 1353. In Florence, Boccaccio described how the sick were abandoned by their own families and the dead buried in trenches, layer upon layer. Modern estimates of the death toll mostly lie between a third and a half of Europe's population; Benedictow argues for as much as 60 per cent. Many blamed the Jews, and despite bulls of Pope Clement VI condemning the violence, Jewish communities in Strasbourg and scores of other towns were massacred. DNA recovered from victims buried in London has since confirmed that the cause was the bacterium Yersinia pestis.

With so many dead, surviving workers demanded higher wages. Rulers tried to freeze pay, as in England's Ordinance of Labourers of 1349, but labour shortage loosened serfdom in western Europe, and the plague kept returning for three centuries.
story.zh:
14世纪40年代中期，鼠疫似乎从中亚传到了黑海沿岸。公证人加布里埃莱·德穆西记载，围攻热那亚港口卡法的蒙古军队用投石机把染疫的尸体抛进城内；这个故事流传甚广，但可靠性存疑。1347年10月，热那亚的桨帆船把疾病带到墨西拿，数月之内便传到热那亚、威尼斯和马赛。

1348年疫情席卷法国和意大利，1348至1349年传遍英格兰，1349年传到德意志，1353年前蔓延至斯堪的纳维亚和罗斯。薄伽丘在佛罗伦萨描写道，病人被自己的家人抛弃，死者被一层层埋进壕沟。现代学者对死亡人数的估计大多在欧洲人口的三分之一到一半之间，贝内迪克托则认为高达百分之六十。许多人归罪于犹太人，尽管教宗克雷芒六世颁布诏书谴责暴行，斯特拉斯堡等数十座城镇的犹太社群仍遭屠杀。后来从伦敦遇难者遗骸中提取的DNA证实，病原体是鼠疫耶尔森菌。

死者如此之多，幸存的劳动者纷纷要求提高工资。统治者试图冻结工资，如英格兰1349年的《劳工条例》，但劳动力短缺使西欧的农奴制逐渐松动。此后三个世纪，鼠疫仍反复卷土重来。

summary.en: The allied armies of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania under Władysław II Jagiełło and Vytautas crushed the Teutonic Knights; Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen was killed. The defeat began the long decline of the Teutonic Order's state in Prussia.
summary.zh: 波兰王国与立陶宛大公国联军在瓦迪斯瓦夫二世·雅盖沃和维陶塔斯指挥下大败条顿骑士团，大团长乌尔里希·冯·容金根阵亡。此役开启了条顿骑士团国家在普鲁士的长期衰落。

sources.title: Jan Długosz, Annales seu cronicae incliti Regni Poloniae, Book XI

summary.en: Dante Alighieri completed the Commedia, an allegorical poem in three parts—Inferno, Purgatorio and Paradiso—written in the Tuscan vernacular during his exile. It became a founding work of Italian literature and of the literary Italian language.
summary.zh: 但丁在流亡期间完成了以托斯卡纳方言写成的寓言长诗《神曲》，分为《地狱篇》《炼狱篇》《天堂篇》三部。该作品成为意大利文学和意大利文学语言的奠基之作。

sources.title: Giovanni Boccaccio, Trattatello in laude di Dante

note: Composed c. 1308–1321; Wikidata gives c. 1320. Paradiso was finished at Ravenna shortly before Dante's death in September 1321.

name.en: Founding of the University of Bologna

summary.en: Bologna's law school, traditionally dated to 1088, grew from teachers of Roman law into a university organised by student associations. Often regarded as the oldest university in continuous operation, it became a model for others across Europe.
summary.zh: 博洛尼亚的法学院按传统说法创立于1088年，由讲授罗马法的教师群体发展为由学生团体组织的大学。它通常被视为持续办学至今最古老的大学，并成为欧洲各地大学的典范。

sources.title: Hastings Rashdall, The Universities of Europe in the Middle Ages, vol. 1 (1895)

note: 1088 (Wikidata inception) is a traditional date fixed by a committee in the 1880s; teaching of law at Bologna is documented from the late 11th–12th century.

name.zh: 谷登堡《圣经》与活字印刷

summary.en: In Mainz, Johannes Gutenberg's workshop completed the 42-line Latin Bible, the first major book printed in Europe with movable metal type. Printing spread to more than 200 European towns by 1500, transforming the circulation of knowledge.
summary.zh: 约翰内斯·谷登堡在美因茨的作坊完成了四十二行拉丁文《圣经》，这是欧洲首部以金属活字印刷的重要书籍。到1500年，印刷术已传播至欧洲两百多个城镇，彻底改变了知识的传播方式。

sources.title: Albert Kapr, Johann Gutenberg: The Man and His Invention (1996)

note: The Bible has no colophon; it is dated c. 1454–55 from a letter of Enea Silvio Piccolomini (March 1455) and a rubricator's note of 1456. Wikidata has no date.

story.en:
Johannes Gutenberg, a goldsmith's son from Mainz, was experimenting with printing in Strasbourg by the late 1430s, as a lawsuit of 1439 reveals. Back in Mainz, with large loans from the merchant Johann Fust, he combined several inventions: a hand mould for casting identical letters quickly, a tin-lead alloy for type, an oil-based ink and a screw press of the kind long used for pressing wine.

The Bible was his great project: about 1,280 pages in two volumes, set in a Gothic type imitating fine manuscripts, with 42 lines to a column. Perhaps 160 to 180 copies were printed, most on paper and the rest on vellum, and illuminators added decoration by hand. In March 1455 the future Pope Pius II wrote that he had seen sections of it at Frankfurt, so clear they could be read without spectacles, and that every copy was already spoken for. That same year Fust sued Gutenberg and took over much of the workshop with Peter Schöffer. Today 49 copies survive, many incomplete.

Metal type had been used earlier in Korea, but Gutenberg's system suited Europe's alphabet and market. Printers trained in Mainz spread out across Europe, and by 1500 millions of printed books were in circulation.
story.zh:
约翰内斯·谷登堡是美因茨一位金匠的儿子。从1439年的一桩诉讼可知，他在14世纪30年代末已在斯特拉斯堡试验印刷。回到美因茨后，他依靠商人约翰·福斯特的大笔贷款，把几项发明结合起来：能快速铸造统一字模的手持铸模、锡铅合金活字、油性油墨，以及仿照榨酒用螺旋压机制成的印刷机。

《圣经》是他的宏大工程：两卷共约一千二百八十页，采用模仿精美手抄本的哥特式字体，每栏四十二行。印数大约在一百六十至一百八十部之间，多数印在纸上，其余印在犊皮纸上，再由装饰画师手工添加彩饰。1455年3月，后来成为教宗庇护二世的皮科洛米尼写信说，他在法兰克福见过其中的部分书帖，字迹清晰到不戴眼镜也能阅读，而且每一部都已被预订一空。同年，福斯特起诉谷登堡，与彼得·舍弗尔一起接管了作坊的大部分。如今存世的有四十九部，许多并不完整。

朝鲜半岛更早就使用过金属活字，但谷登堡的体系更适合欧洲的字母文字和图书市场。在美因茨学成的印刷工散布到欧洲各地，到1500年，流通的印刷书籍已达数百万册。

summary.en: After a siege of about seven weeks, the Ottoman army of Sultan Mehmed II stormed Constantinople; the last emperor, Constantine XI Palaiologos, died in the fighting. The conquest ended the Byzantine Empire and made the city the Ottoman capital.
summary.zh: 经过约七周的围攻，苏丹穆罕默德二世的奥斯曼军队攻破君士坦丁堡，末代皇帝君士坦丁十一世·巴列奥略战死。此役终结了拜占庭帝国，该城随后成为奥斯曼帝国的首都。

sources.title: Kritoboulos of Imbros, History of Mehmed the Conqueror
Steven Runciman, The Fall of Constantinople 1453 (1965)

summary.en: After a ten-year war (1482–1492), Emir Muhammad XII surrendered Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia, to Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile. The surrender completed the Christian Reconquista.
summary.zh: 经过十年战争（1482—1492年），埃米尔穆罕默德十二世将伊比利亚最后的穆斯林政权格拉纳达交给阿拉贡的斐迪南二世与卡斯蒂利亚的伊莎贝拉一世，基督教的“收复失地运动”至此完成。

sources.title: L. P. Harvey, Islamic Spain, 1250 to 1500 (1990)

note: QID is the Granada War; Wikidata's start date for it (1492) conflicts with the standard 1482 start, so only the surrender date is used here.

summary.en: Sailing for the Crown of Castile, Christopher Columbus left Palos with three ships, crossed the Atlantic via the Canary Islands and reached the Bahamas on 12 October 1492. His return in 1493 launched sustained European contact with, and colonisation of, the Americas.
summary.zh: 哥伦布受卡斯蒂利亚王室资助，率三艘船从帕洛斯出发，经加那利群岛横渡大西洋，于1492年10月12日抵达巴哈马。1493年他返航后，欧洲开始与美洲持续接触并殖民美洲。

label.zh: 离开加那利群岛戈梅拉岛
登陆瓜纳哈尼（圣萨尔瓦多岛）

label.en: Santa María wrecked; La Navidad founded
label.zh: 圣玛丽亚号触礁，建立纳维达德

sources.title: Christopher Columbus, Diario of the First Voyage (abstract by Bartolomé de las Casas)
Samuel Eliot Morison, Admiral of the Ocean Sea (1942)

note: The Wikidata item covers all four voyages (1492–1504); this record is the first.

story.en:
Columbus, a Genoese navigator, spent years trying to win backing for a westward route to Asia; he badly underestimated the distance, and Portuguese experts turned him down. In April 1492, shortly after the conquest of Granada, Isabella and Ferdinand agreed to his terms. On 3 August the Santa María, Pinta and Niña, with about 90 men, left Palos, refitted in the Canary Islands and on 6 September sailed west.

After more than a month without land the crews grew restless. Then at about two in the morning of 12 October a lookout on the Pinta, Rodrigo de Triana, sighted land, though Columbus claimed the promised reward for a light he said he had seen hours earlier. The island, called Guanahani by its Lucayan Taíno people, he named San Salvador. He went on to Cuba and Hispaniola, convinced he was near Japan and China. On Christmas Eve the Santa María ran aground off Hispaniola, and 39 men were left in a fort built from its timbers, La Navidad.

Columbus reached Palos again on 15 March 1493, bringing gold, parrots and several captive Taíno. On his return later that year, he found La Navidad destroyed and its garrison dead.
story.zh:
热那亚航海家哥伦布多年来四处寻求资助，想向西航行到达亚洲；他严重低估了航程，葡萄牙专家拒绝了他。1492年4月，攻克格拉纳达不久，伊莎贝拉和斐迪南同意了他的条件。8月3日，“圣玛丽亚”号、“平塔”号和“尼尼亚”号载着约九十人从帕洛斯出发，在加那利群岛整修后，于9月6日向西驶去。

一个多月不见陆地，船员们开始躁动不安。10月12日凌晨两点左右，“平塔”号上的瞭望员罗德里戈·德特里亚纳发现了陆地，但哥伦布声称自己几小时前就看到了灯光，领走了许诺的赏金。这座岛被当地卢卡约泰诺人称为瓜纳哈尼，哥伦布将其命名为圣萨尔瓦多。他接着到达古巴和伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，深信自己已接近日本和中国。平安夜，“圣玛丽亚”号在伊斯帕尼奥拉岛外搁浅，哥伦布用船上的木料筑起拉纳维达德堡，留下三十九人驻守。

1493年3月15日，哥伦布回到帕洛斯，带回了黄金、鹦鹉和几名被俘的泰诺人。同年晚些时候他再度来到这里，发现拉纳维达德已被摧毁，守军全部死亡。

name.zh: 路德发表《九十五条论纲》

summary.en: Martin Luther, a theology professor at Wittenberg, circulated 95 theses disputing the sale of indulgences and sent them to Archbishop Albert of Mainz. Rapidly printed and spread, they sparked the Protestant Reformation that divided Western Christianity.
summary.zh: 维滕贝格大学神学教授马丁·路德提出《九十五条论纲》，抨击出售赎罪券，并寄呈美因茨大主教阿尔布雷希特。论纲经印刷迅速传播，引发了导致西方基督教分裂的宗教改革。

sources.title: Martin Luther, Disputatio pro declaratione virtutis indulgentiarum (1517)

note: Luther's covering letter to Archbishop Albert is dated 31 October 1517; whether he also nailed the theses to the Castle Church door is debated.

story.en:
In 1517 the Dominican friar Johann Tetzel was selling indulgences just across the border of Electoral Saxony. The campaign was meant to fund the rebuilding of St Peter's in Rome, and half the takings were to repay the Fugger bank, which had lent Archbishop Albert of Mainz the money to buy papal permission to hold several sees at once. Martin Luther, an Augustinian friar who lectured on the Bible at Wittenberg, believed the trade sold ordinary people a false sense of security.

On 31 October he sent Albert a letter enclosing 95 Latin propositions for academic debate. The famous picture of Luther hammering them to the Castle Church door rests on an account by Philipp Melanchthon written after Luther's death; Melanchthon had not yet arrived in Wittenberg in 1517, and historians still argue over whether it happened. What is certain is that printers in Nuremberg, Leipzig and Basel had the theses out before the year was over, and German versions soon followed.

The quarrel escalated quickly. Pope Leo X threatened excommunication in 1520, Luther burned the papal bull in public, and at the Diet of Worms in 1521 he refused to recant. The movement that grew from his challenge split Western Christendom.
story.zh:
1517年，多明我会修士约翰·台彻尔在萨克森选侯国边境外兜售赎罪券。这笔收入名义上用于重建罗马圣彼得大教堂，其中一半却要偿还富格尔银行——美因茨大主教阿尔布雷希特曾向它借钱，向教廷买下同时兼领数个主教区的特许。在维滕贝格讲授《圣经》的奥古斯丁会修士马丁·路德认为，这种买卖让普通信徒误以为花钱就能买到得救的保障。

10月31日，路德致信阿尔布雷希特，随信附上九十五条供学术辩论的拉丁文论纲。路德手执铁锤把论纲钉上城堡教堂大门的著名场景，出自梅兰希通在路德去世后写下的记述，而梅兰希通1517年尚未来到维滕贝格，此事是否属实至今仍有争论。可以确定的是，不到年底，纽伦堡、莱比锡和巴塞尔的印刷商便已印出论纲，德文译本也随即问世。

争端迅速升级。1520年，教宗利奥十世以绝罚相威胁，路德当众焚毁教宗诏书；1521年在沃尔姆斯帝国会议上，他拒绝撤回自己的主张。由他的挑战发展起来的运动，最终使西方基督教世界一分为二。

name.zh: 哥白尼出版《天体运行论》

summary.en: Nicolaus Copernicus's De revolutionibus orbium coelestium was printed in Nuremberg shortly before his death. Placing the Sun near the centre of the universe with Earth orbiting it, the book laid the groundwork for the Scientific Revolution.
summary.zh: 哥白尼的《天体运行论》在纽伦堡付印，出版于他去世前不久。该书提出太阳位于宇宙中心附近、地球绕其运行，为科学革命奠定了基础。

sources.title: Owen Gingerich, The Book Nobody Read (2004)

story.en:
Nicolaus Copernicus spent most of his working life as a canon of Frombork Cathedral on the Baltic coast of Royal Prussia, doing astronomy alongside church administration. Around 1514 he circulated a short handwritten sketch, the Commentariolus, proposing that the Earth turns daily on its axis and circles the Sun once a year, but for decades he held back the full mathematical treatise.

The push came from a young Lutheran mathematician, Georg Joachim Rheticus, who arrived from Wittenberg in 1539, studied with him for two years and took the manuscript to the Nuremberg printer Johannes Petreius. The theologian Andreas Osiander, who saw it through the press, inserted an unsigned preface presenting the theory as a mere aid to calculation; Kepler later revealed who had written it. According to Copernicus's friend Tiedemann Giese, a printed copy reached the dying astronomer only on the day he died, 24 May 1543.

The book was far from ignored. Owen Gingerich's census of surviving first and second editions found many of them annotated by working astronomers. Kepler and Galileo built on it, and in 1616 the Catholic Church suspended it until corrected.
story.zh:
尼古拉·哥白尼一生大部分时间在波罗的海沿岸王室普鲁士的弗龙堡大教堂担任教士，在教会事务之余从事天文研究。约1514年，他以手稿形式传阅了一篇简短的《短论》，提出地球每天绕轴自转、每年绕太阳公转一周，但完整的数学论著却迟迟不肯发表。

促成出版的是年轻的路德派数学家雷蒂库斯。他于1539年从维滕贝格前来求教，追随哥白尼两年，随后把手稿带到纽伦堡印刷商佩特赖乌斯处付印。负责监印的神学家奥西安德尔擅自加入一篇未署名的序言，把日心说说成仅供计算的假设，后来开普勒揭示了序言的真正作者。据哥白尼的友人蒂德曼·吉泽记述，印好的书直到1543年5月24日才送到病榻前，哥白尼当天便去世了。

此书绝非无人问津。天文学史家欧文·金格里奇普查现存的第一、二版，发现其中许多留有天文学家的批注。开普勒和伽利略在此基础上继续推进，而天主教会于1616年将它列为“修正前停止流通”。

summary.en: The parliament meeting at Lublin turned the personal union of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania into a single Commonwealth with a jointly elected monarch and common Sejm. The new state was one of Europe's largest until its partitions in the late 18th century.
summary.zh: 在卢布林召开的议会将波兰王国与立陶宛大公国的君合国转变为统一的联邦，两国共同选举君主、设立共同议会。这一新国家在18世纪末被瓜分之前，一直是欧洲面积最大的国家之一。

sources.title: Norman Davies, God's Playground: A History of Poland, vol. 1 (1981)

summary.en: Philip II of Spain sent a fleet of about 130 ships to escort an invasion army from Flanders to England. Harried in the Channel, scattered by fireships off Calais and beaten at Gravelines, the Armada fled round Scotland and Ireland, losing many ships to storms.
summary.zh: 西班牙国王腓力二世派出约130艘战舰，意图护送驻佛兰德的军队入侵英格兰。无敌舰队在英吉利海峡遭英舰袭扰，在加来外海被火船冲散，又在格拉沃利讷战败，被迫绕道苏格兰和爱尔兰返航，途中因风暴损失惨重。

sources.title: Garrett Mattingly, The Defeat of the Spanish Armada (1959)
Colin Martin and Geoffrey Parker, The Spanish Armada (1988)

note: Event coordinates follow Wikidata (off Plymouth, the first engagement). English contemporaries used Old Style dates, ten days behind the Spanish (New Style) ones.

summary.en: Beginning with the Defenestration of Prague, a revolt of Bohemian Protestants against Habsburg rule grew into a European war involving the Holy Roman Empire, Sweden, Denmark, France and Spain. The fighting devastated Germany, where perhaps a fifth or more of the population died.
summary.zh: 以布拉格掷出窗外事件为开端，波希米亚新教徒反抗哈布斯堡统治的起义演变为一场席卷欧洲的大战，神圣罗马帝国、瑞典、丹麦、法国和西班牙相继卷入。战火重创德意志地区，可能有五分之一以上的人口丧生。

sources.title: Peter H. Wilson, Europe's Tragedy: A History of the Thirty Years War (2009)

note: Placed at Prague Castle, site of the Defenestration of 23 May 1618.

story.en:
On 23 May 1618 a party of Protestant nobles climbed to a chancery room in Prague Castle, accused two of Emperor Matthias's regents of trampling on Bohemia's religious liberties, and threw them, along with their secretary, out of the window. All three survived the fall; Catholics credited angels, Protestant pamphlets a heap of dung. The rebels offered the Bohemian crown to Frederick V of the Palatinate, who lost it at the Battle of White Mountain in 1620 and was mocked as the Winter King.

The provincial revolt drew in one power after another. Christian IV of Denmark intervened and was beaten by the imperial armies of Tilly and Wallenstein. Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden landed in 1630 and swept south until he was killed at Lützen in 1632. In 1635 Catholic France openly joined the war against the Habsburgs. When Tilly's troops stormed Magdeburg in 1631, perhaps 20,000 of its people died.

Armies lived off the land, spreading plague and famine wherever they marched. Peter Wilson estimates that the Empire lost about a fifth of its population, and far more in the worst-hit regions, before the Peace of Westphalia ended the fighting in 1648.
story.zh:
1618年5月23日，一群新教贵族登上布拉格城堡的一间公署，指责皇帝马蒂亚斯的两名摄政官践踏波希米亚的宗教自由，随即把二人连同一名秘书扔出窗外。三人竟都大难不死：天主教徒说是天使相救，新教小册子则说他们落在了粪堆上。起事者把波希米亚王冠献给普法尔茨选帝侯腓特烈五世，他在1620年白山战役中惨败，被讥为“冬王”。

这场地方叛乱把列强一个接一个卷了进来。丹麦国王克里斯蒂安四世出兵干预，被蒂利和华伦斯坦统率的帝国军击败；瑞典国王古斯塔夫二世·阿道夫于1630年登陆，一路南下，直到1632年在吕岑阵亡；1635年，信奉天主教的法国也公开对哈布斯堡家族开战。1631年蒂利的军队攻陷马格德堡，城中约两万人丧生。

军队所到之处就地征粮劫掠，瘟疫和饥荒随之蔓延。据史学家彼得·威尔逊估计，到1648年《威斯特伐利亚和约》结束战事时，神圣罗马帝国约损失五分之一人口，重灾区远不止此数。

summary.en: The Roman Inquisition found Galileo Galilei 'vehemently suspect of heresy' for defending Copernican heliocentrism in his Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems. He was forced to recant and spent his remaining years under house arrest near Florence.
summary.zh: 罗马宗教裁判所认定伽利略因在《关于两大世界体系的对话》中为哥白尼日心说辩护而“有强烈异端嫌疑”。他被迫公开放弃其观点，余生在佛罗伦萨附近遭软禁。

sources.title: Maurice A. Finocchiaro (ed.), The Galileo Affair: A Documentary History (1989)

note: The Wikidata item covers the whole Galileo affair (1610–1633); this record marks the sentence and abjuration at Santa Maria sopra Minerva on 22 June 1633.

summary.en: Treaties signed at Osnabrück and Münster ended the Thirty Years' War in the Holy Roman Empire and the Eighty Years' War between Spain and the Dutch Republic. They recognised Dutch and Swiss independence, extended toleration to Calvinists and strengthened the sovereignty of the German princes.
summary.zh: 在奥斯纳布吕克与明斯特签订的一系列条约，结束了神圣罗马帝国境内的三十年战争以及西班牙与荷兰共和国之间的八十年战争。和约承认荷兰与瑞士独立，将宗教宽容扩展至加尔文派，并增强了德意志诸侯的主权。

note: The Spanish–Dutch Peace of Münster was signed on 30 January 1648; the imperial treaties on 24 October 1648 (Wikidata date).

story.en:
Peace talks began while the armies were still fighting. From 1643 envoys gathered in two Westphalian towns some 50 kilometres apart: France and the Catholic powers negotiated at Münster, Sweden and the Protestant estates at Osnabrück, with couriers riding between them. It was the largest diplomatic gathering Europe had yet seen, and it took five years.

The first settlement came on 30 January 1648, when Spain recognised the independence of the Dutch Republic in the Peace of Münster, ending eighty years of war; Gerard ter Borch painted the envoys swearing to its ratification that May. The treaties with the emperor followed on 24 October. Sweden gained western Pomerania and the bishoprics of Bremen and Verden; France secured Metz, Toul and Verdun and Habsburg rights in Alsace; and the Swiss Confederation was formally released from imperial jurisdiction.

Inside the Empire, Calvinists gained the legal standing of Lutherans and Catholics, church lands were fixed as they had stood in 1624, and the princes' right to make alliances was confirmed, so long as these were not aimed at the emperor. Later writers made Westphalia the founding charter of a system of sovereign states, a reading many historians now think exaggerated. France and Spain fought on until 1659.
story.zh:
战事尚未停歇，和谈便已开始。自1643年起，各国使节汇聚于威斯特伐利亚地区相距约50公里的两座城市：法国与天主教各方在明斯特谈判，瑞典与新教诸邦在奥斯纳布吕克谈判，信使往来奔走于两地之间。这是欧洲此前规模最大的外交聚会，前后耗时五年。

最先达成的是1648年1月30日的《明斯特和约》：西班牙承认荷兰共和国独立，八十年战争就此结束；同年5月使节们宣誓批准和约的场面，被画家赫拉德·特博赫绘成名画。与皇帝的和约则于10月24日签订。瑞典获得西波美拉尼亚以及不来梅、费尔登两个主教区；法国确保了对梅斯、图勒、凡尔登的控制，并取得哈布斯堡家族在阿尔萨斯的权利；瑞士联邦也正式脱离帝国管辖。

在帝国内部，加尔文派获得与路德派、天主教同等的法律地位，教会产业以1624年的状况为准，诸侯的结盟权也得到确认，只要不针对皇帝即可。后世常把威斯特伐利亚和约视为主权国家体系的奠基文件，但许多史学家如今认为这种说法言过其实。法国与西班牙之间的战争则一直打到1659年。

summary.en: A relief army of imperial, German and Polish–Lithuanian troops under King John III Sobieski routed the Ottoman forces of Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha besieging Vienna. The victory began a long Habsburg counter-offensive that recovered Hungary by 1699.
summary.zh: 由神圣罗马帝国、德意志诸邦和波兰—立陶宛军队组成、波兰国王扬三世·索别斯基统率的援军，击溃了围攻维也纳的大维齐尔卡拉·穆斯塔法帕夏的奥斯曼军队。此役开启了哈布斯堡王朝的长期反攻，至1699年收复匈牙利。

sources.title: John Stoye, The Siege of Vienna (1964)

name.zh: 牛顿《自然哲学的数学原理》出版

summary.en: Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica, issued in London under the Royal Society's imprimatur at Edmond Halley's expense, set out the laws of motion and universal gravitation. It unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics and became a foundation of modern physics.
summary.zh: 牛顿的《自然哲学的数学原理》经皇家学会批准在伦敦出版，费用由埃德蒙·哈雷承担。书中提出运动定律和万有引力定律，统一了地面力学与天体力学，成为近代物理学的基石。

sources.title: Richard S. Westfall, Never at Rest: A Biography of Isaac Newton (1980)

note: Wikidata's inception (1680) reflects when Newton began the work. Publication was announced on 5 July 1687 in the Julian calendar then used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent (15 July).

story.en:
In August 1684 the astronomer Edmond Halley visited Cambridge with a question that he, Robert Hooke and Christopher Wren had been unable to settle: what path would a planet follow if the Sun pulled on it with a force that weakened as the square of the distance? Isaac Newton answered at once that it would be an ellipse. He had calculated it, he said, but could not find the paper. A few months later he sent Halley a short tract, De motu corporum in gyrum, and then spent some eighteen months expanding it into three books.

The Royal Society agreed to publish but was short of money, having spent heavily on a lavish history of fishes, so Halley paid the costs himself and corrected the proofs. When Hooke claimed credit for the inverse-square law, Newton threatened to withhold the third book and struck out references to him.

Issued in the summer of 1687 with an imprimatur signed by the Society's president, Samuel Pepys, the Principia showed that one set of laws of motion and one law of gravitation explained falling bodies, the tides, comets and the orbits of the planets. Revised editions followed in 1713 and 1726.
story.zh:
1684年8月，天文学家埃德蒙·哈雷来到剑桥，带来一个他与罗伯特·胡克、克里斯托弗·雷恩都未能解决的问题：如果太阳对行星的引力与距离的平方成反比，行星会沿什么轨道运行？艾萨克·牛顿当即回答是椭圆，并说自己早已算过，只是一时找不到草稿。几个月后，他把一篇短文《论物体在轨道中的运动》寄给哈雷，随后又用约一年半时间把它扩展为三卷巨著。

皇家学会同意出版，却因刚为一部豪华的鱼类志花了大笔钱而囊中羞涩，于是哈雷自掏腰包承担费用，还亲自校对清样。胡克声称反平方定律是他的发现，牛顿大为恼火，一度扬言不出第三卷，并删去了书中提及胡克的地方。

1687年夏，《自然哲学的数学原理》由学会会长塞缪尔·佩皮斯签署出版许可后问世。书中表明，同一套运动定律和同一条引力定律，可以解释落体、潮汐、彗星和行星的轨道。修订版于1713年和1726年相继出版。

summary.en: Peter the Great's Russian army decisively defeated Charles XII of Sweden near Poltava in the Great Northern War. The battle ended Sweden's era as a great power and established Russia as the dominant state of north-eastern Europe.
summary.zh: 大北方战争中，彼得大帝的俄军在波尔塔瓦附近决定性地击败瑞典国王卡尔十二世。此役终结了瑞典的强国时代，确立了俄国在东北欧的主导地位。

sources.title: Peter Englund, The Battle That Shook Europe: Poltava and the Birth of the Russian Empire (2003)

note: Wikidata gives 27 June 1709, the Julian (Old Style) date used in Russia; 8 July is the Gregorian date (28 June in the Swedish calendar).

summary.en: On All Saints' Day a great earthquake, followed by a tsunami and fires, destroyed most of Lisbon and killed tens of thousands. The disaster prompted Pombal's planned rebuilding of the city and fuelled Enlightenment debate about providence, notably in Voltaire's writings.
summary.zh: 万圣节当天，一场大地震及随后的海啸和大火摧毁了里斯本大部分城区，造成数万人死亡。灾后庞巴尔侯爵主持规划重建，这场灾难也引发了以伏尔泰为代表的启蒙思想家关于天意的辩论。

sources.title: Voltaire, Poème sur le désastre de Lisbonne (1756)

note: Wikidata's coordinates (36.0, −11.0) are the estimated offshore epicentre; this record is placed at Lisbon, the city destroyed.

summary.en: Fiscal crisis and Enlightenment ideas led the Estates-General of 1789 to transform itself into a National Assembly; the storming of the Bastille on 14 July became the Revolution's symbol. It abolished feudal privilege and the monarchy, proclaimed the Rights of Man, and ended with Napoleon Bonaparte's coup in 1799.
summary.zh: 财政危机与启蒙思想促使1789年的三级会议转变为国民议会，7月14日攻占巴士底狱成为革命的象征。大革命废除了封建特权和君主制，发表《人权宣言》，最终以1799年拿破仑·波拿巴发动政变告终。

sources.title: Déclaration des droits de l'homme et du citoyen (1789)
William Doyle, The Oxford History of the French Revolution (1989)

note: Coordinates are those of the Bastille (Wikidata Q6539).

story.en:
By 1788 the French crown was effectively bankrupt, and Louis XVI summoned the Estates-General for the first time since 1614. When it met at Versailles in May 1789, the Third Estate, which represented the vast majority of the population, refused to sit apart from the clergy and nobility. On 17 June its deputies declared themselves the National Assembly, and three days later, finding their hall locked, they swore in a nearby tennis court not to disperse until France had a constitution.

The king's dismissal of the popular minister Jacques Necker set Paris alight. On 14 July crowds searching for gunpowder stormed the Bastille, a fortress that held just seven prisoners; its governor, the Marquis de Launay, was killed and his head paraded on a pike. In August the Assembly abolished feudal privileges and adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.

The revolution then radicalised. The royal family's failed flight to Varennes in 1791, war with Austria and Prussia and the fall of the monarchy in 1792 led to Louis's execution in January 1793 and to the Terror. After Robespierre fell in 1794, the Directory governed uneasily until Napoleon Bonaparte seized power on 18 Brumaire (9 November 1799).
story.zh:
到1788年，法国王室实际上已经破产，路易十六不得不召开自1614年以来从未召开过的三级会议。1789年5月会议在凡尔赛开幕，代表绝大多数国民的第三等级拒绝与教士、贵族分开议事。6月17日，第三等级代表宣布成立国民议会；三天后，他们发现会场被锁，便聚集到附近的网球场宣誓：不制定出宪法，决不解散。

国王罢免深得民心的大臣内克尔，点燃了巴黎的怒火。7月14日，寻找火药的民众攻占巴士底狱——这座要塞当时只关着七名囚犯；典狱长德洛奈侯爵被杀，首级被挑在长矛上游街示众。8月，议会废除封建特权，并通过了《人权和公民权宣言》。

此后革命日趋激进。1791年王室出逃至瓦雷讷未遂，随后与奥地利、普鲁士开战，1792年君主制被推翻，路易十六于1793年1月被处决，恐怖统治随之而来。1794年罗伯斯庇尔倒台后，督政府勉强维持统治，直到拿破仑·波拿巴于雾月十八日（1799年11月9日）夺取政权。

summary.en: Napoleon crossed the Niemen with some 450,000 men of the Grande Armée, won a costly victory at Borodino and entered a burning Moscow in September. Without a Russian surrender, the retreat through winter, hunger and Cossack attacks destroyed most of his army.
summary.zh: 拿破仑率领约45万人的大军渡过涅曼河，在博罗季诺付出惨重代价取胜，9月进入陷于大火的莫斯科。俄国拒不求和，大军在严寒、饥饿与哥萨克袭扰中撤退，几乎全军覆没。

label.zh: 小雅罗斯拉韦茨战役，开始撤退

sources.title: Adam Zamoyski, 1812: Napoleon's Fatal March on Moscow (2004)

note: Estimates of the invading force range from about 450,000 to over 600,000 including reinforcements. Event placed at Borodino.

story.en:
After Tsar Alexander I broke with the Continental System, Napoleon's blockade of British trade, the emperor led the largest army Europe had ever seen across the Niemen in June 1812. Perhaps half of it was French; Poles, Germans, Italians and others filled the ranks. The Russian armies under Barclay de Tolly kept falling back, and the Grande Armée lost tens of thousands of men to heat, disease and desertion long before any great battle.

The new Russian commander, Mikhail Kutuzov, finally stood at Borodino on 7 September. In one of the bloodiest days of the era, with perhaps 70,000 or more killed and wounded on both sides, the Russians withdrew but were not destroyed. A week later Napoleon entered a Moscow emptied of most of its people, and fires, widely blamed on the governor, Fyodor Rostopchin, burned much of the city. He waited five weeks for peace terms that never came.

The retreat began on 19 October. Blocked at Maloyaroslavets, the army was forced back along the ravaged road it had come by, through hunger, early frost and Cossack raids. At the Berezina in late November engineers working in icy water built the bridges that let the survivors cross. Napoleon hurried back to Paris, and only a fraction of his army returned.
story.zh:
沙皇亚历山大一世退出拿破仑封锁英国贸易的大陆封锁体系后，1812年6月，拿破仑率领欧洲前所未见的庞大军队渡过涅曼河。其中大约只有一半是法国人，其余是波兰、德意志、意大利等地的士兵。巴克莱·德托利指挥的俄军节节后撤，大军尚未打一场大仗，就已因酷热、疾病和逃亡损失数万人。

新任俄军总司令库图佐夫终于在9月7日于博罗季诺迎战。这是那个时代最血腥的战斗之一，双方伤亡合计可能达七万人以上，俄军撤出战场，却未被歼灭。一周后，拿破仑进入几乎人去城空的莫斯科，随后大火吞噬了城市大半，人们普遍认为是总督罗斯托普钦下令纵火。他在城中等了五个星期，始终没有等来俄国的求和。

10月19日，法军开始撤退。在小雅罗斯拉韦茨受阻后，大军被迫沿来时已被洗劫一空的道路回撤，饥饿、早霜和哥萨克的袭扰接踵而至。11月下旬在别列津纳河，工兵站在冰冷的河水中架起桥梁，残部才得以渡河。拿破仑先行赶回巴黎，他的大军最终只有一小部分生还。

summary.en: Diplomats of the great powers, led by Metternich, Castlereagh, Alexander I and Talleyrand, redrew the map of Europe after Napoleon's defeat. The settlement, signed in June 1815, sought a balance of power and kept general peace among the great powers for decades.
summary.zh: 以梅特涅、卡斯尔雷、亚历山大一世和塔列朗为代表的列强外交官，在拿破仑战败后重新划定欧洲版图。1815年6月签署的最后议定书追求均势，使列强之间维持了数十年的大体和平。

sources.title: Final Act of the Congress of Vienna (9 June 1815)

note: Held September 1814 – June 1815 (Wikidata start/end); Wikidata point in time 1815 refers to the Final Act of 9 June 1815.

story.en:
From September 1814 the Austrian capital played host to emperors, kings, ministers and a crowd of lesser princes, all hoping for a share of the spoils of Napoleon's defeat. The real decisions were taken by a handful of men: Austria's Prince Metternich, Britain's Lord Castlereagh, Tsar Alexander I, Prussia's Hardenberg and, once he had talked his way into the inner circle, Talleyrand for the restored French monarchy. Between sessions came balls, hunts and concerts, prompting the quip, credited to the elderly Prince de Ligne, that the congress danced but made no progress.

The bitterest quarrel was over Poland and Saxony. Russia wanted most of Poland and Prussia all of Saxony, and in January 1815 Austria, Britain and France signed a secret alliance against them. Compromise averted war: Russia gained a Polish kingdom under the tsar, and Prussia took part of Saxony and lands on the Rhine.

Napoleon's escape from Elba in March concentrated minds, and the Final Act was signed on 9 June, nine days before Waterloo. It created a German Confederation, united the Low Countries in one kingdom and guaranteed Swiss neutrality, and the powers also condemned the slave trade. No war involving all the great powers broke out again until 1914, though liberals and nationalists resented a settlement that ignored their hopes.
story.zh:
自1814年9月起，奥地利首都接待了众多皇帝、国王、大臣和大批小邦君主，人人都想从拿破仑的失败中分一杯羹。真正拍板的只有寥寥数人：奥地利的梅特涅亲王、英国的卡斯尔雷子爵、沙皇亚历山大一世、普鲁士的哈登贝格，以及凭口才挤进核心圈子、代表复辟法国王室的塔列朗。会议之余舞会、狩猎和音乐会不断，据说年迈的利涅亲王因此调侃：“会议在跳舞，却毫无进展。”

争执最激烈的是波兰和萨克森问题。俄国想要波兰大部，普鲁士想吞并整个萨克森；1815年1月，奥地利、英国和法国为此秘密结盟加以抵制。最终双方妥协，避免了战争：俄国得到一个由沙皇兼任国王的波兰王国，普鲁士则获得萨克森的一部分和莱茵河沿岸的领土。

1815年3月拿破仑逃离厄尔巴岛，促使各方加快了步伐，最后议定书于6月9日签署，比滑铁卢战役早九天。议定书建立了德意志邦联，把低地国家合并为一个王国，保障瑞士中立，列强还谴责了奴隶贸易。此后直到1914年，欧洲再未发生所有大国都卷入的战争，但自由派和民族主义者对这一无视其诉求的安排深感不满。

summary.en: An Anglo-allied army under the Duke of Wellington and a Prussian army under Blücher defeated Napoleon south of Brussels. The defeat ended his Hundred Days' return to power; he abdicated again and was exiled to Saint Helena.
summary.zh: 威灵顿公爵统率的英国及其盟军与布吕歇尔统率的普鲁士军队在布鲁塞尔以南击败拿破仑。此役终结了他重掌政权的“百日王朝”，拿破仑再度退位并被流放至圣赫勒拿岛。

sources.title: Andrew Roberts, Waterloo: Napoleon's Last Gamble (2005)

story.en:
Back in power after escaping from Elba, Napoleon struck north into Belgium in June 1815, hoping to beat Wellington and Blücher before their armies could join. On 16 June he mauled the Prussians at Ligny, but they withdrew in good order, and Blücher promised to march to Wellington's aid.

On 18 June Wellington's mixed army of British, Dutch, Belgian and German troops held a low ridge at Mont-Saint-Jean, south of the village of Waterloo. Napoleon delayed his attack until late morning to let the rain-soaked ground dry. The farm of Hougoumont on the allied right held out all day against repeated assaults; Marshal Ney's massed cavalry charges broke against squares of infantry; the farmhouse of La Haye Sainte in the centre fell only in the early evening. By then Prussian corps were pushing into Napoleon's right flank at Plancenoit. When the Imperial Guard climbed the slope and was thrown back, the French army dissolved.

According to the diarist Thomas Creevey, Wellington called it the nearest-run thing he had ever seen. Around 50,000 men were killed, wounded or missing in a single day. Napoleon abdicated four days later and died in exile on Saint Helena in 1821.
story.zh:
拿破仑逃离厄尔巴岛重掌政权后，于1815年6月挥师北上进入比利时，企图在威灵顿与布吕歇尔两军会合之前各个击破。6月16日，他在利尼重创普军，但普军有序撤退，布吕歇尔承诺率部驰援威灵顿。

6月18日，威灵顿指挥由英国、荷兰、比利时和德意志部队组成的联军，扼守滑铁卢村以南圣让山的一道低矮山脊。为了让被雨水浸透的地面变干，拿破仑把进攻推迟到上午晚些时候。联军右翼的乌古蒙农庄整日顶住了一轮又一轮猛攻；内伊元帅的大规模骑兵冲锋撞上步兵方阵而纷纷溃退；中央的拉海圣农舍直到傍晚才失守。此时普军各军已从普朗斯努瓦压向拿破仑的右翼。帝国近卫军攀坡进攻被击退后，法军全线崩溃。

据日记作者托马斯·克里维记载，威灵顿称这是他平生所见最险的一仗。一天之内约有五万人阵亡、负伤或失踪。四天后拿破仑再度退位，1821年死于流放地圣赫勒拿岛。

summary.en: A wave of liberal and national uprisings spread from Palermo and Paris to Vienna, Berlin, Budapest and Milan. Most were suppressed by 1849, but serfdom was abolished in the Austrian lands and the revolutions shaped later national movements.
summary.zh: 一股自由主义和民族主义起义浪潮从巴勒莫和巴黎蔓延至维也纳、柏林、布达佩斯和米兰。多数起义到1849年遭到镇压，但奥地利境内废除了农奴制，这场革命也深刻影响了此后的民族运动。

note: The wave began in Palermo on 12 January 1848 (Wikidata start date); placed at Paris, where the February Revolution triggered the wider uprisings.

name.en: Darwin's On the Origin of Species

summary.en: Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species, published in London by John Murray, argued that species evolve over generations through natural selection. The book transformed biology and provoked wide religious and philosophical debate.
summary.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文的《物种起源》由伦敦约翰·默里出版社出版，提出物种通过自然选择代代演化。此书彻底改变了生物学，并引发广泛的宗教与哲学争论。

sources.title: The Complete Work of Charles Darwin Online (ed. John van Wyhe)
Janet Browne, Charles Darwin: The Power of Place (2002)
Britannica: On the Origin of Species

story.en:
Charles Darwin came home in 1836 from five years aboard HMS Beagle with notebooks full of puzzles: giant fossil mammals in South America, and mockingbirds that differed from island to island in the Galápagos. In 1838, reading Thomas Malthus on population, he saw how a struggle for existence could preserve favourable variations. He sketched the theory in 1842 and 1844, then spent years on barnacles, pigeons and correspondence, gathering evidence for a vast book.

In June 1858 a letter arrived from Alfred Russel Wallace, collecting in the Malay Archipelago, that set out almost the same idea. Darwin's friends Charles Lyell and Joseph Hooker arranged for papers by both men to be read at the Linnean Society on 1 July, and Darwin hurried to write what he called an abstract.

John Murray published On the Origin of Species on 24 November 1859, and booksellers took the whole first printing of 1,250 copies. Drawing on animal breeding, geology and geography, it argued that species descend from common ancestors through natural selection. It said almost nothing about humans, but readers drew the conclusion anyway; at Oxford in 1860 Thomas Huxley clashed with Bishop Samuel Wilberforce, in an exchange whose famous wording survives only in later recollections.
story.zh:
1836年，查尔斯·达尔文结束了在“小猎犬号”上五年的航行回到英国，笔记本里满是谜题：南美洲巨大的哺乳动物化石，以及加拉帕戈斯群岛上各岛互不相同的嘲鸫。1838年，他读到马尔萨斯的人口论，领悟到生存斗争可以保留有利的变异。他在1842年和1844年写下理论草稿，此后多年研究藤壶、鸽子，广泛通信，为一部鸿篇巨制积累证据。

1858年6月，正在马来群岛采集标本的阿尔弗雷德·拉塞尔·华莱士寄来一封信，阐述的观点几乎与他如出一辙。达尔文的朋友查尔斯·莱尔和约瑟夫·胡克安排两人的论文于7月1日在林奈学会同时宣读，达尔文随即赶写他所谓的“摘要”。

1859年11月24日，约翰·默里出版社出版《物种起源》，首印1250册全部被书商订购一空。书中借助家养动物的育种、地质学和生物地理学，论证物种通过自然选择由共同祖先演化而来。书中几乎只字未提人类，但读者还是自行得出了结论。1860年在牛津，托马斯·赫胥黎与塞缪尔·威尔伯福斯主教展开交锋，而那段著名对话的措辞只见于后人的回忆。

summary.en: Led by Piedmont-Sardinia's prime minister Cavour and the volunteer campaigns of Giuseppe Garibaldi, most Italian states were united and the Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in Turin in 1861 under Victor Emmanuel II. Venetia joined in 1866, and Rome, taken in 1870, became the capital in 1871.
summary.zh: 在撒丁王国首相加富尔的主导和朱塞佩·加里波第志愿军的征战下，意大利大部分邦国得以统一，1861年在都灵宣告成立以维克托·伊曼纽尔二世为国王的意大利王国。威尼托于1866年并入，1870年攻占的罗马于1871年成为首都。

sources.title: Lucy Riall, Risorgimento: The History of Italy from Napoleon to Nation State (2009)

note: Wikidata dates the Risorgimento 1815–1871; this record runs from the proclamation of the kingdom in Turin (17 March 1861) to Rome becoming capital (1871).

story.en:
Before 1859 Italy was, as Metternich had put it, a geographical expression: Austria ruled Lombardy and Venetia, the pope governed central Italy, and a Bourbon king reigned in Naples. Count Camillo di Cavour, prime minister of Piedmont-Sardinia from 1852, set out to enlarge his kingdom by diplomacy. At Plombières in 1858 he secretly won the support of Napoleon III, and in 1859 French and Piedmontese armies defeated Austria at Magenta and Solferino. Piedmont gained Lombardy, the central duchies voted to join, and Nice and Savoy went to France as the price.

Then Giuseppe Garibaldi, a veteran revolutionary, sailed from near Genoa in May 1860 with about a thousand red-shirted volunteers. They landed at Marsala in Sicily, took Palermo and crossed to the mainland, and by September Garibaldi was in Naples. Fearing he would march on Rome, Cavour sent Piedmontese troops through the Papal States, and at Teano in October Garibaldi handed his conquests to Victor Emmanuel II.

The Kingdom of Italy was proclaimed in March 1861, and Cavour died that June. Venetia came in 1866 after Austria's defeat by Prussia. Once the French garrison had left, Italian troops entered Rome through a breach near Porta Pia on 20 September 1870, and the city became the capital in 1871.
story.zh:
1859年以前，意大利正如梅特涅所说，只是一个“地理名词”：奥地利统治伦巴第和威尼托，教宗管辖意大利中部，那不勒斯则由波旁王朝的国王统治。1852年出任撒丁王国首相的卡米洛·加富尔伯爵决心以外交手段扩张王国。1858年他在普隆比耶尔秘密争取到拿破仑三世的支持，1859年法国与撒丁联军在马真塔和索尔费里诺击败奥地利。撒丁王国得到伦巴第，中部各公国经公民投票加入，作为代价，尼斯和萨伏依割让给法国。

接着，老革命家朱塞佩·加里波第于1860年5月率约一千名红衫志愿军从热那亚附近出海。他们在西西里的马尔萨拉登陆，攻占巴勒莫，再渡海进入半岛，9月加里波第已进入那不勒斯。加富尔担心他进军罗马，便派撒丁军队穿过教宗国南下；10月在泰阿诺，加里波第把征服的土地交给了维克托·伊曼纽尔二世。

1861年3月意大利王国宣告成立，同年6月加富尔去世。1866年奥地利败于普鲁士后，威尼托并入意大利。法国驻军撤离后，意大利军队于1870年9月20日从皮亚门附近的城墙缺口攻入罗马，次年罗马成为首都。

summary.en: After Prussian victories over Denmark, Austria and France engineered by Otto von Bismarck, King Wilhelm I of Prussia was proclaimed German Emperor in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles. The new German Empire became continental Europe's leading industrial and military power.
summary.zh: 在俾斯麦主导下，普鲁士先后战胜丹麦、奥地利和法国，随后普鲁士国王威廉一世在凡尔赛宫镜厅被宣布为德意志皇帝。新成立的德意志帝国成为欧洲大陆首屈一指的工业与军事强国。

sources.title: Christopher Clark, Iron Kingdom: The Rise and Downfall of Prussia, 1600–1947 (2006)

note: QID is the unification process (1866–1871), whose point in time in Wikidata is the proclamation of 18 January 1871.

story.en:
Otto von Bismarck became Prussia's minister-president in 1862 in the middle of a budget fight with liberal deputies, telling them that the great questions of the day would be settled not by speeches and majority votes but by iron and blood. Over the next eight years he used three short wars to settle them. In 1864 Prussia and Austria together took Schleswig and Holstein from Denmark. In 1866 Prussia turned on Austria, beat it at Königgrätz in a war of seven weeks and formed the North German Confederation without it.

The last obstacle was France, which feared a united Germany on its border. In July 1870 Bismarck edited a telegram from Bad Ems about King Wilhelm's meeting with the French ambassador so that it read as a snub, and France declared war. The south German states sided with Prussia, and at Sedan on 2 September the German armies captured Napoleon III himself.

With Paris still under siege, the German princes gathered in the Hall of Mirrors at Versailles on 18 January 1871 to proclaim Wilhelm German Emperor. Wilhelm, unhappy with the title and with seeing Prussia merged into Germany, reportedly ignored Bismarck at the ceremony. The new empire annexed Alsace and part of Lorraine, a loss France never accepted.
story.zh:
1862年，奥托·冯·俾斯麦在与自由派议员的预算之争中出任普鲁士首相，他对议员们说，当代的重大问题不是靠演说和多数决议，而是要用铁和血来解决。此后八年间，他以三场短促的战争实现了这一目标。1864年，普鲁士与奥地利联手从丹麦手中夺取石勒苏益格和荷尔斯泰因；1866年，普鲁士转而对奥地利开战，在为期七周的战争中于克尼格雷茨击败奥军，随后撇开奥地利组建了北德意志邦联。

最后的障碍是法国，它担心边境出现一个统一的德国。1870年7月，俾斯麦删改了一份从埃姆斯发来、报告威廉国王会见法国大使经过的电报，使之读来像是对法国的羞辱，法国随即宣战。南德各邦站到普鲁士一边，9月2日在色当，德军连拿破仑三世本人也俘虏了。

巴黎仍在围困之中，1871年1月18日，德意志诸侯齐聚凡尔赛宫镜厅，拥立威廉为德意志皇帝。威廉不满这一称号，也不愿看到普鲁士融入德国，据说在典礼上故意冷落了俾斯麦。新帝国吞并了阿尔萨斯和洛林的一部分，法国对此始终耿耿于怀。

summary.en: Triggered by the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo, war between the Central Powers and the Allies brought trench deadlock in the west and vast campaigns in the east. About 9–10 million soldiers died, and the German, Austro-Hungarian, Russian and Ottoman empires collapsed.
summary.zh: 奥匈帝国皇储弗朗茨·斐迪南大公在萨拉热窝遇刺，引发同盟国与协约国之间的大战，西线陷入堑壕僵持，东线则展开大规模运动战。约九百万至一千万军人阵亡，德意志、奥匈、俄罗斯和奥斯曼四大帝国相继崩溃。

sources.title: Hew Strachan, The First World War (2003)
