note: Placed at Verdun on the Western Front (Wikidata has no coordinates). Wikidata point in time (11 Nov 1918) is the Armistice; start and end dates match.

story.en:
On 28 June 1914 Gavrilo Princip, a young Bosnian Serb nationalist, shot Archduke Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne, in Sarajevo. Assured of German backing, Austria-Hungary declared war on Serbia on 28 July. Within a week the alliance system had pulled in Russia, Germany and France, and Germany's march through neutral Belgium brought Britain in on 4 August.

The German plan to knock France out quickly failed at the Marne in September, and by the end of 1914 trenches ran from the Channel coast to the Swiss border. Machine guns, barbed wire and artillery made every attack ruinously costly: at Verdun in 1916 the French and Germans fought for ten months, and on the first day of the Somme that July the British army suffered some 57,000 casualties. In the east the fronts moved more, but Russia's losses helped bring revolution in 1917 and a separate peace in March 1918.

The entry of the United States in April 1917 tipped the balance. After its last offensives failed, Germany signed an armistice in a railway carriage near Compiègne that took effect at 11 a.m. on 11 November 1918. The Kaiser had abdicated two days earlier, Austria-Hungary and the Russian Empire had already broken apart, and the Ottoman Empire was dismantled soon after.
story.zh:
1914年6月28日，年轻的波斯尼亚塞族民族主义者加夫里洛·普林西普在萨拉热窝刺杀了奥匈帝国皇储弗朗茨·斐迪南大公。在德国承诺支持之下，奥匈帝国于7月28日对塞尔维亚宣战。不到一周，同盟体系便把俄国、德国和法国卷入战争；德军借道中立的比利时，又使英国在8月4日参战。

德国速战击溃法国的计划在9月的马恩河战役中破产，到1914年底，堑壕已从英吉利海峡沿岸一直延伸到瑞士边境。机枪、铁丝网和大炮使每一次进攻都代价惨重：1916年，法德两军在凡尔登鏖战十个月；同年7月索姆河战役首日，英军伤亡约五万七千人。东线的战线变动较大，但巨大的损失促使俄国在1917年爆发革命，并于1918年3月单独媾和。

1917年4月美国参战，扭转了力量对比。德国最后的攻势失败后，在贡比涅附近的一节火车车厢里签订停战协定，于1918年11月11日上午11时生效。两天前德皇已经退位，奥匈帝国和俄罗斯帝国此时早已瓦解，奥斯曼帝国也在不久之后被肢解。

summary.en: The Bolsheviks under Vladimir Lenin overthrew Russia's Provisional Government in Petrograd, seizing the Winter Palace. Their seizure of power led to civil war and to the founding of the Soviet Union in 1922.
summary.zh: 列宁领导的布尔什维克在彼得格勒推翻俄国临时政府，攻占冬宫。这次夺权引发了内战，并导致1922年苏联的建立。

sources.title: John Reed, Ten Days That Shook the World (1919)
Orlando Figes, A People's Tragedy: The Russian Revolution 1891–1924 (1996)

note: Wikidata gives 25 October 1917, the Julian date then used in Russia; 7 November is the Gregorian equivalent. Coordinates: Winter Palace. No polity link: the Russian Empire ended in March 1917 and the Soviet Union was founded in 1922; the government overthrown was the Provisional Government of the Russian Republic, which has no polity record.

summary.en: Signed in the Hall of Mirrors five years to the day after the Sarajevo assassination, the treaty ended the war between Germany and the Allies. Germany lost territory and colonies and accepted limits on its armed forces and liability for reparations; the treaty also created the League of Nations.
summary.zh: 和约在萨拉热窝事件整整五年后于凡尔赛宫镜厅签署，结束了德国与协约国之间的战争。德国丧失领土和殖民地，接受军备限制并承担赔款责任；和约还创建了国际联盟。

sources.title: Margaret MacMillan, Peacemakers: The Paris Conference of 1919 and Its Attempt to End War (2001)

note: Signed 28 June 1919; Wikidata's start date (10 January 1920) is its entry into force.

story.en:
The Paris Peace Conference opened on 18 January 1919, the anniversary of the German Empire's proclamation, and was dominated by the Big Four: Woodrow Wilson of the United States, David Lloyd George of Britain, Georges Clemenceau of France and Vittorio Orlando of Italy. Wilson wanted a peace built on his Fourteen Points and a League of Nations; Clemenceau wanted security against a neighbour that had invaded France twice in half a century. Germany was not invited to negotiate. Its delegation received the terms in May and was allowed only written objections.

The treaty returned Alsace-Lorraine to France, gave territory to a revived Poland, put the Saar under the League and demilitarised the Rhineland. Germany's army was capped at 100,000 men with no air force, its colonies were taken, and Article 231 made it accept responsibility for the war's damage as the basis for reparations, fixed in 1921 at 132 billion gold marks. A week before the signing, German crews scuttled their interned fleet at Scapa Flow.

Two German ministers signed on 28 June in the Hall of Mirrors. Germans denounced a dictated peace, and John Maynard Keynes attacked its economics. The US Senate refused to ratify the treaty, and the United States never joined the League.
story.zh:
巴黎和会于1919年1月18日——德意志帝国宣告成立的纪念日——开幕，由“四巨头”主导：美国的伍德罗·威尔逊、英国的劳合·乔治、法国的克列孟梭和意大利的奥兰多。威尔逊希望以他的“十四点”和国际联盟为基础缔造和平；克列孟梭则要防范一个半个世纪内两度入侵法国的邻国。德国未获邀参加谈判，其代表团5月才收到条款，只被允许提出书面异议。

和约把阿尔萨斯-洛林归还法国，将部分领土划给复国的波兰，萨尔交由国际联盟管理，莱茵兰实行非军事化。德国陆军被限制在十万人以内，不得拥有空军，殖民地全部被剥夺；第231条要求德国承认对战争造成的损失负有责任，以此作为赔款的依据，赔款总额于1921年定为1320亿金马克。签约前一周，被扣押在斯卡帕湾的德国舰队由本国水兵自行凿沉。

6月28日，两名德国部长在凡尔赛宫镜厅签字。德国人斥之为“强加的和平”，凯恩斯则抨击其经济条款。美国参议院拒绝批准和约，美国始终没有加入国际联盟。

name.zh: 第二次世界大战（欧洲战场）

summary.en: Germany's invasion of Poland on 1 September 1939 began a war that by 1941 pitted the Axis against Britain, the Soviet Union and the United States. In Europe it ended with Germany's unconditional surrender in May 1945, after tens of millions of deaths, including some six million Jews murdered in the Holocaust.
summary.zh: 1939年9月1日德国入侵波兰，战争爆发；至1941年，轴心国已与英国、苏联和美国全面交战。欧洲战事以1945年5月德国无条件投降告终，战争造成数千万人死亡，其中包括在大屠杀中遇害的约六百万犹太人。

label.zh: 韦斯特普拉特：入侵波兰

label.en: Battle of Britain and the Blitz
label.zh: 不列颠之战与伦敦大轰炸

sources.title: Gerhard L. Weinberg, A World at Arms: A Global History of World War II (1994)

note: Wikidata's end date (2 September 1945) is the global end with Japan's surrender; the war in Europe ended on 8 May 1945.

story.en:
A week after Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed a non-aggression pact with a secret protocol dividing eastern Europe, the German battleship Schleswig-Holstein opened fire on the Polish depot at Westerplatte, outside Danzig, early on 1 September 1939. Britain and France declared war two days later but could not save Poland, which the Soviets invaded from the east on 17 September.

In 1940 Germany overran Denmark, Norway, the Low Countries and France. Some 338,000 Allied soldiers escaped from Dunkirk, and Britain, now led by Winston Churchill, survived the Battle of Britain and the Blitz. On 22 June 1941 Hitler invaded the Soviet Union, and after Pearl Harbor he declared war on the United States. Behind the eastern front, mass shootings and then death camps such as Auschwitz-Birkenau carried out the murder of Europe's Jews.

The surrender of the German Sixth Army at Stalingrad in February 1943 marked the turning point. The Allies invaded Italy in 1943 and Normandy in 1944 while the Red Army drove west. Hitler killed himself in Berlin on 30 April 1945, and Germany's unconditional surrender, signed at Reims and again in Berlin, took effect on 8 May. The Soviet Union alone lost some 27 million people.
story.zh:
纳粹德国与苏联签订附有瓜分东欧秘密议定书的互不侵犯条约一周后，1939年9月1日凌晨，德国战列舰“石勒苏益格-荷尔斯泰因号”向但泽城外的波兰军需站韦斯特普拉特开火。两天后英法对德宣战，却未能挽救波兰；9月17日，苏联又从东面入侵波兰。

1940年，德国相继攻占丹麦、挪威、低地国家和法国。约33.8万盟军士兵从敦刻尔克撤出，由丘吉尔领导的英国挺过了不列颠之战和伦敦大轰炸。1941年6月22日，希特勒入侵苏联；珍珠港事件后，他又对美国宣战。在东线后方，先是大规模枪杀，继而是奥斯维辛-比克瑙等灭绝营，欧洲犹太人遭到系统屠杀。

1943年2月德国第六集团军在斯大林格勒投降，成为战争的转折点。盟军于1943年进攻意大利、1944年登陆诺曼底，红军则一路西进。1945年4月30日希特勒在柏林自杀，德国先后在兰斯和柏林签署无条件投降书，于5月8日生效。仅苏联一国就损失了约2700万人。

summary.en: Germany and its allies invaded the Soviet Union on 22 June 1941 in Operation Barbarossa, opening the largest land war in history. After defeats at Moscow, Stalingrad and Kursk, the Red Army drove west and took Berlin in May 1945; Soviet deaths reached roughly 27 million.
summary.zh: 1941年6月22日，德国及其盟国发动“巴巴罗萨行动”入侵苏联，开启了史上规模最大的陆地战争。德军在莫斯科、斯大林格勒和库尔斯克相继失利后，红军一路西进，于1945年5月攻克柏林；苏联死亡人数约达2700万。

label.zh: 巴格拉季昂行动（明斯克）
维斯瓦河—奥得河攻势（华沙）

sources.title: David M. Glantz and Jonathan M. House, When Titans Clashed: How the Red Army Stopped Hitler (1995)

note: Soviet death estimates vary (c. 24–27 million, military and civilian).

summary.en: German and Axis forces fought to take Stalingrad on the Volga in months of street fighting. A Soviet counter-offensive in November 1942 encircled the German Sixth Army, which surrendered in February 1943—a turning point of the war in Europe.
summary.zh: 德国及轴心国军队为夺取伏尔加河畔的斯大林格勒，展开了长达数月的巷战。1942年11月苏军发动反攻，包围德军第六集团军，后者于1943年2月投降，此役成为欧洲战场的转折点。

summary.en: On D-Day, American, British, Canadian and other Allied forces landed on five beaches in Normandy in the largest seaborne invasion in history. The landings opened a western front that, together with the Soviet advance in the east, led to Germany's defeat.
summary.zh: D日当天，美、英、加等盟军在诺曼底五处海滩登陆，这是史上规模最大的海上登陆作战。登陆开辟了西线战场，与东线苏军的推进一道导致德国战败。

sources.title: Antony Beevor, D-Day: The Battle for Normandy (2009)

story.en:
Operation Overlord had been in preparation for more than a year when General Dwight Eisenhower, the Allied supreme commander, faced his hardest decision. The invasion was set for 5 June 1944, but a storm forced a postponement. On the evening of the 4th his chief meteorologist, Group Captain James Stagg, forecast a brief break in the weather, and Eisenhower ordered the assault for the 6th. He also scribbled a note, to be released if the landings failed, taking the blame on himself.

Overnight, airborne divisions dropped behind the coast, and at dawn a fleet of some 7,000 vessels carried troops to five beaches: Utah and Omaha for the Americans, Gold and Sword for the British, Juno for the Canadians. At Omaha, high bluffs and intact defences pinned the first waves on the sand, and losses were heaviest there; elsewhere troops pushed inland faster. About 156,000 men landed by sea and air that day.

An elaborate deception, Operation Fortitude, had persuaded the Germans that the main blow would fall near Calais, and Field Marshal Rommel was at home in Germany for his wife's birthday. Even so, the battle for Normandy lasted until August, when the Allies broke out and Paris was liberated.
story.zh:
“霸王行动”已筹备了一年多，盟军最高统帅德怀特·艾森豪威尔将军此刻面临最艰难的抉择。登陆原定于1944年6月5日，却因风暴被迫推迟。6月4日晚，首席气象官詹姆斯·斯塔格上校预报天气将短暂好转，艾森豪威尔遂下令于6日发起进攻。他还匆匆写下一张便条，准备在登陆失败时发表，表示由自己承担全部责任。

夜间，空降师在海岸后方伞降；黎明时分，约七千艘舰船载着部队驶向五处海滩：美军登陆犹他和奥马哈，英军登陆黄金和宝剑，加拿大军登陆朱诺。在奥马哈海滩，高耸的峭壁和完好无损的防御工事把第一波部队压制在沙滩上，伤亡最为惨重；其他海滩的部队则较快向内陆推进。当天经海空两路登陆的盟军约有15.6万人。

精心策划的“坚韧行动”使德军相信主攻方向将在加来附近，隆美尔元帅当时也正回德国为妻子庆祝生日。即便如此，诺曼底战役仍一直持续到8月，盟军这才实现突破，并解放了巴黎。

summary.en: Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and West Germany signed treaties in Rome creating the European Economic Community and Euratom. The EEC's common market became the core of what later developed into the European Union.
summary.zh: 比利时、法国、意大利、卢森堡、荷兰和联邦德国在罗马签署条约，建立欧洲经济共同体和欧洲原子能共同体。欧共体的共同市场成为日后欧洲联盟的核心。

sources.title: EUR-Lex: Treaty establishing the European Economic Community (1957)

note: Signed on the Capitoline Hill (Palazzo dei Conservatori).

summary.en: A flawed safety test caused reactor No. 4 of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in Soviet Ukraine to explode, spreading radioactive contamination across much of Europe. Some 116,000 people were evacuated in 1986, and a 30-km exclusion zone remains.
summary.zh: 一次存在缺陷的安全测试导致苏联乌克兰切尔诺贝利核电站4号反应堆爆炸，放射性污染扩散至欧洲大部分地区。1986年约11.6万人被疏散，30公里隔离区至今仍在。

sources.title: International Atomic Energy Agency, INSAG-7: The Chernobyl Accident: Updating of INSAG-1 (1992)

summary.en: Amid mass protests and an exodus of East Germans, the GDR's announcement of eased travel rules led crowds to force open the Berlin Wall's checkpoints on the night of 9 November. The event symbolised the end of the Cold War division of Europe and led to German reunification in October 1990.
summary.zh: 在大规模抗议和东德民众出逃潮中，民主德国宣布放宽出行限制，11月9日夜民众涌向柏林墙并迫使检查站开放。这一事件象征着冷战时期欧洲分裂的终结，并促成1990年10月的两德统一。

sources.title: Mary Elise Sarotte, The Collapse: The Accidental Opening of the Berlin Wall (2014)

story.en:
For 28 years the Wall had divided Berlin, and at least 140 people died there, most of them shot or killed while trying to flee the East. In 1989 the pressure on the East German regime became overwhelming. Hungary opened its border with Austria in September and tens of thousands of East Germans poured west, while in Leipzig the Monday demonstrations swelled from thousands to hundreds of thousands. Erich Honecker was forced out in October, but his successors could not stem the tide.

On the evening of 9 November the Politburo member Günter Schabowski read out new travel rules at a televised press conference. He had not been properly briefed, and when a journalist asked when they took effect, he shuffled through his papers and said that, as far as he knew, it was immediately. West German television spread the news, and thousands of East Berliners hurried to the crossings. At Bornholmer Strasse the overwhelmed officer in charge, Harald Jäger, opened the gate shortly before midnight rather than risk bloodshed. Within hours people were dancing on the Wall at the Brandenburg Gate.

As Mary Elise Sarotte has shown, nobody had planned the opening. Less than a year later, on 3 October 1990, Germany was reunified.
story.zh:
柏林墙把柏林分隔了28年，至少有140人在墙边丧生，其中大多数是在试图逃离东柏林时被射杀或遇难的。1989年，民主德国政权承受的压力已到极限。9月匈牙利开放与奥地利的边界，数以万计的东德人涌向西方；在莱比锡，每周一的示威游行从数千人发展到数十万人。昂纳克在10月被迫下台，但继任者已无力回天。

11月9日晚，政治局委员君特·沙博夫斯基在电视直播的记者会上宣读新的出行规定。他事先并未充分了解情况，当记者追问规定何时生效时，他翻了翻文件，说据他所知是“立即”。西德电视台播出了这一消息，成千上万的东柏林人随即涌向各个过境点。在博恩霍尔默大街检查站，不堪重负的值班军官哈拉尔德·耶格尔为避免流血，在午夜前打开了闸门。几个小时后，人们已在勃兰登堡门前的墙头上欢舞。

正如历史学家玛丽·伊丽丝·萨罗特所揭示的，这次开放并无任何人事先策划。不到一年后，1990年10月3日，两德实现统一。

summary.en: After the failed August coup and independence declarations by the republics, the leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus agreed in December to replace the USSR with the Commonwealth of Independent States. Gorbachev resigned on 25 December and the Soviet Union formally ceased to exist the next day.
summary.zh: 八月政变失败、各加盟共和国纷纷宣布独立后，俄罗斯、乌克兰和白俄罗斯领导人于12月商定以独立国家联合体取代苏联。戈尔巴乔夫于12月25日辞职，苏联于次日正式解体。

sources.title: Serhii Plokhy, The Last Empire: The Final Days of the Soviet Union (2014)
Britannica: Collapse of the Soviet Union

note: Wikidata's coordinates (65, 90) are a centroid of the USSR; this record is placed at the Moscow Kremlin.

name.zh: 本笃创建卡西诺山修道院

summary.en: Benedict of Nursia established a monastery on the hilltop above Cassino, where he wrote the Rule that set out a balanced life of prayer, work and study. The Benedictine Rule became the basis of Western monasticism, and houses that followed it preserved learning through the early Middle Ages.
summary.zh: 努西亚的本笃在卡西诺镇上方的山顶建立修道院，并在此撰写会规，确立祈祷、劳动与研读相平衡的生活。《本笃会规》成为西方修道制度的基础，遵行它的修道院在中世纪早期保存了学术文化。

sources.title: Gregory the Great, Dialogues, Book II

note: 529 is traditional; Gregory the Great's Dialogues give no year.

story.en:
Almost everything known about Benedict comes from the second book of Gregory the Great's Dialogues, written around 593. Born at Nursia, he abandoned his studies in Rome to live as a hermit at Subiaco, where disciples gathered around him. Around 529, by tradition, he moved south to the hilltop above Cassino, smashed an ancient temple of Apollo there and built oratories to St Martin and St John the Baptist.

Gregory tells how Benedict's sister Scholastica, also a nun, begged him at their yearly meeting to stay and talk through the night; when he refused, she prayed and a violent storm broke, keeping him there. She died three days later. At Monte Cassino Benedict wrote his Rule, 73 short chapters on how a community should pray, work, eat and obey an abbot, admired for its moderation. He died around 547.

The abbey was sacked by the Lombards and later by Arab raiders, wrecked by an earthquake in 1349 and flattened by Allied bombing in February 1944, and each time it was rebuilt. Charlemagne promoted Benedict's Rule across his empire, and in 1964, at the reconsecration of the rebuilt abbey, Pope Paul VI named Benedict patron saint of Europe.
story.zh:
关于本笃的生平，几乎全部出自教宗格列高利一世约593年写成的《对话录》第二卷。本笃生于努西亚，曾在罗马求学，后弃学到苏比亚科隐修，门徒渐渐聚集在他身边。按传统说法，约529年他南迁至卡西诺上方的山顶，捣毁那里的一座古代阿波罗神庙，改建供奉圣马丁和施洗者圣约翰的小礼拜堂。

格列高利讲述了一个故事：本笃的妹妹思嘉（斯科拉斯蒂卡）也是修女，在兄妹一年一度的会面中恳求他留下彻夜长谈；本笃不肯，她便祈祷，顿时狂风暴雨大作，使他无法离开。三天后她便去世了。本笃在卡西诺山写下会规，共七十三章，规定修道团体如何祈祷、劳动、饮食和服从院长，以中庸平和著称。他约于547年去世。

修道院先后遭伦巴第人和阿拉伯袭击者洗劫，1349年又毁于地震，1944年2月更被盟军轰炸夷为平地，但每次都得以重建。查理曼在全国推行《本笃会规》；1964年重建后的修道院重新祝圣时，教宗保禄六世宣布本笃为欧洲主保圣人。

summary.en: From Columbus's second voyage of 1493, ships between Spain and the Americas carried horses, cattle, wheat and sugar cane west, and maize, potatoes, tomatoes, cacao and tobacco east, along with devastating Old World diseases. American crops spread across Europe, Africa and Asia, feeding population growth from Ireland to China.
summary.zh: 自1493年哥伦布第二次航行起，往来于西班牙与美洲之间的船只把马、牛、小麦和甘蔗运往美洲，把玉米、马铃薯、番茄、可可和烟草带回欧洲，同时也带去了毁灭性的旧大陆疾病。美洲作物传遍欧洲、非洲和亚洲，推动了从爱尔兰到中国的人口增长。

sources.title: N. Nunn & N. Qian, "The Columbian Exchange: A History of Disease, Food, and Ideas", Journal of Economic Perspectives 24 (2010)
Alfred W. Crosby, The Columbian Exchange: Biological and Cultural Consequences of 1492 (1972)

note: Marker at Seville, whose Casa de Contratación (1503) controlled the Indies trade; the end year is conventional, as the exchange continued.

story.en:
The historian Alfred Crosby coined the phrase in 1972 for the two-way traffic in plants, animals and microbes that followed 1492. Columbus's second voyage of 1493, seventeen ships carrying some 1,200 settlers, brought horses, cattle, pigs, wheat and sugar cane to Hispaniola. Within a century there were horses on the Great Plains and the pampas, and sugar plantations worked by enslaved Africans spread across the Caribbean and Brazil.

The cost in the Americas was catastrophic. Peoples who had never met smallpox, measles or influenza had no immunity: smallpox reached Hispaniola by 1518 and swept through Tenochtitlan in 1520, during the Spanish conquest of the Aztec capital. Over the following century epidemics, war and forced labour cut the indigenous population of the Americas by most estimates by more than half, and in many places by far more.

In the other direction came maize, potatoes, tomatoes, chili peppers, cacao, tobacco and cassava. These crops changed diets worldwide: potatoes became the staple of northern Europe and Ireland, maize and cassava fed much of Africa, chillies transformed the cooking of India and Sichuan, and maize and sweet potatoes, grown on hillsides unsuited to rice, helped China's population grow in the 18th century.
story.zh:
历史学家艾尔弗雷德·克罗斯比于1972年创造了这个术语，用来指1492年之后植物、动物和微生物在新旧大陆之间的双向流动。1493年哥伦布第二次航行，十七艘船载着约一千二百名移民，把马、牛、猪、小麦和甘蔗带到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛。不到一个世纪，北美大平原和南美潘帕斯草原上已有马群奔驰，由非洲奴隶劳作的甘蔗种植园遍布加勒比和巴西。

美洲为此付出了灾难性的代价。从未接触过天花、麻疹和流感的民族毫无免疫力：天花于1518年传到伊斯帕尼奥拉岛，1520年西班牙人征服阿兹特克首都特诺奇蒂特兰期间，又在城中肆虐。此后一个世纪里，瘟疫、战争和强迫劳动使美洲原住民人口锐减，多数估计认为减少了一半以上，许多地方远不止于此。

反方向传来的有玉米、马铃薯、番茄、辣椒、可可、烟草和木薯。这些作物改变了全世界的饮食：马铃薯成为北欧和爱尔兰的主食，玉米和木薯养活了非洲的大量人口，辣椒改变了印度和四川的烹饪，而能在不宜种稻的山坡上生长的玉米和番薯，则助推了18世纪中国的人口增长。

name.zh: 麦哲伦—埃尔卡诺环球航行

summary.en: Five ships under Ferdinand Magellan left Sanlúcar de Barrameda to reach the Spice Islands by sailing west. Magellan was killed at Mactan in 1521; Juan Sebastián Elcano brought the Victoria home with 18 men in September 1522, completing the first circumnavigation of the Earth.
summary.zh: 麦哲伦率五艘船从桑卢卡尔-德巴拉梅达出发，向西航行寻找香料群岛。麦哲伦于1521年在麦克坦岛被杀；1522年9月，埃尔卡诺率“维多利亚”号及18名船员返航，完成人类首次环球航行。

sources.title: Antonio Pigafetta, Relazione del primo viaggio intorno al mondo (c. 1524)

note: Julian dates: the fleet left Seville on 10 August and Sanlúcar on 20 September 1519; Victoria reached Sanlúcar on 6 September 1522 and Seville on 8 September (Wikidata's dates).

story.en:
Ferdinand Magellan, a Portuguese captain who had fought in the Indian Ocean, persuaded the young Charles I of Spain that the Spice Islands could be reached by sailing west and might lie in Spain's half of the world. Five ships with about 240 to 270 men sailed in September 1519. At Port San Julián in Patagonia Magellan crushed a mutiny, executing one captain and marooning another; one ship was wrecked, and another deserted and sailed home from the strait that now bears his name, which the fleet threaded between October and November 1520.

The Pacific was far wider than anyone had imagined. Antonio Pigafetta, the Venetian chronicler aboard, says men ate ox hides softened in seawater, sawdust and rats, and many died of scurvy before they reached Guam in March 1521. In the Philippines, Magellan made allies at Cebu and was killed on 27 April fighting the chief Lapulapu on Mactan.

Two ships reached the Moluccas and loaded cloves. Juan Sebastián Elcano took the Victoria across the Indian Ocean and round Africa, avoiding Portuguese ports. At the Cape Verde Islands the crew found their log was a day behind, the first lost day of a circumnavigation. Eighteen men returned to Spain in September 1522.
story.zh:
麦哲伦是曾在印度洋作战的葡萄牙船长，他说服年轻的西班牙国王卡洛斯一世：向西航行可以到达香料群岛，而且那里可能位于西班牙所属的半个世界之内。1519年9月，五艘船载着约二百四十至二百七十人出航。在巴塔哥尼亚的圣胡利安港，麦哲伦镇压了一次哗变，处死一名船长，把另一名放逐荒岸；随后一艘船触礁沉没，另一艘在今天以他命名的海峡中擅自返航。1520年10月至11月，船队穿过了这条海峡。

太平洋比任何人想象的都要宽广。随船记事的威尼斯人安东尼奥·皮加费塔写道，船员们吃用海水泡软的牛皮、木屑和老鼠，许多人在1521年3月抵达关岛之前便死于坏血病。在菲律宾，麦哲伦在宿务结交了盟友，4月27日在麦克坦岛与酋长拉普拉普作战时被杀。

两艘船抵达摩鹿加群岛，装满了丁香。埃尔卡诺驾驶“维多利亚”号横渡印度洋，绕过非洲，一路避开葡萄牙港口。在佛得角群岛，船员发现航海日志比当地日期慢了一天，这是环球航行“丢失一天”的首次记录。1522年9月，十八人回到西班牙。

summary.en: Starting in a bakery on Pudding Lane, a fire fanned by an east wind burned for four days and destroyed about 13,200 houses, 87 parish churches and old St Paul's Cathedral in the City of London. The City was rebuilt in brick and stone, with Christopher Wren's new St Paul's and City churches.
summary.zh: 大火起于布丁巷的一家面包坊，在东风助长下燃烧四天，伦敦城内约13200所房屋、87座教区教堂和旧圣保罗大教堂被毁。此后城区以砖石重建，克里斯托弗·雷恩设计了新的圣保罗大教堂和城中诸教堂。

sources.title: The Diary of Samuel Pepys, 2 September 1666

note: Began on 2 September 1666 in the Julian (Old Style) calendar then used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent.

summary.en: Beginning in Britain, coal-fired steam power, mechanised cotton spinning and new iron-making methods moved production from homes and workshops into factories. Manchester became the first industrial city, and the transformation spread to Europe and beyond, reshaping work, cities, trade and the global balance of power.
summary.zh: 工业革命始于英国，以煤为燃料的蒸汽动力、机械化棉纺和新的炼铁方法使生产从家庭和作坊转入工厂。曼彻斯特成为第一座工业城市，这一变革扩展到欧洲及其他地区，重塑了劳动、城市、贸易和全球力量格局。

sources.title: Robert C. Allen, The British Industrial Revolution in Global Perspective (2009)

note: Span is conventional (c. 1760–1820/1840); Wikidata ends it in 1820. Marker at Manchester.

story.en:
No single invention started the Industrial Revolution. In 1709 Abraham Darby began smelting iron with coke instead of charcoal at Coalbrookdale, and from 1712 Thomas Newcomen's steam engines pumped water out of mines. In textiles a run of machines multiplied what one worker could spin: James Hargreaves's spinning jenny, Richard Arkwright's water frame and Samuel Crompton's mule. Arkwright's mill at Cromford, opened in 1771, set the pattern of the factory, with workers bound to the pace of machines and the clock. James Watt's separate condenser, patented in 1769, made steam engines far more efficient, and Boulton and Watt engines were soon driving mills as well as pumps.

Why Britain first? The economic historian Robert Allen argues that British wages were high and coal was cheap, so labour-saving, fuel-hungry machines paid there before anywhere else.

Manchester, nicknamed Cottonopolis, grew from a market town into a city of mills and smoke, and from 1830 a railway linked it to the port of Liverpool. Friedrich Engels's 1845 account of its slums became a classic indictment of industrial poverty. Factory methods spread to Belgium, France, Germany and the United States, and the gap in wealth and power between industrial nations and the rest of the world widened sharply.
story.zh:
工业革命并非由某一项发明开启。1709年，亚伯拉罕·达比在科尔布鲁克代尔改用焦炭代替木炭炼铁；自1712年起，托马斯·纽科门的蒸汽机开始为矿井抽水。纺织业中一连串新机器成倍提高了每个工人的纺纱量：詹姆斯·哈格里夫斯的珍妮纺纱机、理查德·阿克赖特的水力纺纱机和塞缪尔·克朗普顿的走锭纺纱机。阿克赖特1771年在克罗姆福德开办的纱厂奠定了工厂制度的模式，工人从此要跟随机器和时钟的节奏劳作。詹姆斯·瓦特1769年取得专利的分离式冷凝器大大提高了蒸汽机的效率，博尔顿与瓦特公司的蒸汽机很快便不仅用于抽水，也用来驱动纱厂。

为什么英国最先发生？经济史学家罗伯特·艾伦认为，英国工资高而煤价低廉，节省人力、耗费燃料的机器因而在那里最先有利可图。

号称“棉都”的曼彻斯特由一座集镇变成了工厂林立、烟雾弥漫的城市，1830年起铁路把它与利物浦港连接起来。恩格斯1845年对当地贫民窟的描述，成为控诉工业贫困的经典之作。工厂生产方式传播到比利时、法国、德国和美国，工业国家与世界其他地区之间的财富和实力差距急剧拉大。

summary.en: In Berkeley, Gloucestershire, the country doctor Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with matter from a cowpox sore and later showed that he resisted smallpox. Jenner's 1798 report launched vaccination, which spread worldwide within a decade and ultimately led to smallpox's eradication in 1980.
summary.zh: 格洛斯特郡伯克利的乡村医生爱德华·詹纳用牛痘疱疹中的物质为八岁的詹姆斯·菲普斯接种，随后证明他能抵抗天花。詹纳1798年发表的报告开启了疫苗接种，十年内传遍世界，最终使天花于1980年被宣布根除。

sources.title: S. Riedel, "Edward Jenner and the history of smallpox and vaccination", Proceedings (Baylor University Medical Center) 18 (2005)

note: No Wikidata item exists for the inoculation itself; the QID is omitted.

story.en:
Country people in Gloucestershire had long said that milkmaids who caught cowpox, a mild disease of cows' udders, never took smallpox. Edward Jenner, a surgeon in the small town of Berkeley, set out to test the belief. On 14 May 1796 he took fluid from a cowpox sore on the hand of a dairymaid, Sarah Nelmes, and introduced it through two small cuts into the arm of James Phipps, the eight-year-old son of a local labourer. The boy was briefly feverish and recovered. On 1 July Jenner inoculated him with matter from a smallpox pustule, and no illness followed.

After the Royal Society declined his first account, Jenner published An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae at his own expense in 1798, describing Phipps and other cases. He was not the very first to try cowpox: a Dorset farmer, Benjamin Jesty, had protected his family with it in 1774. But Jenner's systematic trials and tireless promotion turned folk wisdom into medicine.

Vaccination, named from the Latin vacca, cow, spread across Europe and overseas within a few years. In 1980 the World Health Organization declared smallpox eradicated. Jenner later gave Phipps a cottage in Berkeley rent-free.
story.zh:
格洛斯特郡的乡民早就流传一种说法：得过牛痘（一种发生在牛乳房上的轻微疾病）的挤奶女工不会染上天花。伯克利小镇的外科医生爱德华·詹纳决定验证这一说法。1796年5月14日，他从挤奶女工萨拉·内尔姆斯手上的牛痘疱中取出浆液，通过两道小切口接种到当地一名劳工八岁的儿子詹姆斯·菲普斯臂上。男孩短暂发烧后便康复了。7月1日，詹纳又用天花脓疱中的物质给他接种，结果他没有发病。

詹纳的首篇报告未被皇家学会接受，于是他在1798年自费出版《牛痘的成因与效果之探究》，记述了菲普斯等病例。他并不是第一个尝试牛痘的人：早在1774年，多塞特郡农夫本杰明·杰斯蒂就曾用牛痘保护家人。但正是詹纳系统的试验和不懈的推广，使这一民间经验成为医学。

“疫苗接种”一词源自拉丁文vacca（牛），这种方法在数年之内便传遍欧洲及海外。1980年，世界卫生组织宣布天花已被根除。詹纳后来还把伯克利的一座小屋免租借给菲普斯居住。

summary.en: Potato blight destroyed the staple crop of Ireland's rural poor in successive years while food exports continued and relief was limited. About one million people died of starvation and disease and over a million emigrated, cutting Ireland's population by roughly a quarter.
summary.zh: 马铃薯晚疫病连年摧毁爱尔兰农村贫民的主粮，而粮食出口照常、救济有限。约100万人死于饥饿和疾病，逾100万人移居海外，爱尔兰人口减少约四分之一。

sources.title: Cormac Ó Gráda, Black '47 and Beyond: The Great Irish Famine in History, Economy, and Memory (1999)

note: Marker at Skibbereen, Co. Cork, one of the worst-hit districts; Wikidata gives the centre of Ireland.

story.en:
By the 1840s some three million Irish people lived almost entirely on potatoes. In September 1845 a blight caused by the water mould Phytophthora infestans, newly arrived from North America, rotted part of the crop; in 1846 it destroyed nearly all of it. Sir Robert Peel's government bought Indian corn from America and repealed the Corn Laws, but his successor, Lord John Russell, relied on public works funded by local rates and on the principle that the market should not be disturbed. Grain and cattle continued to leave Irish ports.

The winter of 1846–47 was the worst. In December 1846 a Cork magistrate, Nicholas Cummins, described starving families in the cabins around Skibbereen in a letter to the Duke of Wellington that was printed in The Times. Soup kitchens were feeding about three million people a day by the summer of 1847, but they were soon closed and relief shifted to overcrowded workhouses. The 'quarter-acre clause' refused aid to anyone holding more land, pushing tenants to give up their holdings, and evictions, typhus and cholera followed.

Roughly a million people died and more than a million emigrated, many in crowded, fever-ridden 'coffin ships'. Emigration went on for decades, and the famine left a lasting bitterness toward British rule.
story.zh:
到19世纪40年代，约有三百万爱尔兰人几乎完全靠马铃薯为生。1845年9月，由刚从北美传入的致病疫霉引起的晚疫病使部分马铃薯烂在地里；1846年，收成几乎全部被毁。罗伯特·皮尔政府从美国购进玉米，并废除了《谷物法》，但继任的约翰·罗素勋爵主要依靠由地方税负担的公共工程，并坚持不干预市场的原则。谷物和牲畜仍源源不断地从爱尔兰港口运出。

1846至1847年的冬天最为惨烈。1846年12月，科克郡治安法官尼古拉斯·卡明斯致信威灵顿公爵，描述斯基伯林一带茅屋中忍饥挨饿的家庭，此信刊登在《泰晤士报》上。到1847年夏，施粥所每天供养约三百万人，但不久即被关闭，救济转由拥挤不堪的济贫院承担。“四分之一英亩条款”规定，凡持有土地超过此数者一律不予救济，迫使佃农放弃土地；驱逐、斑疹伤寒和霍乱接踵而至。

约一百万人死亡，一百多万人移居海外，许多人乘坐的是拥挤不堪、热病横行的“棺材船”。移民潮此后持续了数十年，饥荒也在爱尔兰人心中留下了对英国统治的长久怨恨。

summary.en: Back from holiday at his laboratory in St Mary's Hospital, London, Alexander Fleming noticed that a Penicillium mould had killed the staphylococcus bacteria around it. Howard Florey and Ernst Chain's Oxford team turned penicillin into a usable drug in 1940–41, opening the antibiotic era.
summary.zh: 亚历山大·弗莱明度假归来，在伦敦圣玛丽医院的实验室里发现一种青霉菌杀死了周围的葡萄球菌。1940至1941年，弗洛里和钱恩领导的牛津团队把青霉素制成可用的药物，开启了抗生素时代。

sources.title: American Chemical Society: Discovery and Development of Penicillin (National Historic Chemical Landmark)

story.en:
Alexander Fleming was a gifted but famously untidy bacteriologist at St Mary's Hospital Medical School in Paddington. In September 1928, back from a family holiday, he was sorting through culture plates of Staphylococcus left on his bench when he noticed one contaminated by a mould, around which the bacteria had dissolved. The mould was a Penicillium, probably drifted up from a mycology laboratory on the floor below. Fleming grew it, named the active substance penicillin and in 1929 reported that it killed many disease-causing bacteria without harming white blood cells. But it was unstable and hard to purify, and he moved on to other work.

A decade later, at Oxford's Sir William Dunn School of Pathology, Howard Florey and Ernst Chain took up the problem, with Norman Heatley devising ways to extract it. In May 1940 penicillin saved infected mice. In February 1941 their first patient, the police constable Albert Alexander, began to recover from a severe infection, but the supply ran out and he died.

American firms using deep-tank fermentation scaled up production during the war, and by D-Day in 1944 there was enough for Allied casualties. Fleming, Florey and Chain shared the 1945 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
story.zh:
亚历山大·弗莱明是帕丁顿圣玛丽医院医学院一位才华出众、却以实验台凌乱出名的细菌学家。1928年9月，他度假归来，整理留在台上的葡萄球菌培养皿时，发现其中一个被霉菌污染，霉菌周围的细菌都已溶解。这是一种青霉菌，很可能是从楼下真菌实验室飘上来的。弗莱明培养了这种霉菌，把其中的有效物质命名为青霉素，并在1929年报告它能杀死多种致病菌而不伤害白细胞。但青霉素性质不稳定，难以提纯，他便转向了其他研究。

十年后，牛津大学威廉·邓恩爵士病理学院的霍华德·弗洛里和恩斯特·钱恩重新攻关，诺曼·希特利则设计出提取方法。1940年5月，青霉素救活了受感染的小鼠。1941年2月，他们的第一位病人、警员阿尔伯特·亚历山大的严重感染开始好转，但药物用尽，他终告不治。

战争期间，美国企业采用深罐发酵技术实现了大规模生产，到1944年诺曼底登陆时，青霉素已足以供应盟军伤员。弗莱明、弗洛里和钱恩共同获得1945年诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

name.en: World Wide Web invented at CERN
name.zh: 万维网在欧洲核子研究中心诞生

summary.en: At CERN near Geneva, Tim Berners-Lee proposed a hypertext system for sharing information in March 1989 and, with Robert Cailliau, had the first web server and browser running by the end of 1990. Opened to the public in 1991 and released royalty-free in 1993, the Web made the Internet a mass medium.
summary.zh: 1989年3月，蒂姆·伯纳斯-李在日内瓦附近的欧洲核子研究中心提出一种共享信息的超文本系统，并与罗伯特·卡约于1990年底建成第一台网络服务器和浏览器。万维网1991年向公众开放，1993年免版税发布，使互联网成为大众媒介。

sources.title: Tim Berners-Lee, Information Management: A Proposal (CERN, March 1989), W3C archive
CERN: The World Wide Web project (the first website, info.cern.ch)

story.en:
CERN, the European particle-physics laboratory on the Franco-Swiss border near Geneva, was a place where thousands of scientists using incompatible computers struggled to keep track of documents. In March 1989 Tim Berners-Lee, a British software engineer there, wrote a proposal for a linked information system. His supervisor, Mike Sendall, wrote 'Vague but exciting' on the cover and let him carry on.

Working on a NeXT computer, with the Belgian engineer Robert Cailliau as his chief ally, Berners-Lee defined the three pieces that still underpin the Web: HTML for writing pages, HTTP for transferring them and URLs for addressing them. By the end of 1990 the first web server and a browser-editor called WorldWideWeb were running at CERN, and a label on the machine warned colleagues not to switch it off. On 6 August 1991 Berners-Lee posted a summary of the project to a public newsgroup, inviting anyone to join in.

The decisive step came on 30 April 1993, when CERN put the Web software into the public domain, free of royalties. That same year the Mosaic browser made the Web easy to use, and the number of sites exploded. In 1994 Berners-Lee founded the World Wide Web Consortium to look after its standards.
story.zh:
欧洲核子研究中心坐落在日内瓦附近的法瑞边境上，数千名科学家在互不兼容的计算机上工作，要追踪各种文档极为困难。1989年3月，在那里工作的英国软件工程师蒂姆·伯纳斯-李写了一份建立互相链接的信息系统的建议书。他的上司迈克·森德尔在封面上批了一句“含糊，但令人兴奋”，准许他继续做下去。

伯纳斯-李在一台NeXT计算机上工作，最得力的伙伴是比利时工程师罗伯特·卡约。他定义了至今仍支撑着万维网的三项基础：编写网页的HTML、传输网页的HTTP和标识网页地址的URL。到1990年底，第一台网络服务器和名为WorldWideWeb的浏览编辑器已在中心运行，机器上还贴着标签，提醒同事不要关机。1991年8月6日，伯纳斯-李在一个公共新闻组上发布项目简介，邀请所有人参与。

决定性的一步发生在1993年4月30日：欧洲核子研究中心宣布将万维网软件免版税地置于公有领域。同年问世的Mosaic浏览器使万维网简单易用，网站数量随之激增。1994年，伯纳斯-李创立万维网联盟，负责维护其技术标准。

summary.en: Between the murder of Severus Alexander in 235 and the accession of Diocletian in 284, the Roman Empire went through some two dozen emperors, foreign invasions, plague and runaway debasement of the coinage, and for a time split into Roman, Gallic and Palmyrene realms.
summary.zh: 从235年亚历山大·塞维鲁遇刺到284年戴克里先即位，罗马帝国先后更换了二十余位皇帝，外敌入侵、瘟疫和货币急剧贬值接踵而至，帝国一度分裂为罗马、高卢和帕尔米拉三部分。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Crisis of the Third Century
Britannica: ancient Rome, the crisis of the third century
D. S. Potter, The Roman Empire at Bay, AD 180–395 (2004)

note: A period rather than a single event; the point is placed at Rome. Start and end years follow the usual convention (235 murder of Severus Alexander, 284 accession of Diocletian).

story.en:
In 235 soldiers on the Rhine murdered the emperor Severus Alexander and his mother at Mogontiacum (Mainz) and acclaimed the officer Maximinus Thrax. For the next half-century the army made and unmade emperors, and most of the two dozen or so rulers recognised in Rome died violently.

Pressure came from every side. Goths crossed the Danube and killed Decius at Abritus in 251, the first emperor to fall to a foreign enemy. In 260 the Persian king Shapur I captured Valerian, who died a prisoner. A Gallic Empire broke away in the west, while Queen Zenobia of Palmyra took over the eastern provinces. Plague swept the cities, and the silver coinage was debased until the antoninianus held only a few per cent of silver.

Aurelian reunited the empire by 274 and ringed Rome itself with new walls, a telling sign of insecurity. Diocletian, acclaimed in 284, rebuilt the state on a more bureaucratic and military footing, and the late Roman world that emerged was very different from the empire of Augustus.
story.zh:
235年，莱茵河前线的士兵在莫贡提亚库姆（今美因茨）杀死皇帝亚历山大·塞维鲁及其母亲，拥立军官马克西米努斯·色雷克斯。此后半个世纪，皇帝的废立操于军队之手，在罗马获得承认的二十余位统治者大多死于非命。

帝国四面受敌。哥特人渡过多瑙河，251年在阿布里图斯杀死德西乌斯，这是第一位死于外敌之手的罗马皇帝。260年，波斯国王沙普尔一世俘虏了瓦勒良，后者最终死于囚禁之中。西部分裂出“高卢帝国”，帕尔米拉女王芝诺比娅则占据东方诸省。瘟疫席卷城市，银币不断贬值，安东尼尼安努斯银币的含银量最终只剩百分之几。

奥勒良到274年重新统一帝国，并为罗马城本身修筑新城墙，足见当时的不安。284年即位的戴克里先以更加官僚化、军事化的方式重建国家，由此形成的晚期罗马世界已与奥古斯都时代的帝国大不相同。

summary.en: Diocletian divided imperial rule between two senior emperors (Augusti) and two junior ones (Caesars). From 1 March 293 Diocletian, based at Nicomedia, and Maximian, based at Milan, shared power with Galerius and Constantius I; the system steadied the frontiers but dissolved into civil war after Diocletian abdicated in 305.
summary.zh: 戴克里先把帝国统治权分给两位正帝（奥古斯都）和两位副帝（恺撒）。自293年3月1日起，坐镇尼科米底亚的戴克里先与坐镇米兰的马克西米安，同伽列里乌斯和君士坦提乌斯一世共治天下。这一制度稳定了边疆，但在305年戴克里先退位后陷入内战。

sources.title: T. D. Barnes, The New Empire of Diocletian and Constantine (1982)

note: Year is the appointment of the two Caesars (traditionally 1 March 293); Maximian had been Diocletian's colleague since 285/286. Point at Milan (Mediolanum), Maximian's seat; Diocletian resided mainly at Nicomedia in Asia Minor.

summary.en: On 28 October 312 Constantine defeated his rival Maxentius just north of Rome, and Maxentius drowned in the Tiber. Constantine credited the Christian God with his victory, and his patronage set Christianity on its way to becoming the dominant faith of the empire.
summary.zh: 312年10月28日，君士坦丁在罗马城北击败对手马克森提乌斯，后者溺死于台伯河。君士坦丁把胜利归功于基督教的上帝，他的扶持使基督教逐步成为帝国的主导信仰。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of the Milvian Bridge
Britannica: Battle of the Milvian Bridge

story.en:
By 312 Diocletian's system of four emperors had broken down into rival claimants. Constantine, acclaimed by his father's troops at York in 306, crossed the Alps from Gaul and marched on Rome, held by Maxentius, son of the old emperor Maximian.

Two Christian writers describe a divine sign before the battle. Lactantius, writing within a few years, says Constantine was told in a dream to mark a heavenly symbol, the Chi-Rho, on his soldiers' shields. Eusebius, retelling what he says Constantine told him long afterwards, adds a cross of light in the sky with the words 'by this conquer'. Historians still debate what Constantine saw and believed.

Maxentius chose to fight with the Tiber at his back, beside the stone Milvian Bridge and a temporary bridge of boats. When his line broke, the fleeing troops jammed the crossing and Maxentius drowned. Constantine entered Rome the next day, and in 313 he and Licinius agreed the policy of toleration known as the Edict of Milan. The arch the Senate raised for him beside the Colosseum vaguely credits his victory to the prompting of the divinity.
story.zh:
到312年，戴克里先的四帝体制已瓦解为群雄并立。306年在约克被其父部下拥立的君士坦丁从高卢翻越阿尔卑斯山，进军由老皇帝马克西米安之子马克森提乌斯据守的罗马。

两位基督教作家记载了战前的神迹。数年后写作的拉克坦提乌斯说，君士坦丁在梦中得到指示，要在士兵盾牌上画上一个天上的符号，即“凯乐”符号。尤西比乌斯则转述多年后君士坦丁亲口对他讲的话，说天空中出现了一个光芒十字架，并伴有“以此得胜”的字样。君士坦丁究竟看到了什么、信仰了什么，史家至今仍有争论。

马克森提乌斯选择背靠台伯河作战，阵地在石砌的米尔维安大桥和一座临时浮桥旁。阵线崩溃后，溃兵挤满桥面，马克森提乌斯落水溺亡。次日君士坦丁进入罗马，313年又与李锡尼共同确立了宽容基督教的政策，即《米兰敕令》。元老院在斗兽场旁为他建造的凯旋门上，只含糊地把胜利归于“神明的感召”。

summary.en: In June 455 the Vandal king Gaiseric sailed from Carthage and plundered Rome for some two weeks, after the emperor Petronius Maximus had been killed while fleeing. Pope Leo I reportedly persuaded him to spare the city from burning and massacre; the Vandals carried off treasure, captives and the imperial women.
summary.zh: 455年6月，汪达尔国王盖萨里克从迦太基渡海而来，在皇帝佩特罗尼乌斯·马克西穆斯出逃时被杀之后，劫掠罗马约两周。据记载，教宗利奥一世劝说他不要纵火屠城；汪达尔人掳走了大批财宝、俘虏和皇室妇女。

sources.title: Prosper of Aquitaine, Epitoma chronicon, s.a. 455
Procopius, History of the Wars III.5

note: Dates follow the usual reconstruction: Vandals enter Rome on 2 June 455 and leave after about fourteen days.

story.en:
The murder of Valentinian III in March 455 broke the alliance that bound the Vandal kingdom of Africa to Rome. The new emperor, Petronius Maximus, forced Valentinian's widow Licinia Eudoxia to marry him and married his son to her daughter Eudocia, who had been promised to Gaiseric's son Huneric. Gaiseric sailed for Italy. As his fleet approached, Maximus tried to flee and was killed by a Roman crowd on 31 May.

Three days later the Vandals entered the city unopposed. According to the chronicler Prosper of Aquitaine, Pope Leo I met Gaiseric and persuaded him to refrain from fire, torture and killing. For about two weeks the Vandals stripped Rome methodically, loading their ships with gold, statues and, Procopius says, treasures that Titus had once taken from the Temple in Jerusalem. They also carried Eudoxia and her daughters to Carthage.

The sack was far more thorough than Alaric's in 410 and showed that the western emperors could no longer protect their ancient capital. In 1794 the French cleric Henri Grégoire coined the word vandalism, giving the Vandals a reputation for mindless destruction that historians think exaggerated.
story.zh:
455年3月瓦伦提尼安三世遇刺，汪达尔非洲王国与罗马之间的同盟随之破裂。新皇帝佩特罗尼乌斯·马克西穆斯强娶瓦伦提尼安的遗孀李锡尼娅·欧多克西娅，又让儿子娶了她的女儿欧多西娅，而欧多西娅原已许配给盖萨里克之子胡内里克。盖萨里克于是渡海进攻意大利。舰队逼近时，马克西穆斯企图出逃，5月31日被罗马民众杀死。

三天后，汪达尔人兵不血刃进入罗马。据编年史家阿基坦的普罗斯珀记载，教宗利奥一世面见盖萨里克，劝他不要纵火、施刑和杀戮。此后约两周，汪达尔人有条不紊地搜刮全城，把黄金、雕像装上船只；据普罗柯比记载，其中还有当年提图斯从耶路撒冷圣殿掠来的珍宝。欧多克西娅和她的女儿们也被带往迦太基。

这次洗劫远比410年阿拉里克那次彻底，表明西罗马皇帝已无力保护自己的古都。1794年，法国神职人员亨利·格雷古瓦创造了“汪达尔主义”（意为恣意破坏）一词，使汪达尔人背上了野蛮破坏的名声，而史家认为这一名声有所夸大。

name.zh: 盎格鲁-撒克逊人定居不列颠

summary.en: In the fifth and sixth centuries Angles, Saxons, Jutes and other Germanic peoples settled lowland Britain after the end of Roman rule. Bede dated the arrival of Hengest and Horsa to about 449, but archaeology and ancient DNA point to a gradual, regionally varied mix of migration and cultural change that laid the foundations of England.
summary.zh: 罗马统治结束后，盎格鲁人、撒克逊人、朱特人等日耳曼人群在5至6世纪陆续定居不列颠低地。比德把亨吉斯特和霍萨的到来定在449年前后，但考古和古DNA研究显示，这是一个渐进且因地而异的移民与文化转变过程，奠定了英格兰的基础。

sources.title: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English People I.15
Gildas, De excidio et conquestu Britanniae 23
J. Gretzinger et al., The Anglo-Saxon migration and the formation of the early English gene pool, Nature 610 (2022)

note: A long process with approximate dates (c. 450–600). Bede's 449 and the story of Hengest and Horsa invited by Vortigern are traditional and partly legendary. Point placed at Ebbsfleet on the Isle of Thanet, the traditional landing place named in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

name.zh: 狄奥多里克攻取拉文纳

summary.en: After a siege of nearly three years, Odoacer surrendered Ravenna to the Ostrogothic king Theodoric under an agreement to share power. Days later Theodoric killed him with his own hands at a banquet, and went on to rule Italy from Ravenna until 526.
summary.zh: 经过近三年的围攻，奥多亚克以分享权力为条件，将拉文纳交给东哥特国王狄奥多里克。几天后，狄奥多里克在宴会上亲手杀死奥多亚克，此后以拉文纳为都城统治意大利，直到526年。

note: QID is the siege of 490–493, which ended with Theodoric's entry on 5 March 493; Odoacer was killed on 15 March.

story.en:
Odoacer had ruled Italy as king since deposing the boy emperor Romulus Augustulus in 476. In 488 the eastern emperor Zeno encouraged Theodoric, the Ostrogothic king whose people had become a troublesome presence in the Balkans, to go west and replace him. Theodoric beat Odoacer on the Isonzo and at Verona in 489 and on the Adda in 490, and Odoacer withdrew behind the marshes of Ravenna, which held out for almost three years.

Early in 493, with the city starving, Bishop John of Ravenna brokered a deal by which the two kings would rule jointly. Theodoric entered on 5 March. Ten days later, according to the chronicler John of Antioch, he invited Odoacer to a feast and cut him down with his own sword, remarking that the wretch seemed to have no bones in him. Odoacer's family and followers were then hunted down.

Theodoric governed Italy until 526 with Roman ministers such as Cassiodorus and Boethius, kept the Senate and Roman law, and filled Ravenna with buildings such as his mausoleum and the church now called Sant'Apollinare Nuovo.
story.zh:
476年废黜少年皇帝罗慕路斯·奥古斯都路斯之后，奥多亚克一直以国王身份统治意大利。488年，东罗马皇帝芝诺鼓动东哥特国王狄奥多里克西进取而代之，因为他的部众在巴尔干已成心腹之患。489年，狄奥多里克在伊松佐河和维罗纳两次击败奥多亚克，490年又在阿达河获胜。奥多亚克退守沼泽环绕的拉文纳，坚持了近三年。

493年初，城中饥荒严重，拉文纳主教约翰出面斡旋，约定两王共治。3月5日狄奥多里克入城。据编年史家安条克的约翰记载，十天后他设宴款待奥多亚克，席间亲手挥剑将其砍倒，还说这个可怜虫身上好像没有骨头。奥多亚克的家人和部下随即遭到追杀。

狄奥多里克统治意大利直到526年，重用卡西奥多鲁斯、波爱修斯等罗马大臣，保留元老院和罗马法，并在拉文纳兴建了他的陵墓以及今称新圣阿波利纳雷教堂等建筑。

summary.en: In 507 Clovis and his Franks defeated the Visigoths near Poitiers, and King Alaric II was killed, by Clovis himself according to Gregory of Tours. The Franks took most of Aquitaine, and the Visigothic kingdom was reduced to Hispania and Septimania.
summary.zh: 507年，克洛维率法兰克人在普瓦捷附近击败西哥特人，国王阿拉里克二世阵亡，据图尔的格雷戈里记载是被克洛维亲手所杀。法兰克人夺取了阿基坦大部，西哥特王国则退缩到西班牙和塞普提曼尼亚。

sources.title: R. W. Mathisen and D. Shanzer (eds.), The Battle of Vouillé, 507 CE (2012)

note: The year 507 is secure, but the site of the campus Vogladensis is debated (Vouillé and Voulon near Poitiers are the main candidates); point placed at Vouillé.

story.en:
By the early sixth century Clovis had made the Franks masters of northern Gaul. South of the Loire lay the Visigothic kingdom of Toulouse under Alaric II. Clovis, recently baptised a Catholic, could present himself to the Gallo-Roman bishops as the champion of orthodoxy against the Arian Goths.

According to Gregory of Tours, writing about seventy years later, Clovis told his men that he could not bear Arians holding part of Gaul and led them south. Gregory reports omens on the march: a deer that showed the army a ford across the flooded Vienne, and a light that shone from the church of St Hilary at Poitiers. On the plain of Vouillé the Goths fled, and Gregory says Clovis killed Alaric with his own hand and narrowly escaped two Gothic spearmen.

The victory brought Toulouse and most of Aquitaine under Frankish rule. Only Ostrogothic intervention saved Septimania for the Visigoths, whose centre of gravity moved to Spain. In 508 the emperor Anastasius honoured Clovis with the title of consul, celebrated at Tours, and Clovis made Paris his seat.
story.zh:
到6世纪初，克洛维已使法兰克人成为高卢北部的主人。卢瓦尔河以南是阿拉里克二世统治的西哥特图卢兹王国。新近受洗为天主教徒的克洛维，可以在高卢-罗马主教们面前以正统信仰捍卫者的姿态，对抗信奉阿里乌派的哥特人。

据约七十年后写作的图尔的格雷戈里记载，克洛维对部下说，他不能容忍阿里乌派占据高卢的一部分，随即挥师南下。格雷戈里还记下了行军途中的征兆：一头鹿为大军指出了涨水的维埃纳河的渡口，普瓦捷圣伊莱尔教堂上方则闪耀起光芒。在武耶平原上，哥特人溃逃；格雷戈里说克洛维亲手杀死了阿拉里克，自己也险些死于两名哥特长矛手之手。

这场胜利使图卢兹和阿基坦大部归于法兰克统治。全赖东哥特人出兵干预，西哥特人才保住塞普提曼尼亚，其重心随后转向西班牙。508年，东罗马皇帝阿纳斯塔修斯授予克洛维执政官荣衔，庆典在图尔举行，克洛维此后定都巴黎。

summary.en: In spring 568 King Alboin led the Lombards and allied peoples from Pannonia over the Julian Alps into an Italy exhausted by the Gothic War. They took Cividale, Milan (569) and, after a long siege, Pavia, breaking Byzantine Italy into scattered enclaves and founding a kingdom that lasted until 774.
summary.zh: 568年春，阿尔博因率伦巴第人及其盟友从潘诺尼亚翻越尤利安阿尔卑斯山，进入因哥特战争而元气大伤的意大利。他们攻占奇维达莱、米兰（569年），又经长期围攻拿下帕维亚，使拜占庭在意大利的领土支离破碎，所建王国一直延续到774年。

sources.title: Paul the Deacon, History of the Lombards II.7–27

note: No Wikidata item for the invasion itself (Q3857240, Lombard migration, covers the whole migration). Point at Cividale del Friuli (Forum Iulii), the first city taken and seat of the first Lombard duchy. End year is the fall of Pavia (572 or 573). Paul the Deacon's claim that the general Narses invited the Lombards is generally regarded as legend.

name.zh: 格里高利传教团赴英格兰

summary.en: Sent by Pope Gregory the Great, the monk Augustine and about forty companions landed in Kent in 597. King Æthelberht, whose Frankish queen Bertha was already Christian, welcomed them to Canterbury and soon accepted baptism, and Augustine became the first archbishop of Canterbury.
summary.zh: 597年，奉教宗格里高利一世之命，修士奥古斯丁带领约四十名同伴在肯特登陆。王后伯莎是信奉基督教的法兰克公主，国王埃塞尔伯特在坎特伯雷接待了他们，不久便接受洗礼，奥古斯丁则成为首任坎特伯雷大主教。

sources.title: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English People I.23–33, II.1
Gregory the Great, Letter to Eulogius of Alexandria (Register VIII.29)

note: Point at St Augustine's Abbey, Canterbury. The date of Æthelberht's baptism is not recorded; 597 is traditional.

story.en:
Pope Gregory I chose Augustine, prior of his own monastery of St Andrew in Rome, to lead a mission to the pagan English. Bede preserves the famous story that Gregory, years before, had seen fair-haired English boys for sale in Rome and punned that they were not Angles but angels; Bede himself presents it as a tradition handed down.

The missionaries nearly turned back in Gaul, but Gregory urged them on. They landed on the Isle of Thanet in 597, and King Æthelberht of Kent met them in the open air, Bede says, because he feared they might work magic on him indoors. His wife Bertha, a Frankish princess, already worshipped with her own bishop in the old church of St Martin outside Canterbury.

Æthelberht was baptised, probably soon after, and Gregory boasted in a letter that more than ten thousand English had been baptised at Christmas 597. Augustine founded Christ Church cathedral and a monastery outside the walls, and Canterbury has remained the seat of the senior archbishop of the English church ever since.
story.zh:
教宗格里高利一世挑选他在罗马创立的圣安德烈修道院院长奥古斯丁，率团向信奉异教的英格兰人传教。比德记下了一个著名的故事：多年前，格里高利在罗马看到被贩卖的金发英格兰少年，便用双关语说他们不是“盎格鲁人”，而是“天使”；比德本人也说明这只是代代相传的说法。

传教士们在高卢时几乎打了退堂鼓，但格里高利敦促他们继续前行。597年，他们在萨尼特岛登陆。比德说，肯特国王埃塞尔伯特担心他们在室内施展法术，特意在露天接见。他的王后伯莎是法兰克公主，早已带着自己的主教在坎特伯雷城外古老的圣马丁教堂礼拜。

埃塞尔伯特很可能不久便受了洗。格里高利在信中自豪地说，597年圣诞节有一万多名英格兰人受洗。奥古斯丁创建了基督教会座堂，又在城外建立修道院。此后坎特伯雷一直是英格兰教会首席大主教的驻地。

summary.en: In the mountains of Asturias a small Christian force under Pelayo defeated a Muslim expedition at Covadonga, probably around 722. Militarily minor, the victory secured an independent kingdom of Asturias and was later celebrated as the beginning of the Christian Reconquista.
summary.zh: 大约在722年，佩拉约率领一支小规模的基督徒队伍在阿斯图里亚斯山区的科瓦东加击败穆斯林远征军。这场胜利在军事上规模不大，却保住了独立的阿斯图里亚斯王国，后来被尊为基督徒“收复失地运动”的开端。

sources.title: R. Collins, The Arab Conquest of Spain, 710–797 (1989)

note: Date disputed: Spanish tradition gives 722, other reckonings 718 (Wikidata), and Britannica says about 720. Point at the cave of Covadonga (Santa Cueva). The battle narrative survives mainly in Asturian chronicles written some 160 years later.

story.en:
Within a few years of 711 Muslim armies had overrun almost the whole Visigothic kingdom. In the Cantabrian Mountains, however, a nobleman named Pelayo refused to pay tribute and was chosen as leader by the Asturians.

The main narrative comes from the Chronicle of Alfonso III, written some 160 years later. It describes a large army under a commander called Alqama, accompanied by the collaborating bishop Oppas, advancing up the narrow valley below the cave of Covadonga. Pelayo's men, sheltering in and around the cave, were saved, the chronicle says, when the stones and arrows hurled at them turned back on the attackers, and the fleeing enemy was later buried by a landslide. A much later Arab account mentions only some thirty wild men on a rock, judged not worth pursuing.

Whatever its scale, the clash let Pelayo keep a mountain realm centred on Cangas de Onís. His successors expanded it into the kingdoms of Asturias and León, and later Spanish tradition made Covadonga the founding victory of the Reconquista. The cave shrine remains a place of pilgrimage.
story.zh:
711年后不过数年，穆斯林军队便席卷了几乎整个西哥特王国。然而在坎塔布里亚山区，一位名叫佩拉约的贵族拒绝纳贡，被阿斯图里亚斯人推举为首领。

主要的战斗记载出自约一百六十年后成书的《阿方索三世编年史》。据其描述，一位名叫阿尔卡马的将领率大军，在投靠穆斯林的主教奥帕斯陪同下，沿科瓦东加山洞下方狭窄的山谷推进。佩拉约的部下据守山洞内外，编年史说，射向他们的石块和箭矢竟反转回去打中了进攻者，溃逃的敌军后来又被山崩掩埋。一部晚得多的阿拉伯文献则只提到岩石上约三十个“野人”，认为不值得追击。

无论规模如何，这场冲突使佩拉约保住了以坎加斯-德奥尼斯为中心的山地王国。他的继承者将其扩展为阿斯图里亚斯王国和莱昂王国，后来的西班牙传统更把科瓦东加奉为收复失地运动的开山之战。山洞圣所至今仍是朝圣之地。

name.en: Founding of the Great Mosque of Córdoba
name.zh: 科尔多瓦大清真寺始建

summary.en: About 785 Abd al-Rahman I, founder of the Umayyad emirate in al-Andalus, began a great congregational mosque in Córdoba. Enlarged by his successors until 987, its forest of columns and double arches made it a masterpiece of Islamic architecture; since 1236 it has served as the city's cathedral.
summary.zh: 约785年，安达卢斯倭马亚埃米尔国的创建者阿卜杜·拉赫曼一世在科尔多瓦兴建一座大清真寺。经后继者不断扩建至987年，其林立的柱子和双层拱券使之成为伊斯兰建筑的杰作；1236年起它一直是该城的主教座堂。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Centre of Cordoba
J. D. Dodds (ed.), Al-Andalus: The Art of Islamic Spain (Metropolitan Museum of Art, 1992)

note: QID is the building. Construction is dated 785 or 786 (Wikidata gives 786).

story.en:
Abd al-Rahman I was the only prominent Umayyad prince to escape the Abbasid massacre of his family in 750. He reached al-Andalus, made himself emir at Córdoba in 756, and about 785 began a new congregational mosque on the site of the church of St Vincent, which later Arabic accounts say he bought from the city's Christians.

The builders reused Roman and Visigothic columns and, to gain height, set a second tier of arches above the first, striped in red brick and pale stone. Abd al-Rahman II and al-Hakam II extended the prayer hall; al-Hakam's mihrab of the 960s, sheathed in gold mosaic made with help from a craftsman sent by the Byzantine emperor, is its jewel. Al-Mansur's enlargement of 987 made it one of the largest mosques in the world.

After Ferdinand III of Castile took Córdoba in 1236 the mosque was consecrated as a cathedral, and in the sixteenth century a Renaissance nave was built into its heart. Charles V is said to have lamented that the canons had destroyed something unique to build what could be found anywhere, though the remark is known only from later tradition.
story.zh:
阿卜杜·拉赫曼一世是750年阿拔斯王朝屠杀其家族时唯一逃脱的重要倭马亚王子。他辗转来到安达卢斯，756年在科尔多瓦自立为埃米尔，约785年在圣文森特教堂旧址上动工兴建新的聚礼清真寺；后世阿拉伯文献称，这块地是他从城中基督徒手中买下的。

工匠们重复利用了罗马和西哥特时代的石柱，为增加高度，在下层拱券之上再叠一层，拱券以红砖和浅色石块相间砌成。阿卜杜·拉赫曼二世和哈卡姆二世相继扩建礼拜大殿；哈卡姆二世在960年代修建的米哈拉布饰以金色马赛克，据载曾得到拜占庭皇帝派来的工匠相助，堪称全寺精华。987年曼苏尔的扩建使之跻身世界最大的清真寺之列。

1236年卡斯蒂利亚国王费尔南多三世攻占科尔多瓦后，清真寺被祝圣为主教座堂；16世纪又在其中心建起文艺复兴式的中殿。相传查理五世曾感叹，教士们毁掉了独一无二的东西，换来随处可见的建筑，不过这句话只见于后世传说。

summary.en: After defeating the Lombard king Aistulf, the Frankish king Pepin the Short handed the conquered lands of the exarchate of Ravenna and the Pentapolis to Pope Stephen II instead of returning them to Byzantium. The grant laid the territorial foundation of the Papal States, which lasted until 1870.
summary.zh: 法兰克国王矮子丕平击败伦巴第国王艾斯图尔夫后，没有把夺得的拉文纳总督区和彭塔波利斯归还拜占庭，而是献给教宗斯德望二世。这次献土奠定了教皇国的领土基础，教皇国一直存续到1870年。

sources.title: Liber Pontificalis, Life of Stephen II
T. F. X. Noble, The Republic of St. Peter: The Birth of the Papal State, 680–825 (1984)

note: Pepin promised the lands at Quierzy in 754 and handed them over after his second Italian campaign in 756. According to the Liber Pontificalis his envoy Abbot Fulrad laid the keys of the cities on the tomb of St Peter, so the point is placed at St Peter's in Rome.

name.zh: 维京人袭击林迪斯法恩

summary.en: On 8 June 793 Norse raiders plundered the island monastery of Lindisfarne off the Northumbrian coast, killing monks and seizing treasure. It was not the first Viking attack on England, but it shocked Christian Europe and is conventionally taken as the start of the Viking Age.
summary.zh: 793年6月8日，北欧袭掠者洗劫了诺森布里亚海岸外林迪斯法恩岛上的修道院，杀害修士，掠走财宝。这并非维京人第一次袭击英格兰，却震动了整个基督教欧洲，通常被视为维京时代的开端。

sources.title: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (MS D and E), entry for 793
Alcuin, Letter to King Æthelred of Northumbria (793)

note: The Chronicle's date is 8 June (some manuscripts read 8 January, usually corrected to June since raiders sailed in summer). The wider phenomenon is covered by ev-viking-expansion.

story.en:
Lindisfarne, a tidal island off the Northumbrian coast, had been a centre of English Christianity since Aidan founded a monastery there in 635. It held the shrine of St Cuthbert, and earlier in the century its monks had produced the Lindisfarne Gospels.

The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle reports that 793 began with dire portents over Northumbria: whirlwinds, lightning and fiery dragons flying in the sky, followed by famine. Then, on 8 June, the ravaging of heathen men destroyed God's church on Lindisfarne with plunder and slaughter. Some monks were killed, others drowned or carried off as slaves, and the church's treasures were taken.

The scholar Alcuin, a Northumbrian then at Charlemagne's court, wrote to King Æthelred that no such terror had ever appeared in Britain and that no one had believed such a voyage from the sea possible. He saw the attack as God's punishment for the sins of the English. Raids on Jarrow, Iona and Irish monasteries soon followed, and in 875 the Lindisfarne community abandoned the island, carrying Cuthbert's body with them.
story.zh:
林迪斯法恩是诺森布里亚海岸外的一座潮汐岛，635年艾丹在此建立修道院后，一直是英格兰基督教的中心。这里供奉着圣卡斯伯特的圣龛，本世纪早些时候岛上修士还绘制了《林迪斯法恩福音书》。

《盎格鲁-撒克逊编年史》记载，793年开年，诺森布里亚上空凶兆频现：旋风、闪电，还有火龙在空中飞舞，随后又是饥荒。接着在6月8日，异教徒的劫掠以抢夺和杀戮摧毁了林迪斯法恩岛上的上帝教堂。一些修士被杀，另一些溺水而亡或被掳为奴，教堂的珍宝被洗劫一空。

当时在查理曼宫廷的诺森布里亚学者阿尔昆致信国王埃塞尔雷德，说不列颠从未出现过如此恐怖之事，也没有人相信有人能从海上发动这样的袭击。他认为这是上帝对英格兰人罪孽的惩罚。不久，贾罗、艾奥纳和爱尔兰的修道院也相继遭袭。875年，林迪斯法恩的修士们抬着卡斯伯特的遗体离开了这座岛。

summary.en: In May 878 Alfred of Wessex, emerging from refuge in the Somerset marshes, defeated Guthrum's Danish army at Ethandun. Guthrum accepted baptism with Alfred as his godfather and withdrew to East Anglia, saving Wessex and preparing the ground for a united English kingdom.
summary.zh: 878年5月，韦塞克斯国王阿尔弗雷德走出萨默塞特沼泽中的避难地，在埃丹顿击败古特伦率领的丹麦大军。古特伦接受洗礼，由阿尔弗雷德担任教父，随后退往东盎格利亚。这一胜利保住了韦塞克斯，也为日后统一的英格兰王国奠定了基础。

note: Ethandun is generally identified with Edington, Wiltshire; the exact battlefield is not known.

story.en:
Around Twelfth Night 878, Guthrum's Danes made a surprise winter attack on the royal estate at Chippenham. Much of Wessex submitted, and Alfred withdrew with a small band to the marshes of Athelney in Somerset. The tale of the king letting a peasant woman's cakes burn there first appears in a later life of St Neot and is best treated as legend.

From his fortified refuge Alfred harried the Danes, and in the seventh week after Easter he rode to Egbert's Stone, where, Asser says, the men of Somerset, Wiltshire and Hampshire joyfully joined him. Two days later he met the Danish army at Ethandun, fought in a close shield wall and drove it from the field. He then besieged the survivors in their stronghold, probably Chippenham, for two weeks until they surrendered.

Guthrum and thirty of his leading men were baptised at Aller, with Alfred as godfather. The Danes withdrew to East Anglia, where Guthrum ruled as a Christian king, and Wessex survived to become the core around which Alfred's successors built England.
story.zh:
878年第十二夜前后，古特伦的丹麦军在冬季突袭了奇彭纳姆的王室庄园。韦塞克斯大部分地区归降，阿尔弗雷德带着一小队人马退入萨默塞特的阿塞尔尼沼泽。国王在那里替农妇看饼却把饼烤焦的故事，最早见于后世的《圣尼奥特传》，应视为传说。

阿尔弗雷德以设防的避难地为基地不断袭扰丹麦人。复活节后第七周，他驰往“埃格伯特之石”，据阿瑟记载，萨默塞特、威尔特郡和汉普郡的兵士欣然前来会合。两天后，他在埃丹顿与丹麦大军交锋，以紧密的盾墙作战，将敌军逐出战场，随后又把残部围困在其据点（很可能是奇彭纳姆）两周，直至对方投降。

古特伦和他手下三十名首领在阿勒受洗，阿尔弗雷德担任教父。丹麦人退往东盎格利亚，古特伦在那里以基督徒国王身份统治；韦塞克斯得以保全，成为阿尔弗雷德的继承者们建立英格兰的核心。

summary.en: Duke William I of Aquitaine founded the Benedictine abbey of Cluny in Burgundy under Abbot Berno, placing it under the protection of the pope and freeing it from control by lay lords and local bishops. Cluny became the head of a vast network of monasteries and a leading force in the reform of the medieval church.
summary.zh: 阿基坦公爵威廉一世在勃艮第创立本笃会克吕尼修道院，以贝尔诺为院长，把修道院置于教宗保护之下，使其不受世俗领主和地方主教的控制。克吕尼后来成为庞大修道院网络的首脑，是中世纪教会改革的重要力量。

sources.title: Foundation charter of Cluny (910), in Internet Medieval Sourcebook
B. H. Rosenwein, To Be the Neighbor of Saint Peter (1989)

note: QID is the abbey. The foundation charter is dated 11 September 910 (Wikidata gives 909, a minority dating).

summary.en: About 930 the chieftains of Iceland set up the Althing, a general assembly meeting every summer at Þingvellir to make law and settle disputes. Often called the oldest surviving parliament, it accepted Christianity for Iceland around 1000 and, after a break from 1800 to 1845, still sits in Reykjavík.
summary.zh: 约930年，冰岛各地首领建立了全岛大会“阿尔庭”，每年夏天在议会平原（辛格韦德利）集会，制定法律、裁决纷争。它常被称为现存最古老的议会，约1000年在此决定冰岛皈依基督教；1800年至1845年中断后恢复，至今仍在雷克雅未克开会。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Þingvellir National Park

note: The date 930 rests on Ari Þorgilsson's twelfth-century reckoning. QID is the institution (its Wikidata coordinates are the modern parliament in Reykjavík); the point here is the original assembly site at Þingvellir.

story.en:
Iceland was settled from about 870, mostly by Norwegians and the Irish and Scottish slaves and dependants they brought. The island had no king. According to Ari Thorgilsson's Book of the Icelanders, written in the 1120s, a man named Úlfljótr went to Norway to adapt its laws, and around 930 the chieftains created a general assembly for the whole country.

The Althing met for two weeks each summer in the rift valley later called Þingvellir, the assembly plains. A law council of chieftains made and amended law, courts heard cases, and an elected lawspeaker recited a third of the law each year from the Law Rock. It was also a great fair and meeting place.

Its most famous decision came around 1000, when pagan and Christian factions threatened to split the country. Ari relates that the lawspeaker Thorgeir, himself a pagan, lay under his cloak for a day and a night before ruling that all Icelanders should be baptised, while private pagan worship was tolerated for a time. The Althing lost its powers under the Norwegian and Danish kings, was abolished in 1800 and revived in Reykjavík in 1845.
story.zh:
冰岛自约870年起开始有人定居，移民主要是挪威人以及他们带来的爱尔兰、苏格兰奴隶和依附者。岛上没有国王。据阿里·索吉尔松在1120年代写成的《冰岛人之书》记载，一位名叫乌尔夫廖特的人前往挪威参照当地法律，约930年各地首领建立了全国性的大会。

阿尔庭每年夏天在后来称为辛格韦德利（意为“议会平原”）的裂谷中集会两周。由首领组成的立法会议制定和修改法律，法庭审理案件，选举产生的“法律宣讲人”每年在“法律岩”上背诵三分之一的法律。这里也是盛大的集市和社交场所。

它最著名的决定发生在约1000年，当时异教徒与基督徒两派势同水火，国家濒临分裂。阿里记载，本身是异教徒的法律宣讲人索尔盖尔裹着斗篷躺了一天一夜，然后裁定全体冰岛人受洗，同时暂时容许私下的异教崇拜。在挪威和丹麦国王统治下，阿尔庭失去权力，1800年被废除，1845年在雷克雅未克恢复。

summary.en: On 10 August 955 King Otto I, with Franconian, Bavarian, Swabian and Bohemian troops, routed a Hungarian army on the Lechfeld near Augsburg. The defeat ended half a century of Magyar raids into western Europe, raised Otto's prestige toward the imperial crown and helped steer the Hungarians toward a settled Christian kingdom.
summary.zh: 955年8月10日，国王奥托一世率领法兰克尼亚、巴伐利亚、施瓦本和波希米亚军队，在奥格斯堡附近的莱希菲尔德击溃匈牙利大军。这场失败终结了马扎尔人对西欧长达半个世纪的劫掠，提升了奥托问鼎帝位的威望，也促使匈牙利人走向定居的基督教王国。

sources.title: Widukind of Corvey, Deeds of the Saxons III.44–49
Gerhard of Augsburg, Life of St Ulrich

story.en:
For decades mounted Magyar raiders from the Carpathian Basin had struck deep into Germany, Italy and France. In summer 955 a large Hungarian force besieged Augsburg, whose bishop Ulrich directed the defence of its weak walls. King Otto I hurried south with Franconian, Bavarian and Swabian contingents and a Bohemian force; most Saxons were away fighting the Slavs. The chronicler Widukind of Corvey counts eight legions in all.

On 10 August, the feast of St Lawrence, the armies met on the Lech plain south of the city. Hungarian horsemen first fell on the Bohemians guarding the baggage, but Duke Conrad the Red, Otto's son-in-law and lately a rebel, counter-attacked and restored the line. Otto, bearing the Holy Lance, led the main charge, and the Hungarians broke. Many drowned or were hunted down in the following days, and their leaders Bulcsú and Lehel were hanged at Regensburg. Conrad, who had loosened his armour in the heat, was killed by an arrow in the throat.

Widukind says the victorious army hailed Otto as emperor on the field. The raids ceased, and within two generations Stephen I made Hungary a Christian kingdom.
story.zh:
数十年来，来自喀尔巴阡盆地的马扎尔骑兵深入德意志、意大利和法兰西劫掠。955年夏，一支庞大的匈牙利军队围攻奥格斯堡，主教乌尔里希指挥守军据守残破的城墙。国王奥托一世率法兰克尼亚、巴伐利亚、施瓦本兵马和一支波希米亚部队火速南下，萨克森人大多正与斯拉夫人作战而未能参战。据编年史家科维的维杜金德记载，全军共编为八个“军团”。

8月10日，即圣劳伦斯节，两军在城南的莱希平原相遇。匈牙利骑兵先袭击了守护辎重的波希米亚人，奥托的女婿、不久前还是叛臣的“红色”康拉德公爵发起反击，稳住了阵线。奥托手持圣矛率主力冲锋，匈牙利人全线崩溃。此后数日，许多人溺毙或遭追杀，首领布尔丘和莱赫尔在雷根斯堡被处绞刑。康拉德因天热松开铠甲，被一箭射中咽喉身亡。

维杜金德说，得胜的军队当场拥戴奥托为皇帝。马扎尔人的劫掠从此停止，不到两代人之后，伊什特万一世便把匈牙利建成了基督教王国。

summary.en: On 2 February 962 Pope John XII crowned the German king Otto I emperor in St Peter's, Rome, with his queen Adelaide as empress. The coronation revived the western empire of Charlemagne and bound the imperial title to the German crown in what became the Holy Roman Empire.
summary.zh: 962年2月2日，教宗约翰十二世在罗马圣彼得大教堂为德意志国王奥托一世加冕为皇帝，王后阿德尔海德同时加冕为皇后。这次加冕复兴了查理曼的西方帝国，使帝号与德意志王冠紧密相连，形成后来的神圣罗马帝国。

sources.title: Liudprand of Cremona, History of Otto (Historia Ottonis)

note: No separate Wikidata item for the coronation. Point at St Peter's Basilica.

story.en:
Otto I had been king of East Francia since 936, had crushed rebellions within his own family and, at the Lechfeld in 955, ended the Hungarian raids. In 951 he intervened in Italy, married Adelaide, the widowed queen of Italy, and took the Italian crown. When Pope John XII, threatened by King Berengar II of Italy, appealed for help, Otto crossed the Alps again in 961.

He was crowned in St Peter's on 2 February 962, the feast of the Purification. Eleven days later the privilege known as the Ottonianum confirmed the papacy's territorial claims, while requiring that each newly elected pope swear loyalty to the emperor's envoys before his consecration.

The partnership soon collapsed. John XII intrigued with Otto's enemies, and in 963 Otto returned, had a synod depose the pope and installed Leo VIII. From then on emperors regularly claimed a say in papal elections, a source of conflict that would erupt in the Investiture Controversy. The idea that the king of the Germans was by right emperor of the Romans endured until 1806.
story.zh:
奥托一世自936年起任东法兰克国王，平定了家族内部的多次叛乱，又在955年的莱希菲尔德之战中终结了匈牙利人的劫掠。951年他出兵意大利，娶了意大利王太后阿德尔海德，取得意大利王冠。教宗约翰十二世受到意大利国王贝伦加尔二世威胁，向他求援，奥托遂于961年再度翻越阿尔卑斯山。

962年2月2日圣母取洁节，他在圣彼得大教堂加冕。十一天后颁布的《奥托特权令》确认了教廷的领土要求，同时规定每位新当选的教宗在祝圣之前须向皇帝的使节宣誓效忠。

双方的合作很快破裂。约翰十二世与奥托的敌人暗中勾结，963年奥托重返罗马，召开宗教会议废黜教宗，另立利奥八世。此后皇帝经常要求插手教宗选举，这一矛盾后来在叙任权斗争中全面爆发。“德意志国王理应是罗马人的皇帝”这一观念一直延续到1806年。

summary.en: In January 1077 the excommunicated German king Henry IV stood for three days as a penitent at the gate of Countess Matilda's castle of Canossa until Pope Gregory VII absolved him. The scene became the defining image of the Investiture Controversy between papal and imperial power.
summary.zh: 1077年1月，被开除教籍的德意志国王亨利四世以忏悔者的身份在玛蒂尔达女伯爵的卡诺莎城堡门外站了三天，直到教宗格里高利七世为他解除绝罚。这一幕成为教权与皇权之间叙任权斗争最具代表性的画面。

sources.title: Gregory VII, letter to the German princes (Register IV.12, January 1077)

note: Henry IV was king, not yet emperor (crowned 1084). He waited at the gate 25–27 January and was absolved on 28 January 1077. Wikidata's item spans the wider 1076–1077 affair.

story.en:
The quarrel was over who should appoint bishops. Gregory VII, a forceful reformer, insisted that lay rulers must not invest clergy with their offices. Henry IV, who relied on bishops to govern Germany, refused to yield, and in January 1076 a synod of German bishops at Worms declared the pope deposed; Henry's letter addressed him as Hildebrand, now not pope but false monk. Gregory replied by excommunicating Henry and releasing his subjects from their oaths.

Rebellious princes threatened to choose a new king unless Henry was absolved within a year. In the harsh winter of 1076–77 he crossed the Alps with his wife and infant son and found Gregory at Canossa, the Apennine fortress of Matilda of Tuscany. For three days he stood at the gate barefoot and in penitent's wool, as Gregory himself reported, while Matilda and Abbot Hugh of Cluny, Henry's godfather, pleaded for him. On 28 January Gregory lifted the ban.

The peace did not last: Henry was excommunicated again in 1080, and the dispute was settled only by the Concordat of Worms in 1122. In 1872 Bismarck's vow that Germany would not go to Canossa showed how alive the episode remained.
story.zh:
争执的焦点是由谁任命主教。锐意改革的格里高利七世坚持世俗君主不得为教士授职，而依靠主教治理德意志的亨利四世拒不让步。1076年1月，德意志主教在沃尔姆斯召开宗教会议，宣布废黜教宗；亨利在信中称他为“希尔德布兰德，如今不是教宗，而是伪修士”。格里高利则开除亨利教籍，并解除其臣民的效忠誓言。

心怀不满的诸侯扬言，若亨利一年内得不到赦免，便另立新王。1076年至1077年的严冬，亨利带着妻子和年幼的儿子翻越阿尔卑斯山，在亚平宁山中托斯卡纳的玛蒂尔达的卡诺莎要塞找到了格里高利。据格里高利本人记述，亨利赤足、身穿忏悔者的粗毛衣在门外站了三天，玛蒂尔达和亨利的教父克吕尼修道院院长于格为他求情。1月28日，格里高利解除了绝罚。

和解并未持久：1080年亨利再次被开除教籍，直到1122年《沃尔姆斯宗教协定》争端才得以解决。1872年俾斯麦誓言德国“不去卡诺莎”，可见这一事件的影响历久不衰。

name.zh: 阿方索六世攻取托莱多

summary.en: Alfonso VI of León and Castile took Toledo, the old Visigothic capital, after its taifa ruler al-Qadir surrendered. The first great Muslim city of Iberia to fall to the Christian kingdoms, its loss alarmed the other taifa kings into calling in the Almoravids, and Toledo became a meeting place of Arabic and Latin learning.
summary.zh: 莱昂和卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索六世在托莱多泰法国统治者卡迪尔投降后，占领了这座西哥特旧都。这是伊比利亚第一座落入基督教王国之手的穆斯林大城，其失陷令其他泰法诸王惊恐，转而向穆拉比特王朝求援；托莱多此后成为阿拉伯学术与拉丁学术交汇之地。

sources.title: B. F. Reilly, The Kingdom of León-Castilla under King Alfonso VI, 1065–1109 (1988)

note: Surrender terms are dated 6 May and Alfonso's formal entry 25 May 1085 (Julian calendar, as in the other pre-1582 records). Strictly Alfonso was king of León and Castile; the Crown of Castile in the narrow sense dates from 1230.

summary.en: At Gloucester at Christmas 1085 William the Conqueror ordered a survey of his English kingdom. Commissioners recorded who held each estate, its people, ploughs and livestock, and its value in 1066 and 1086. The results, compiled in 1086, form Domesday Book, the most complete record of any realm in medieval Europe.
summary.zh: 1085年圣诞节，征服者威廉在格洛斯特下令对英格兰王国进行普查。调查官逐一记录每处地产的持有人、人口、犁队和牲畜，以及1066年和1086年的价值。1086年汇编成的结果即《末日审判书》，是中世纪欧洲任何王国中最完整的记录。

sources.title: Richard FitzNigel, Dialogue of the Exchequer (c. 1179), I.16

note: QID is the book. Point at Winchester, where the returns were compiled and the book was kept in the royal treasury; it is now at The National Archives, Kew. The name Domesday is first attested in the 12th century.

summary.en: Pope Calixtus II and Emperor Henry V ended the Investiture Controversy with a compromise: the emperor gave up investing bishops with ring and staff, the symbols of spiritual office, and allowed free canonical elections, while keeping the right to grant them their lands and secular powers with the sceptre.
summary.zh: 教宗加里斯都二世与皇帝亨利五世以妥协结束了叙任权斗争：皇帝放弃以象征神职的权戒和权杖为主教授职，允许依教会法自由选举，但保留以权标授予主教领地和世俗权力的权利。

sources.title: U.-R. Blumenthal, The Investiture Controversy: Church and Monarchy from the Ninth to the Twelfth Century (1988)

note: Agreed on 23 September 1122 outside the walls of Worms.

summary.en: On 29 May 1176 the infantry of the Lombard League, rallying around Milan's carroccio war-wagon, withstood and then routed Frederick Barbarossa's knights near Legnano. The defeat pushed the emperor into peace with Pope Alexander III at Venice in 1177 and recognition of the cities' self-government at Constance in 1183.
summary.zh: 1176年5月29日，伦巴第联盟的步兵在莱尼亚诺附近围绕米兰的战车“卡罗乔”坚守阵地，继而击溃腓特烈一世（红胡子）的骑士。这次失败迫使皇帝于1177年在威尼斯与教宗亚历山大三世议和，并于1183年在康斯坦茨承认各城市的自治。

sources.title: J. B. Freed, Frederick Barbarossa: The Prince and the Myth (2016)

note: The hero Alberto da Giussano and his Company of Death are later legend (first recorded in the 14th century).

summary.en: Pope Innocent III proclaimed a crusade against the Cathar heretics of Languedoc and the lords who sheltered them. Northern French barons under Simon de Montfort, and later the French crown, waged two decades of war that devastated the south, broke the counts of Toulouse and brought Languedoc under the king of France.
summary.zh: 教宗英诺森三世号召十字军讨伐朗格多克的卡特里派异端及庇护他们的领主。以西蒙·德·蒙福尔为首的法国北方贵族以及后来的法国王室进行了二十年战争，使南方饱受摧残，图卢兹伯爵的势力瓦解，朗格多克归于法国国王治下。

label.en: Battle of Muret: Peter II of Aragon killed
label.zh: 米雷之战：阿拉贡国王佩德罗二世阵亡

label.en: Simon de Montfort killed besieging Toulouse
label.zh: 西蒙·德·蒙福尔围攻图卢兹时阵亡
路易八世围攻阿维尼翁

label.en: Treaty of Paris; Raymond VII's penance at Notre-Dame
label.zh: 《巴黎条约》；雷蒙七世在巴黎圣母院悔罪

sources.title: Peter of Les Vaux-de-Cernay, Historia Albigensis

note: Point at Béziers, the opening massacre of July 1209.

story.en:
Catharism, a dualist faith that rejected the Catholic Church and its sacraments, had spread widely in the lands of the count of Toulouse. After years of fruitless preaching, the papal legate Peter of Castelnau was murdered in January 1208, apparently by one of Count Raymond VI's men, and Innocent III called for a crusade.

The crusaders opened their campaign at Béziers on 22 July 1209, where much of the population was slaughtered. The monk Caesarius of Heisterbach later claimed that the legate Arnaud Amalric, asked how to tell Catholics from heretics, replied that they should kill them all because God would know his own; most historians doubt he said it. Carcassonne surrendered weeks later, and Simon de Montfort was chosen to lead the crusade.

At Muret in 1213 Montfort defeated and killed King Peter II of Aragon, ending Aragonese hopes north of the Pyrenees. Montfort himself died besieging Toulouse in 1218, struck by a stone from a siege engine. Louis VIII's royal crusade of 1226 finished the work, and the Treaty of Paris in 1229 bound Raymond VII's lands to the French crown. The Inquisition, created to hunt surviving Cathars, outlasted them.
story.zh:
卡特里派是一种二元论信仰，否定天主教会及其圣事，在图卢兹伯爵的领地上广为流传。多年布道毫无成效之后，1208年1月教宗使节卡斯泰尔诺的彼得遇刺，凶手似乎是伯爵雷蒙六世的部下，英诺森三世随即号召十字军。

1209年7月22日，十字军在贝济耶揭开战幕，城中大批居民遭屠杀。修士海斯特巴赫的凯撒里乌斯后来声称，有人问教宗使节阿尔诺·阿莫里如何分辨天主教徒和异端，他回答说统统杀掉，上帝自会认得自己的人；多数史家怀疑他是否说过此话。几周后卡尔卡松投降，西蒙·德·蒙福尔被推举为十字军首领。

1213年，蒙福尔在米雷击败并杀死阿拉贡国王佩德罗二世，断绝了阿拉贡在比利牛斯山以北的野心。1218年蒙福尔在围攻图卢兹时被投石机抛出的石块击中身亡。1226年路易八世亲率王家十字军收拾残局，1229年《巴黎条约》将雷蒙七世的领地与法国王室绑在一起。为追查残余卡特里派而设立的宗教裁判所，比卡特里派存在得更久。

name.en: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
name.zh: 拉斯纳瓦斯-德托洛萨会战

summary.en: On 16 July 1212 the allied kings of Castile, Aragon and Navarre crushed the Almohad caliph Muhammad al-Nasir in the Sierra Morena. The victory broke Almohad power in Iberia and opened Andalusia to the Castilian conquests of Córdoba in 1236 and Seville in 1248.
summary.zh: 1212年7月16日，卡斯蒂利亚、阿拉贡和纳瓦拉三国国王联军在莫雷纳山脉大败穆瓦希德王朝哈里发穆罕默德·纳西尔。这场胜利摧毁了穆瓦希德王朝在伊比利亚的势力，为卡斯蒂利亚1236年攻取科尔多瓦、1248年攻取塞维利亚打开了安达卢西亚的大门。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Britannica: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Rodrigo Jiménez de Rada, De rebus Hispaniae VIII
J. F. O'Callaghan, Reconquest and Crusade in Medieval Spain (2003)

note: Castile here means the kingdom of Alfonso VIII; the Crown of Castile in the narrow sense dates from 1230.

story.en:
In 1195 the Almohads had routed Alfonso VIII of Castile at Alarcos. Seeking revenge, Alfonso obtained crusade privileges from Pope Innocent III, and in June 1212 an army of Castilians, Aragonese under Peter II, Navarrese under Sancho VII, the military orders and many foreign crusaders marched south from Toledo. Most of the crusaders from beyond the Pyrenees went home before the battle, worn down by the heat and quarrels over plunder.

The Almohad army under Muhammad al-Nasir held the main pass through the Sierra Morena. According to the Christian chroniclers, a local shepherd showed the allies another path, letting them reach the plain of Las Navas de Tolosa unexpectedly; the story cannot be verified. On 16 July the Christians attacked in three divisions, and after hours of fighting a final charge led by the kings broke into the caliph's fortified camp. Navarrese tradition holds that the chains in its coat of arms recall Sancho's breakthrough there. Al-Nasir fled to Jaén and later to Marrakesh.

Almohad authority in al-Andalus crumbled within two decades. Ferdinand III of Castile took Córdoba in 1236 and Seville in 1248, leaving only the emirate of Granada under Muslim rule.
story.zh:
1195年，穆瓦希德军队在阿拉尔科斯大败卡斯蒂利亚国王阿方索八世。为雪前耻，阿方索从教宗英诺森三世那里获得十字军特权。1212年6月，由卡斯蒂利亚人、佩德罗二世率领的阿拉贡人、桑乔七世率领的纳瓦拉人、各骑士团以及大批外国十字军组成的大军从托莱多南下。来自比利牛斯山以北的十字军大多因酷暑和争夺战利品而在决战前返乡。

穆罕默德·纳西尔率领的穆瓦希德军扼守莫雷纳山脉的主要隘口。据基督教编年史家记载，一位当地牧羊人为联军指出了另一条小路，使他们出其不意地抵达拉斯纳瓦斯-德托洛萨平原，但这一说法无从查证。7月16日，基督徒分三路进攻，激战数小时后，诸王亲率的最后冲锋攻入了哈里发设防的营地。纳瓦拉的传统说，其纹章上的锁链正是纪念桑乔在此的突破。纳西尔逃往哈恩，后又退回马拉喀什。

不到二十年，穆瓦希德王朝在安达卢斯的统治便土崩瓦解。卡斯蒂利亚国王费尔南多三世于1236年攻取科尔多瓦，1248年攻取塞维利亚，此后只剩格拉纳达埃米尔国仍在穆斯林统治之下。

summary.en: From 1309, when Clement V settled at Avignon, to 1377, when Gregory XI returned to Rome, seven successive popes resided on the Rhône under strong French influence. They built a formidable bureaucracy and palace there, but critics such as Petrarch called the era a Babylonian captivity of the church.
summary.zh: 自1309年克雷芒五世定居阿维尼翁，到1377年格里高利十一世返回罗马，先后七位教宗在法国强大影响下驻跸罗讷河畔。他们在那里建立了高效的教廷机构和宏伟的宫殿，但彼特拉克等批评者称这一时期为教会的“巴比伦之囚”。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre: Historic Centre of Avignon

note: Point at the Palace of the Popes. Avignon belonged to the Angevin counts of Provence until Clement VI bought it in 1348.

story.en:
Bertrand de Got, archbishop of Bordeaux, was elected pope as Clement V in 1305 under heavy pressure from Philip IV of France, whose agents had humiliated Boniface VIII at Anagni two years earlier. Rome was torn by baronial feuds, so Clement stayed north of the Alps and in 1309 settled at Avignon, a town of the Angevin counts of Provence beside the papal Comtat Venaissin.

His successors, all French, stayed too. Benedict XII and Clement VI raised the immense Palace of the Popes, and in 1348 Clement VI bought the town from Queen Joanna I of Naples. The Avignon curia became one of the most efficient governments in Europe, refining papal taxation and appointments. Its luxury appalled critics: Petrarch, who lived nearby, likened the city to Babylon, and the phrase Babylonian captivity stuck.

Mystics such as Bridget of Sweden and Catherine of Siena urged a return. Urban V went back briefly in 1367, and Gregory XI re-entered Rome in January 1377. After his death in 1378 a disputed election produced rival popes in Rome and Avignon, the Western Schism that lasted until 1417.
story.zh:
1305年，在法国国王腓力四世的强大压力下，波尔多大主教贝特朗·德·戈当选教宗，称克雷芒五世；两年前，腓力四世的手下刚在阿纳尼羞辱过卜尼法斯八世。罗马城内贵族纷争不断，克雷芒便留在阿尔卑斯山以北，1309年定居阿维尼翁。这座城当时属于普罗旺斯的安茹伯爵，毗邻教廷领地孔塔-弗内桑。

他的继任者全是法国人，也都留了下来。本笃十二世和克雷芒六世修建了宏伟的教皇宫，1348年克雷芒六世又从那不勒斯女王乔万娜一世手中买下了这座城。阿维尼翁教廷成为欧洲效率最高的政府之一，完善了教廷税收和圣职任命制度。其奢华令批评者愤慨：住在附近的彼特拉克把这座城比作巴比伦，“巴比伦之囚”的说法由此流传开来。

瑞典的比吉塔和锡耶纳的加大利纳等神秘主义者力劝教宗回归。乌尔班五世曾于1367年短暂返回罗马，格里高利十一世则在1377年1月重返罗马。1378年他去世后，一次有争议的选举造成罗马与阿维尼翁两位教宗对立，即持续到1417年的西方教会大分裂。

summary.en: Torrential rain from spring 1315 ruined harvests across northern Europe, from Ireland to Poland, for three years running. Grain prices soared, livestock died, and millions perished from hunger and disease; in Flemish Ypres perhaps a tenth of the townspeople died in 1316 alone. It was the worst famine of the European Middle Ages.
summary.zh: 自1315年春起，连绵暴雨使从爱尔兰到波兰的北欧各地连续三年颗粒歉收。粮价飞涨，牲畜死亡，数以百万计的人死于饥饿和疾病；仅1316年，佛兰德的伊普尔或许就有十分之一的市民死亡。这是欧洲中世纪最严重的饥荒。

sources.title: W. C. Jordan, The Great Famine: Northern Europe in the Early Fourteenth Century (1996)

note: A Europe-wide disaster; the point is placed at Ypres, whose municipal burial accounts are among the best records of its toll. Some historians extend the crisis to 1322 because of cattle plague that followed.

summary.en: On 26 August 1346 Edward III's outnumbered English army, with massed longbowmen and dismounted men-at-arms, destroyed Philip VI's French host in Ponthieu. Among the dead was the blind King John of Bohemia. The victory let Edward besiege and take Calais, which England held until 1558.
summary.zh: 1346年8月26日，爱德华三世以寡敌众，凭借成群的长弓手和下马作战的重装武士，在蓬蒂厄摧毁了腓力六世的法军。阵亡者中有双目失明的波希米亚国王约翰。此役胜利使爱德华得以围攻并夺取加来，英格兰一直占据该城至1558年。

sources.title: J. Sumption, The Hundred Years War I: Trial by Battle (1990)

story.en:
In July 1346 Edward III landed in Normandy, sacked Caen and marched toward Paris before turning north, pursued by a much larger French army under Philip VI. After forcing a crossing of the Somme at the ford of Blanchetaque, Edward chose a slope near Crécy-en-Ponthieu and waited, his knights dismounted beside the archers.

The French arrived late on 26 August and attacked without proper order. Genoese crossbowmen went forward first; Froissart says a shower had wet their strings, and they were shot down by the longbowmen's faster volleys. French knights rode through their own retreating crossbowmen and charged up the slope again and again into the arrows until nightfall. Edward's sixteen-year-old son, later called the Black Prince, fought in the front line; Froissart says that when his division was hard pressed the king refused to send help, so that the boy might win his spurs. The blind King John of Bohemia had his knights tie their horses to his and lead him into the fight, where he was killed.

Edward then besieged Calais, which fell in 1347 and stayed English for two centuries.
story.zh:
1346年7月，爱德华三世在诺曼底登陆，洗劫卡昂，向巴黎进军后又转而北上，身后是腓力六世率领的规模大得多的法军。强渡索姆河上的布朗什塔克浅滩之后，爱德华在克雷西-昂蓬蒂厄附近选定一处山坡严阵以待，让骑士下马与弓箭手并肩列阵。

8月26日傍晚法军赶到，未及整队便发起进攻。热那亚弩手打头阵；傅华萨说一场阵雨打湿了他们的弓弦，他们在长弓手更快的连射下纷纷倒地。法国骑士从后撤的弩手中间冲过，一次又一次冲上山坡，迎着箭雨冲杀，直到天黑。爱德华十六岁的儿子，即后来的“黑太子”，在最前线作战；据傅华萨记载，他所在的部队陷入苦战时，国王拒绝增援，好让这孩子凭自己的战功赢得骑士马刺。双目失明的波希米亚国王约翰让骑士们把马和他的马拴在一起，领他冲入战阵，最终战死。

随后爱德华围攻加来，该城于1347年陷落，此后两个世纪一直归英格兰所有。

summary.en: The Hanse grew out of 12th- and 13th-century associations of German merchants trading across the Baltic and North Sea. The first general diet of its towns met at Lübeck in 1356, giving shape to a league of up to some 200 towns that dominated northern European trade until its last diet in 1669.
summary.zh: 汉萨同盟起源于12至13世纪在波罗的海和北海经商的德意志商人团体。1356年其成员城市在吕贝克召开第一次全体大会，同盟由此成形，鼎盛时联合了约两百座城市，主宰北欧贸易，直到1669年召开最后一次大会。

note: The League had no founding act; 1356, the first general diet (Hansetag) at Lübeck, is a conventional starting point, with roots in the 12th–13th centuries (Wikidata gives 1358 as inception). End year is the last diet, 1669. Point at Lübeck town hall.

story.en:
