The Hanse began not as a state but as a set of merchant fellowships. After Henry the Lion refounded Lübeck in 1159, German traders used it as a gateway to the Baltic, meeting at Visby on Gotland and pushing east to Novgorod. Their great foreign offices, the Kontore, stood at Novgorod, Bergen, Bruges and London, where the walled Steelyard on the Thames enjoyed privileges for centuries.

From the thirteenth century towns such as Lübeck and Hamburg made pacts to protect their merchants, and in 1356 delegates met at Lübeck in the first general Hanseatic diet. The League had no army, treasury or charter of its own; it worked through trade embargoes and, when needed, joint war fleets. Its greatest success came after King Valdemar IV of Denmark sacked Visby in 1361: in the Peace of Stralsund of 1370 Denmark had to hand the towns fortresses on the Scanian coast.

Herring, grain, furs, wax, timber and cloth passed through its ports. Territorial states, Dutch competition and the shift of trade to the Atlantic slowly eroded it; only nine towns sent delegates to the last diet in 1669, and Lübeck, Hamburg and Bremen still call themselves Hanseatic cities.
story.zh:
汉萨最初并非国家，而是一些商人团体。1159年“狮子”亨利重建吕贝克后，德意志商人以此为通往波罗的海的门户，在哥得兰岛的维斯比聚会，并向东远至诺夫哥罗德。他们在海外设立的大商站分布于诺夫哥罗德、卑尔根、布鲁日和伦敦；伦敦泰晤士河畔有围墙环绕的“钢院”，享有特权长达数百年。

13世纪起，吕贝克、汉堡等城市订立盟约保护本城商人。1356年各城代表在吕贝克召开第一次汉萨全体大会。同盟没有自己的军队、国库或章程，靠贸易禁运以及必要时组建的联合舰队行事。它最大的胜利出现在丹麦国王瓦尔德马四世1361年洗劫维斯比之后：1370年的《施特拉尔松德和约》迫使丹麦把斯堪尼亚沿岸的要塞交给汉萨城市。

鲱鱼、谷物、毛皮、蜂蜡、木材和呢绒经由它的港口流通。领土国家的兴起、荷兰人的竞争以及贸易重心移向大西洋，使同盟逐渐衰落；1669年最后一次大会只有九座城市派出代表。吕贝克、汉堡和不来梅至今仍自称“汉萨城市”。

summary.en: Provoked by a third poll tax, peasants and artisans of Essex and Kent rose in 1381 and marched on London, where they burned John of Gaunt's Savoy Palace and killed the archbishop of Canterbury. The fourteen-year-old Richard II faced them; Wat Tyler was killed at Smithfield and the revolt was crushed.
summary.zh: 1381年，因第三次人头税而激愤的埃塞克斯和肯特农民与工匠揭竿而起，进军伦敦，焚毁冈特的约翰的萨伏伊宫，并杀死坎特伯雷大主教。年仅十四岁的理查二世亲自面对起义者；瓦特·泰勒在史密斯菲尔德被杀，起义遭到镇压。

sources.title: R. B. Dobson (ed.), The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 (2nd ed., 1983)

note: Date is the outbreak at Brentwood, Essex (30 May 1381); point at Smithfield, London, where the rising effectively ended on 15 June.

story.en:
The Black Death had made labour scarce, and lords and Parliament tried to hold down wages and enforce old services. A third poll tax, levied in 1380 at a shilling a head, bore hardest on the poor. On 30 May 1381 villagers at Brentwood in Essex drove off a tax commissioner, and within days much of Essex and Kent was in arms. The Kentish rebels chose Wat Tyler as leader and freed the radical priest John Ball from prison in Maidstone. Ball preached on the old rhyme asking who was then the gentleman when Adam delved and Eve span.

On 13 June the rebels entered London and burned the Savoy, John of Gaunt's palace. Next day, while Richard II met one band at Mile End and promised to end serfdom, others stormed the Tower and beheaded Archbishop Simon Sudbury, the chancellor, and Robert Hales, the treasurer.

On 15 June at Smithfield the mayor, William Walworth, struck Tyler down during a parley. Richard rode forward, told the rebels he would be their leader, and led them away. His promises were soon revoked and the leaders executed, but no further poll tax was tried in medieval England.
story.zh:
黑死病之后劳动力奇缺，领主和议会却竭力压低工资、强制恢复旧有劳役。1380年开征的第三次人头税按每人一先令征收，对穷人负担最重。1381年5月30日，埃塞克斯布伦特伍德的村民赶走了一名征税官，数日之内埃塞克斯和肯特大部分地区便燃起烽火。肯特起义者推举瓦特·泰勒为首领，并从梅德斯通的监狱中救出激进神父约翰·鲍尔。鲍尔借一句古老的歌谣布道：“亚当耕田夏娃织布时，谁又是绅士？”

6月13日，起义者进入伦敦，焚毁了冈特的约翰的萨伏伊宫。次日，理查二世在迈尔恩德会见一支起义队伍，许诺废除农奴制；与此同时，另一些人攻入伦敦塔，将身兼大法官的大主教西蒙·萨德伯里和财政大臣罗伯特·黑尔斯斩首。

6月15日在史密斯菲尔德谈判时，伦敦市长威廉·沃尔沃思将泰勒击倒。理查策马上前，对起义者说他愿做他们的首领，把人群带离了现场。他的承诺很快被收回，起义领袖遭到处决，但中世纪英格兰此后再未尝试征收人头税。

summary.en: On 25 October 1415, St Crispin's Day, Henry V's small, weary and sick English army defeated a much larger French force between the woods of Agincourt and Tramecourt. Heavily armoured French knights floundered in the mud under longbow fire; the slaughter of the French nobility opened the way to Henry's conquest of Normandy.
summary.zh: 1415年10月25日圣克里斯宾节，亨利五世疲惫且疫病缠身的小股英军，在阿金库尔与特拉姆库尔两片树林之间击败了数量多得多的法军。身披重甲的法国骑士在长弓箭雨下深陷泥泞；法国贵族遭到重创，为亨利征服诺曼底铺平了道路。

sources.title: A. Curry, Agincourt: A New History (2005)

note: The size of both armies is debated; Curry argues the French advantage was smaller than traditionally claimed.

name.zh: 布鲁内莱斯基设计的佛罗伦萨大教堂穹顶

summary.en: Between 1420 and 1436 Filippo Brunelleschi raised the dome of Florence Cathedral, still the largest masonry dome in the world, over an octagon about 43 metres across without the timber centring builders had thought indispensable. Its consecration by Pope Eugenius IV in 1436 announced the architecture of the Renaissance.
summary.zh: 1420年至1436年，菲利波·布鲁内莱斯基在直径约43米的八角形结构上建起佛罗伦萨大教堂的穹顶，而且没有使用当时被认为必不可少的木制拱架。这至今仍是世界上最大的砖石穹顶。1436年教宗尤金四世为大教堂祝圣，宣告了文艺复兴建筑的到来。

sources.title: Opera di Santa Maria del Fiore: Brunelleschi's Dome

note: QID is the dome itself. Construction began in August 1420; the cathedral was consecrated on 25 March 1436, and the lantern was built from 1446 to 1461.

story.en:
Florence's cathedral, begun in 1296, had for decades a vast octagonal crossing that no one knew how to roof. The city had committed itself to a dome without external buttresses, wider than anything built since antiquity, and no forest could supply timber for the usual wooden centring.

In 1418 the wool guild that ran the works held a competition. Brunelleschi, a goldsmith turned architect who had studied the ruins of Rome, proposed to build without centring. Vasari later told how he won by challenging rivals to stand an egg on end and then cracking its base on the marble; the anecdote is probably invented. In 1420 he and his rival Lorenzo Ghiberti were made joint supervisors, though Brunelleschi soon dominated.

His solution was a double shell of brick, laid in herringbone courses that locked each ring as it rose and bound by chains of stone, iron and wood. He devised an ox-driven hoist with a reversing gear to lift the materials. Pope Eugenius IV consecrated the cathedral on 25 March 1436. The marble lantern on top, also to Brunelleschi's design, was begun only in the year of his death, 1446.
story.zh:
佛罗伦萨大教堂始建于1296年，其巨大的八角形十字交叉部数十年间一直无人知道如何封顶。该城早已决定建造一座不用外部扶壁的穹顶，其跨度超过古代以来的任何建筑，而且没有哪片森林能提供足够木材搭建通常所需的木制拱架。

1418年，负责工程的羊毛行会举办设计竞赛。曾研究过罗马古迹、由金匠转行为建筑师的布鲁内莱斯基提出不用拱架施工。瓦萨里后来讲述，他向对手们挑战让鸡蛋竖立，然后把蛋的底部在大理石上磕破，从而胜出；这则轶事很可能是杜撰的。1420年，他与对手洛伦佐·吉贝尔蒂被同时任命为工程总监，但很快便由布鲁内莱斯基主导。

他的方案是双层砖砌穹壳，以人字形砌法使每一圈砖在升高时相互咬合，并用石、铁、木制成的拉环加固。他还设计了一种带换向装置、由牛驱动的起重机来吊运材料。1436年3月25日，教宗尤金四世为大教堂祝圣。顶端同样由布鲁内莱斯基设计的大理石采光亭，直到他去世的1446年才开始建造。

summary.en: From October 1428 the English besieged Orléans, the key to France south of the Loire. In late April 1429 Joan of Arc entered the city with a relief convoy; within ten days the French stormed the main English forts, and on 8 May the besiegers withdrew. The victory revived Charles VII's cause and led to his coronation at Reims.
summary.zh: 1428年10月起，英军围攻卢瓦尔河以南法国的门户奥尔良。1429年4月底，贞德随援军车队进入城内；十天之内，法军攻克英军主要堡垒，5月8日围城者撤退。这次胜利重振了查理七世的事业，促成他在兰斯加冕。

sources.title: J. Sumption, The Hundred Years War IV: Cursed Kings (2015)

note: Siege conventionally dated 12 October 1428 to 8 May 1429 (Wikidata gives 21 October 1428 to 17 May 1429).

story.en:
By 1428 English and Burgundian forces held Paris and northern France, and the uncrowned Charles VII ruled a shrinking realm from Bourges. In October the earl of Salisbury laid siege to Orléans on the Loire; within weeks he was mortally wounded by a cannon shot while surveying the city from the captured fort of Les Tourelles. The English ringed the city with forts but never closed it completely, and in February 1429 they beat off a French attack on a supply convoy in the so-called Battle of the Herrings.

That spring Joan, a peasant girl from Domrémy who said the voices of saints had sent her to save France, persuaded Charles to let her join a relief army. She entered Orléans on 29 April. In early May the French took the forts of Saint-Loup and the Augustins, and on 7 May they stormed Les Tourelles at the bridgehead; Joan was struck by an arrow between neck and shoulder but returned to the fight. The next day the English drew up for battle, then marched away.

Orléans still celebrates its deliverance every May. In July Joan stood beside Charles VII at his coronation in Reims.
story.zh:
到1428年，英格兰和勃艮第军队已占据巴黎和法国北部，尚未加冕的查理七世在布尔日统治着日益缩小的领土。10月，索尔兹伯里伯爵率军围攻卢瓦尔河畔的奥尔良；数周后，他在已攻占的图雷勒堡观察城防时被炮弹击成重伤而死。英军在城外修筑了一圈堡垒，却始终未能完全封锁；1429年2月，他们击退了法军对一支补给车队的袭击，即所谓“鲱鱼之战”。

那年春天，来自栋雷米的农家少女贞德自称受圣徒的声音差遣来拯救法国，说服查理让她随援军出征。4月29日她进入奥尔良。5月初，法军先后攻克圣卢堡和奥古斯丁堡，7日又强攻桥头的图雷勒堡；贞德被一箭射中颈肩之间，但包扎后重返战场。次日，英军列阵后撤军离去。

奥尔良至今每年5月都庆祝解围。同年7月，贞德站在查理七世身旁，见证了他在兰斯的加冕。

name.en: Michelangelo paints the Sistine Chapel ceiling
name.zh: 米开朗琪罗绘制西斯廷礼拜堂天顶画

summary.en: Commissioned by Pope Julius II, Michelangelo painted the vault of the Sistine Chapel between 1508 and 1512, covering some 500 square metres with scenes from Genesis, prophets, sibyls and the ancestors of Christ. Unveiled on 31 October 1512, it became one of the defining works of High Renaissance art.
summary.zh: 受教宗尤利乌斯二世委托，米开朗琪罗于1508年至1512年绘制西斯廷礼拜堂的拱顶，在约500平方米的面积上描绘了《创世记》场景、先知、女预言家和基督的先祖。天顶画于1512年10月31日揭幕，成为文艺复兴盛期艺术的代表作之一。

sources.title: Giorgio Vasari, Lives of the Artists: Michelangelo (1568)
R. King, Michelangelo and the Pope's Ceiling (2003)

note: QID is the fresco cycle.

story.en:
Julius II, the warrior pope, wanted the plain starry vault of the chapel built by his uncle Sixtus IV replaced. He gave the task to Michelangelo, who thought of himself as a sculptor and was then working on the pope's tomb. The first plan was for twelve apostles; Michelangelo later recalled that he persuaded Julius to let him paint something far grander.

From 1508 he worked on a scaffold of his own design, bridging the chapel at the height of the windows so that services could continue below. He painted standing and craning backwards, not lying down as legend has it; in a comic sonnet he complained that his beard pointed to heaven and paint dripped on his face. Assistants ground pigments and helped with early scenes, but most of the painting is his own.

The nine central panels run from God separating light from darkness to the drunkenness of Noah, with the Creation of Adam near the middle. When the first half was unveiled in 1511, the young Raphael is said to have changed his style. The finished vault was revealed on 31 October 1512, a few months before Julius died.
story.zh:
“战神教宗”尤利乌斯二世希望更换其叔父西克斯图斯四世所建礼拜堂那朴素的星空拱顶。他把这项工作交给了米开朗琪罗，而米开朗琪罗自认为是雕塑家，当时正在为教宗建造陵墓。最初的方案是画十二使徒；据米开朗琪罗后来回忆，是他说服尤利乌斯让他画一幅宏大得多的作品。

从1508年起，他在自己设计的脚手架上工作，脚手架在窗户高度横跨礼拜堂，下方的礼拜可以照常进行。他是站着仰身作画，并非传说中的躺着；他在一首诙谐的十四行诗里抱怨自己胡子朝天，颜料滴得满脸都是。助手们研磨颜料，也参与了早期几幅场景，但大部分画面出自他本人之手。

中央九幅画面从“上帝分开光暗”一直到“挪亚醉酒”，《创造亚当》位于中部附近。1511年前半部分揭幕时，据说年轻的拉斐尔因此改变了画风。完成的天顶画于1512年10月31日揭幕，几个月后尤利乌斯便去世了。

summary.en: On 6 May 1527 unpaid, mutinous troops of Emperor Charles V, Spanish, German and Italian, stormed Rome after Pope Clement VII joined the League of Cognac against him. For weeks they looted, killed and held the city to ransom while Clement was besieged in Castel Sant'Angelo; the sack shocked Europe and ended Rome's Renaissance heyday.
summary.zh: 1527年5月6日，在教宗克雷芒七世加入反对查理五世的科尼亚克同盟之后，这位皇帝麾下由西班牙人、德意志人和意大利人组成、欠饷哗变的军队攻入罗马。此后数周，他们烧杀抢掠，勒索赎金，克雷芒则被围困在圣天使堡中。这场浩劫震惊欧洲，也终结了罗马文艺复兴的鼎盛时代。

sources.title: J. Hook, The Sack of Rome, 1527 (2nd ed., 2004)

note: Point at the Borgo walls near the Vatican, where the assault broke in.

story.en:
In 1526 Pope Clement VII, a Medici, joined France, Venice, Florence and Milan in the League of Cognac against Charles V. The emperor's army in northern Italy, long unpaid, grew mutinous. Charles, duke of Bourbon, a French prince who had gone over to the emperor, led it south toward Rome, with thousands of German Landsknechte, many of them Lutheran in sympathy, alongside Spanish and Italian troops.

On 6 May the attackers scaled the walls near the Vatican in morning fog. Bourbon was shot dead on a ladder; the goldsmith Benvenuto Cellini later boasted that he had fired the shot. Most of the Swiss Guard died covering the pope's flight along the raised corridor to Castel Sant'Angelo, a sacrifice still remembered each 6 May when new guards are sworn in. Without a commander the troops ran amok for weeks, killing, torturing for ransom and desecrating churches, and plague and famine added to the toll.

Clement surrendered in June and remained a prisoner until December. Weakened, he could not grant Henry VIII an annulment of his marriage to Catherine of Aragon, Charles's aunt, and in 1530 he crowned Charles emperor at Bologna.
story.zh:
1526年，出身美第奇家族的教宗克雷芒七世与法国、威尼斯、佛罗伦萨和米兰结成科尼亚克同盟，共同对抗查理五世。皇帝驻意大利北部的军队长期欠饷，军心哗变。投靠皇帝的法国亲王波旁公爵查理率领这支军队南下罗马，其中有数千名德意志雇佣兵，许多人同情路德派，另有西班牙和意大利部队。

5月6日清晨，进攻者趁雾在梵蒂冈附近攀上城墙。波旁公爵在云梯上中弹身亡，金匠本韦努托·切利尼后来夸口说那一枪是他开的。瑞士近卫队大部分战死，掩护教宗经高架通道逃入圣天使堡；如今每年5月6日新卫兵宣誓时仍纪念这一壮举。群龙无首的士兵连续数周肆意妄为，杀人、拷打勒赎、亵渎教堂，瘟疫和饥荒又使死亡人数进一步上升。

克雷芒于6月投降，被囚禁到12月。元气大伤的他无法批准亨利八世与查理的姨母阿拉贡的凯瑟琳解除婚姻；1530年，他在博洛尼亚为查理加冕为皇帝。

summary.en: In November 1534 Parliament confirmed Henry VIII and his successors as the only supreme head on earth of the Church of England, completing the break with Rome after the pope refused to annul his first marriage. Refusing to accept the new order cost Thomas More and Bishop John Fisher their lives in 1535.
summary.zh: 1534年11月，议会确认亨利八世及其继承人为英格兰教会在尘世唯一的最高首脑，在教宗拒绝宣告其第一次婚姻无效之后，彻底完成了与罗马的决裂。托马斯·莫尔和约翰·费希尔主教因拒不接受这一新秩序，于1535年被处死。

sources.title: G. R. Elton, Reform and Reformation: England 1509–1558 (1977)

note: QID Q392226 covers both the 1534 Act and Elizabeth I's Act of 1559; no separate item for 1534 was found. Point at the Palace of Westminster. The act was repealed under Mary I in 1554.

summary.en: Meeting at Trent in three periods between 1545 and 1563, the Catholic Church's nineteenth ecumenical council answered the Protestant Reformation. It defined doctrine on scripture, justification and the seven sacraments and ordered reforms such as seminaries for priests and resident bishops, shaping Catholicism for four centuries.
summary.zh: 天主教会第十九次大公会议于1545年至1563年分三期在特伦托举行，以回应新教宗教改革。会议就圣经、称义和七件圣事确立教义，并下令推行改革，如设立修院培养神父、要求主教驻守教区，塑造了此后四百年的天主教。

sources.title: H. Jedin, A History of the Council of Trent (1957–61)
J. W. O'Malley, Trent: What Happened at the Council (2013)

note: Opened 13 December 1545 and closed 4 December 1563. Point at Trento cathedral (San Vigilio), where the sessions were held; Trent was an imperial prince-bishopric.

story.en:
Luther and others had long called for a general council, and Emperor Charles V pressed for one that might heal the split in Germany. Popes, wary of councils that claimed authority over them, delayed until Paul III finally opened one at Trent, an imperial city just south of the Alps, in December 1545. Attendance was often thin: only about thirty bishops and prelates, mostly Italian, were present at the start.

The council met in three periods: 1545 to 1547, when it moved for a time to Bologna; 1551 to 1552, when some Protestant envoys briefly attended; and 1562 to 1563 under Pius IV. It affirmed scripture and tradition together as sources of revelation, the Latin Vulgate as authoritative, justification through grace with faith and works, and seven sacraments, with the Mass a true sacrifice. It also ordered bishops to live in their dioceses and found seminaries.

A popular legend says the council meant to ban polyphonic church music until Palestrina's Missa Papae Marcelli changed its mind; the story is a later invention. The Roman Catechism, the revised Missal of 1570 and the Index of Forbidden Books carried its decisions forward until the Second Vatican Council.
story.zh:
路德等人早就呼吁召开大公会议，皇帝查理五世也力主借此弥合德意志的分裂。历任教宗担心会议凌驾于教宗权威之上，一再拖延，直到1545年12月保禄三世才终于在阿尔卑斯山南麓的帝国城市特伦托召开会议。出席人数常常寥寥无几：开幕时只有约三十位主教和高级教士，且多为意大利人。

会议分三期举行：1545年至1547年，期间一度迁往博洛尼亚；1551年至1552年，有几位新教使节短暂与会；1562年至1563年，由庇护四世主持。会议确认圣经与圣传同为启示的来源，拉丁文武加大译本具有权威，人借恩典并通过信德与善功得以称义，圣事共有七件，弥撒是真正的献祭。会议还要求主教驻守教区并设立修院。

流传甚广的说法是，会议本打算禁止复调教会音乐，帕莱斯特里纳的《马切鲁斯教皇弥撒》使其回心转意；这其实是后人编造的故事。《罗马要理问答》、1570年修订的《罗马弥撒经书》和《禁书目录》将会议的决定延续下去，直到第二次梵蒂冈大公会议。

summary.en: Days after the Protestant Henry of Navarre married the king's sister in Paris, Catholic forces killed the Huguenot leader Gaspard de Coligny on 24 August 1572 and mobs massacred thousands of Protestants in the capital. The killing spread to provincial towns for weeks, deepening France's Wars of Religion.
summary.zh: 新教徒纳瓦拉的亨利在巴黎迎娶国王之妹几天后，天主教势力于1572年8月24日杀死胡格诺派领袖加斯帕尔·德·科利尼，暴民随即在首都屠杀了数千名新教徒。杀戮在之后数周蔓延到外省城镇，使法国宗教战争愈演愈烈。

sources.title: Britannica: Massacre of Saint Bartholomew's Day
B. Diefendorf, The Saint Bartholomew's Day Massacre: A Brief History with Documents (2009)

note: Death tolls are estimates (roughly 2,000–3,000 in Paris, several thousand more in the provinces). Point at Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois, opposite the Louvre.

story.en:
The marriage of Margaret of Valois, sister of Charles IX, to the Protestant Henry of Navarre on 18 August 1572 was meant to seal peace between France's Catholics and Huguenots, and it drew many leading Protestants to a fiercely Catholic city. On 22 August a gunman wounded Admiral Gaspard de Coligny, the Huguenot leader who had gained influence over the young king.

What followed is still debated, but in the usual account the queen mother, Catherine de' Medici, and a small council, fearing Huguenot revenge, persuaded Charles to strike first. In the early hours of 24 August, St Bartholomew's Day, the duke of Guise's men killed Coligny and threw his body from a window. As the bell of Saint-Germain-l'Auxerrois rang, militia and mobs turned on Protestants across Paris. Navarre survived by converting under duress.

Some two to three thousand people died in Paris, and thousands more as the killing spread to Lyon, Rouen, Bordeaux and other towns into October. Pope Gregory XIII celebrated with a Te Deum and a commemorative medal, while Protestant Europe recoiled. War resumed, and Huguenot writers began to argue that subjects might resist a tyrannical king.
story.zh:
1572年8月18日，查理九世之妹瓦卢瓦的玛格丽特与新教徒纳瓦拉的亨利成婚，本意是巩固法国天主教徒与胡格诺派之间的和平，许多新教领袖因此来到这座天主教气氛浓烈的城市。8月22日，一名枪手打伤了对年轻国王颇有影响的胡格诺派领袖科利尼海军上将。

此后的经过至今仍有争议，但通常的说法是，太后凯瑟琳·德·美第奇和少数近臣担心胡格诺派报复，说服查理先发制人。8月24日圣巴托罗缪节凌晨，吉斯公爵的手下杀死科利尼，并把尸体扔出窗外。随着圣日耳曼-奥塞尔教堂的钟声响起，民兵和暴民在巴黎各处向新教徒下手。纳瓦拉的亨利被迫改宗才保住性命。

巴黎约有两三千人遇难，杀戮又蔓延到里昂、鲁昂、波尔多等城镇，持续到10月，外省又有数千人死亡。教宗格里高利十三世举行感恩赞美颂并铸造纪念章，新教欧洲则为之震惊。战争重新爆发，胡格诺派作家开始主张臣民可以反抗暴君。

summary.en: The revolt of the Low Countries against Philip II of Spain, led at first by William of Orange, began in 1568 over taxation, religious persecution and local liberties. It produced an independent Protestant Dutch Republic in the north, recognised by Spain in the Peace of Münster in 1648, while the southern provinces remained Habsburg and Catholic.
summary.zh: 尼德兰人民反抗西班牙国王腓力二世的起义始于1568年，起初由奥兰治的威廉领导，起因是赋税、宗教迫害和地方特权。战争的结果是北方建立了独立的新教荷兰共和国，1648年西班牙在《明斯特和约》中予以承认，南方诸省则仍归哈布斯堡王朝统治并信奉天主教。

label.en: William of Orange assassinated in Delft
label.zh: 奥兰治的威廉在代尔夫特遇刺
安特卫普被帕尔马公爵攻陷

sources.title: J. I. Israel, The Dutch Republic: Its Rise, Greatness, and Fall, 1477–1806 (1995)

note: Point at Heiligerlee, the battle of 23 May 1568 traditionally taken as the opening of the war. The Twelve Years' Truce (1609–1621) interrupted the fighting.

story.en:
Philip II ruled the seventeen provinces of the Netherlands from Spain. His taxes, persecution of Protestants and disregard of noble privileges stirred protest, and in 1566 a wave of iconoclasm swept the churches. Philip sent the duke of Alba with an army; his Council of Troubles, nicknamed the Council of Blood, sent over a thousand people to their deaths, and the counts of Egmont and Horne were beheaded in Brussels in June 1568. William of Orange had fled to Germany, and his brother Louis won the first battle, at Heiligerlee, that May.

The revolt took root after the Sea Beggars, rebel privateers, seized Brielle on 1 April 1572. In 1574 besieged Leiden was saved when dykes were cut and rebel ships sailed across the flooded fields; the city still celebrates every 3 October. The northern provinces formed the Union of Utrecht in 1579 and renounced Philip in 1581. William was shot dead in Delft in 1584, and Antwerp fell to the duke of Parma in 1585, fixing a line between north and south.

The Dutch Republic became Europe's leading trading power even as the war went on, and in 1648 Spain recognised its independence at Münster.
story.zh:
腓力二世从西班牙统治尼德兰十七省。他的苛税、对新教徒的迫害以及无视贵族特权的做法激起抗议，1566年一股破坏圣像的风潮席卷各地教堂。腓力派阿尔瓦公爵率军前来，其设立的“除暴委员会”被称为“血腥委员会”，处死了一千多人；1568年6月，埃格蒙特伯爵和霍恩伯爵在布鲁塞尔被斩首。奥兰治的威廉已逃往德意志，同年5月他的弟弟路易在海利赫莱打赢了第一仗。

1572年4月1日，起义者的武装私掠船“海上乞丐”攻占布里勒，起义由此扎下根来。1574年，被围困的莱顿在掘开堤坝、起义军船只驶过淹没的田野后得救，该城至今每年10月3日都举行庆祝。北方诸省于1579年结成乌得勒支同盟，1581年宣布废黜腓力。1584年威廉在代尔夫特遇刺身亡，1585年安特卫普被帕尔马公爵攻陷，南北界线由此大致确定。

战争仍在继续，荷兰共和国却已成为欧洲首屈一指的贸易强国。1648年，西班牙在明斯特承认了它的独立。

summary.en: Signed by Henry IV at Nantes in April 1598, the edict ended France's Wars of Religion by granting the Protestant Huguenots liberty of conscience, public worship in specified places, civil equality and garrisoned towns as security, while Catholicism remained the state religion. Louis XIV revoked it in 1685.
summary.zh: 1598年4月，亨利四世在南特签署这道敕令，给予新教胡格诺派信仰自由、在指定地点公开礼拜的权利、公民平等以及驻军城镇作为保障，同时天主教仍为国教，从而结束了法国宗教战争。1685年路易十四将其废除。

sources.title: M. P. Holt, The French Wars of Religion, 1562–1629 (2nd ed., 2005)

note: Dated 13 April 1598 (Gregorian; France adopted the Gregorian calendar in 1582). The general articles were followed by secret articles and royal warrants (brevets) in late April and May. Point at the Château des ducs de Bretagne in Nantes.

story.en:
Henry of Navarre, a Protestant, became heir to the French throne in 1584 and king in 1589, but Catholic Paris and the Catholic League refused to accept him. In 1593 he abjured Protestantism; the remark that Paris was well worth a Mass is attributed to him but is probably apocryphal. He was crowned in 1594, entered Paris, and over the next four years bought or beat most League nobles into submission.

To end more than thirty years of intermittent civil war, Henry signed the Edict of Nantes in April 1598. It granted Huguenots liberty of conscience, public worship in many named places though not in Paris, equal access to offices and universities and special mixed courts, and, in separate royal warrants, garrisoned places of security such as La Rochelle. Catholicism remained the state religion, and the reluctant parlements registered the edict only under royal pressure.

The settlement was a truce rather than true toleration. After the fall of La Rochelle in 1628, the Peace of Alès stripped the Huguenots of their fortresses, and in 1685 Louis XIV revoked the edict entirely, driving perhaps 200,000 Huguenots into exile.
story.zh:
新教徒纳瓦拉的亨利于1584年成为法国王位继承人，1589年即位为王，但信奉天主教的巴黎和天主教联盟拒不承认他。1593年他宣布放弃新教；“巴黎值得一场弥撒”这句话常被归于他名下，但很可能是后人杜撰。1594年他加冕并进入巴黎，此后四年间，以收买或武力迫使联盟的大多数贵族归顺。

为结束三十多年断断续续的内战，亨利于1598年4月签署《南特敕令》。敕令给予胡格诺派信仰自由，允许他们在许多指定地点（巴黎除外）公开礼拜，平等担任公职、进入大学，设立双方人员组成的特别法庭，并在另行颁发的王室特许状中给予拉罗谢尔等驻军的安全城镇。天主教仍为国教，各地高等法院很不情愿，在王室施压下才登记了敕令。

这一安排与其说是真正的宽容，不如说是休战。1628年拉罗谢尔陷落后，《阿莱和约》剥夺了胡格诺派的要塞；1685年路易十四彻底废除敕令，迫使约二十万胡格诺派教徒流亡国外。

name.en: Founding of the Dutch East India Company (VOC)

summary.en: On 20 March 1602 the States General chartered the United East India Company (VOC), merging rival Dutch ventures into a single monopoly for trade east of the Cape of Good Hope. Financed by freely traded shares, it became a quasi-state that made treaties, waged war and dominated the Asian spice trade until it was dissolved in 1799.
summary.zh: 1602年3月20日，尼德兰联省议会特许成立联合东印度公司（VOC），将相互竞争的荷兰远航公司合并为一家，独占好望角以东的贸易。公司以可自由买卖的股份筹资，成为一个能够缔约、开战的准国家，长期主宰亚洲香料贸易，直至1799年解散。

sources.title: Femme S. Gaastra, The Dutch East India Company: Expansion and Decline (2003)

note: Placed at the Oost-Indisch Huis in Amsterdam, headquarters of the largest of the six chambers (acquired 1606).

story.en:
Dutch ships first reached Java in 1596, and within five years half a dozen rival companies were sending fleets east and bidding up the price of pepper. The statesman Johan van Oldenbarnevelt pressed them to merge. The charter of 1602 created one company run by six city chambers under a board known as the Heeren XVII, the Gentlemen Seventeen.

Anyone could subscribe, and the shares soon changed hands on the Amsterdam exchange, which is why the VOC is often called the first publicly traded company. Its charter also let it build forts, keep armies and sign treaties in the name of the Republic. Under Jan Pieterszoon Coen it founded Batavia (Jakarta) in 1619, and in 1621 it conquered the Banda Islands to monopolise nutmeg, killing or deporting most of their people.

For two centuries the company linked Europe to Asia, from Cape Town to Dejima in Nagasaki, where it was the only European trader Japan allowed. Corruption, debt and war with Britain ruined it, and its charter lapsed at the end of 1799.
story.zh:
1596年荷兰船只首次抵达爪哇，此后五年间已有六七家公司竞相派船东航，把胡椒价格越抬越高。政治家奥尔登巴内费尔特力促它们合并。1602年的特许状由此建立了一家统一的公司，由六个城市分会经营，最高机构称为“十七人董事会”。

任何人都可以认购股份，股票很快就在阿姆斯特丹交易所流通，因此东印度公司常被称为世界上第一家公开上市公司。特许状还授权它修筑要塞、组建军队，并以共和国名义缔结条约。在扬·彼得松·科恩主持下，公司于1619年建立巴达维亚（今雅加达），1621年又征服班达群岛以垄断肉豆蔻，岛上居民大多遭杀害或被迁走。

两百年间，公司把欧洲与亚洲连在一起，据点从开普敦一直延伸到长崎出岛，它是日本唯一准许通商的欧洲商人。腐败、债务以及与英国的战争最终拖垮了公司，其特许状于1799年底期满失效。

summary.en: Early in 1605 the Madrid printer Juan de la Cuesta issued the first part of Miguel de Cervantes's The Ingenious Gentleman Don Quixote of La Mancha, the tale of a country gentleman driven mad by chivalric romances. An immediate success, completed by a second part in 1615, it is often called the first modern novel.
summary.zh: 1605年初，马德里印刷商胡安·德·拉·奎斯塔出版了塞万提斯《奇情异想的绅士堂吉诃德·德·拉曼查》第一部，讲述一位乡绅因沉迷骑士小说而发狂的故事。此书一问世便大受欢迎，1615年出版第二部，常被誉为第一部现代小说。

note: Placed at Juan de la Cuesta's printing house on the Calle de Atocha, Madrid. The first edition is dated 1605; its licences date from late 1604.

story.en:
Cervantes was in his late fifties and had little to show for an eventful life. He had been wounded at Lepanto in 1571, losing the use of his left hand, spent five years as a captive in Algiers, and later, as a tax collector, landed in prison in Seville. In the prologue he says the book was conceived in a prison, traditionally taken to mean Seville.

Part One, published by Francisco de Robles in Madrid, was a hit. Pirated editions appeared in Lisbon and Valencia the same year, and the knight tilting at windmills he takes for giants, with his down-to-earth squire Sancho Panza, quickly became proverbial. Translations followed into English (1612) and French (1614).

In 1614 an unknown writer calling himself Alonso Fernández de Avellaneda published a spurious sequel. Cervantes answered with his own Part Two in 1615, in which characters have read Part One and mock the impostor. He died in Madrid the next year, leaving a book that turned parody into a study of illusion and reality.
story.zh:
塞万提斯年近六旬，一生跌宕却并无多少成就。他1571年在勒班陀海战中负伤，左手从此残废；后来在阿尔及尔做了五年俘虏；再后来当收税官，又在塞维利亚身陷囹圄。他在序言中说此书“孕育于监狱之中”，一般认为指的就是塞维利亚。

第一部由弗朗西斯科·德·罗夫莱斯在马德里出版，一炮而红。同年里斯本和巴伦西亚便出现了盗印本；把风车当作巨人冲杀的骑士和他务实的侍从桑丘·潘沙，很快成了家喻户晓的形象。英译本（1612年）和法译本（1614年）相继问世。

1614年，一位化名阿隆索·费尔南德斯·德·阿韦利亚内达的作者出版了伪续篇。塞万提斯于1615年推出自己的第二部作为回应，书中人物读过第一部，还嘲笑那位冒名者。次年他在马德里去世，留下一部把戏仿升华为对幻想与现实之思考的作品。

name.zh: 莎士比亚《第一对开本》出版

summary.en: Seven years after Shakespeare's death, his fellow actors John Heminges and Henry Condell gathered 36 of his plays into one folio volume, Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies. Eighteen of them, including Macbeth, The Tempest, Julius Caesar and Twelfth Night, had never been printed and survive only because of it.
summary.zh: 莎士比亚去世七年后，他的演员同伴约翰·赫明斯和亨利·康德尔将他的36部剧作汇编成一部对开本，题为《威廉·莎士比亚先生的喜剧、历史剧和悲剧》。其中18部此前从未付印，包括《麦克白》《暴风雨》《裘力斯·凯撒》和《第十二夜》，全赖此书才得以流传。

sources.title: Emma Smith, Shakespeare's First Folio: Four Centuries of an Iconic Book (2016)

note: Placed at St Paul's Churchyard, centre of the London book trade, where the co-publisher Edward Blount kept his shop; the book was printed by William and Isaac Jaggard. The print run is usually estimated at about 750 copies (Britannica says about 1,000); some 235 survive. Wikidata Q833645 is the main First Folio item although its English description names a single copy.

summary.en: A struggle between Charles I and Parliament over taxation, religion and royal power became a series of wars (1642–1651) across England, Scotland and Ireland. Parliament's New Model Army crushed the king at Naseby in 1645; Charles was tried and beheaded in 1649, and Oliver Cromwell's victory at Worcester in 1651 ended royalist resistance.
summary.zh: 查理一世与议会围绕税收、宗教和王权的冲突，演变为1642至1651年间席卷英格兰、苏格兰和爱尔兰的一系列战争。1645年议会的新模范军在纳西比大败国王；1649年查理受审并被斩首；1651年奥利弗·克伦威尔在伍斯特获胜，保王党的抵抗就此终结。

label.en: Charles I raises his standard at Nottingham
label.zh: 查理一世在诺丁汉竖起王旗

label.en: Execution of Charles I in Whitehall
label.zh: 查理一世在白厅被处决

note: Marker at Naseby, the decisive battle (14 June 1645). The war opened when Charles raised his standard at Nottingham on 22 August 1642 in the Julian calendar then used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent.

story.en:
Charles I ruled without Parliament from 1629 to 1640, raising money by disputed means and pushing a ceremonial church that many Protestants feared was popish. A failed war with the Scots forced him to recall Parliament, which attacked his ministers. In January 1642 he marched into the Commons to arrest five members, who had already fled; by August both sides were raising armies.

The first battle, at Edgehill, was inconclusive. Parliament allied with the Scots and won at Marston Moor in 1644, then rebuilt its forces as the New Model Army under Sir Thomas Fairfax, with Cromwell commanding the cavalry. At Naseby in June 1645 it destroyed the king's main army and captured his letters, which showed him seeking help from Ireland and abroad and were promptly printed.

Defeated again in a second war in 1648, Charles was tried and executed. Cromwell then crushed resistance in Ireland, with massacres at Drogheda and Wexford, and in Scotland, at Dunbar and finally Worcester in 1651, after which the young Charles II escaped to France. England was a republic until the Restoration of 1660.
story.zh:
1629至1640年间，查理一世撇开议会独自统治，以颇具争议的手段敛财，又推行注重仪式的教会政策，令许多新教徒担心国教正滑向天主教。对苏格兰的战争失利迫使他重新召集议会，议会随即弹劾他的大臣。1642年1月，他亲率卫兵闯入下院捉拿五名议员，对方早已逃走；到8月，双方都在招兵买马。

首战埃奇希尔胜负未分。议会与苏格兰人结盟，1644年在马斯顿荒原获胜，随后把军队改编为新模范军，由托马斯·费尔法克斯爵士统率，克伦威尔指挥骑兵。1645年6月的纳西比战役中，新模范军歼灭了国王的主力，还缴获了他的书信，信中显示他曾向爱尔兰和外国求援，议会立刻将其公开印行。

1648年第二次内战中查理再度失败，随后受审并被处决。克伦威尔接着镇压爱尔兰，在德罗赫达和韦克斯福德制造屠杀；又转战苏格兰，先后取得邓巴战役和1651年伍斯特战役的胜利，年轻的查理二世逃往法国。此后英格兰一直是共和国，直到1660年王政复辟。

summary.en: On 30 January 1649 (Old Style) Charles I was beheaded on a scaffold outside the Banqueting House in Whitehall, after a court created by the purged House of Commons convicted him of treason against his people. Within weeks England abolished the monarchy and the House of Lords and became a republic, the Commonwealth.
summary.zh: 1649年1月30日（旧历），查理一世在白厅国宴厅外的断头台上被斩首。此前，由清洗后的下议院设立的特别法庭判定他犯有背叛人民的叛国罪。数周之内，英格兰废除君主制和上议院，成为共和国，史称“英吉利共和国”。

sources.title: C. V. Wedgwood, The Trial of Charles I (1964)
Britannica: Charles I (king of Great Britain and Ireland)
Wikipedia: Execution of Charles I of England

note: 30 January 1649 in the Julian calendar then used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent.

story.en:
After the army purged Parliament of members willing to negotiate, the remaining "Rump" set up a High Court of Justice. The trial opened in Westminster Hall on 20 January 1649. Charles refused to plead, arguing that no court had authority over a king, and on 27 January he was sentenced to death. Fifty-nine commissioners signed the warrant; Cromwell's name is third.

On the cold morning of 30 January the king walked across St James's Park to the Banqueting House, passed beneath the Rubens ceiling celebrating his father James I, and stepped out through a window onto the scaffold. According to contemporary accounts he wore two shirts so that no one would mistake his shivering for fear. The head was struck off in a single blow, and one witness recorded a deep groan from the crowd.

Monarchy and the House of Lords were abolished in March. A book of the king's supposed meditations, Eikon Basilike, made him a martyr in royalist eyes, and after the Restoration in 1660 several of the surviving regicides were executed.
story.zh:
军队把愿意与国王谈判的议员清洗出议会后，剩下的“残缺议会”设立了高等法院。1649年1月20日，审判在威斯敏斯特厅开庭。查理拒绝答辩，坚称任何法庭都无权审判国王。1月27日他被判处死刑，59名法官在死刑令上签名，克伦威尔的名字列第三。

1月30日清晨天气寒冷，国王步行穿过圣詹姆斯公园来到国宴厅，从鲁本斯为颂扬其父詹姆斯一世而绘的天顶画下走过，再经一扇窗户登上断头台。据当时记载，他特意穿了两件衬衫，以免人们把他的颤抖误认为恐惧。刽子手一斧便砍下了他的头，一位目击者记下了人群中发出的一声沉痛呻吟。

同年3月，君主制和上议院被废除。一部据称收录国王临终沉思的《国王的圣像》使他在保王党人心中成为殉道者；1660年王政复辟后，数名仍在世的弑君者被处死。

summary.en: On 28 November 1660 (Old Style) twelve men meeting after a lecture by Christopher Wren at Gresham College, London, resolved to found a college for promoting experimental learning. Chartered by Charles II in 1662 as the Royal Society, it began Philosophical Transactions in 1665 and counted Isaac Newton, its president from 1703 to 1727, among its fellows.
summary.zh: 1660年11月28日（旧历），十二位学者在伦敦格雷沙姆学院听完克里斯托弗·雷恩的讲座后聚会，决定创办一个促进实验学问的学院。1662年，它获查理二世颁发特许状，成为皇家学会；1665年创办《哲学汇刊》。艾萨克·牛顿是其会员，并于1703至1727年担任会长。

sources.title: Michael Hunter, Science and Society in Restoration England (1981)

note: The QID is the Royal Society itself (no separate founding-event item). Placed at the original Gresham College in Bishopsgate. 28 November 1660 is the Julian date used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent. The royal charter followed on 15 July 1662.

summary.en: In November 1688 William of Orange, stadtholder of the Dutch Republic, landed at Torbay with a large army at the invitation of English opponents of the Catholic James II. James fled to France, and in 1689 Parliament offered the crown jointly to William and Mary and passed the Bill of Rights, limiting royal power.
summary.zh: 1688年11月，应反对天主教国王詹姆斯二世的英格兰人士之邀，荷兰共和国执政奥兰治亲王威廉率大军在托贝登陆。詹姆斯逃往法国。1689年议会将王位共同授予威廉与玛丽，并通过《权利法案》，限制了王权。

sources.title: Tim Harris, Revolution: The Great Crisis of the British Monarchy, 1685–1720 (2006)
Steve Pincus, 1688: The First Modern Revolution (2009)

note: Placed at Brixham on Torbay, where William landed on 5 November 1688 in the Julian calendar then used in England; the date shown is the Gregorian equivalent (the Dutch used 15 November).

story.en:
James II, a Catholic, used his royal powers to suspend laws against Catholics and Dissenters and put the Seven Bishops on trial for refusing to read his Declaration of Indulgence. In June 1688 his queen gave birth to a son, promising a Catholic dynasty; rumour falsely claimed the baby had been smuggled in a warming pan. On the day the bishops were acquitted, seven leading men invited William of Orange, James's nephew and son-in-law, to intervene.

William had his own reasons: he wanted England's resources against Louis XIV. A "Protestant wind" carried his fleet of several hundred ships down the Channel past the English navy to Torbay. James's army crumbled as officers such as John Churchill defected. The king fled, reportedly dropping the Great Seal into the Thames, was caught, and then allowed to escape to France.

A Convention Parliament declared the throne vacant and in February 1689 offered it to William and Mary together with a Declaration of Right, later the Bill of Rights. The revolution was bloodless in England but not in Scotland and Ireland, where it was settled at Killiecrankie and the Boyne.
story.zh:
信奉天主教的詹姆斯二世动用王权中止针对天主教徒和不信国教者的法律，并因七位主教拒绝宣读其《信教自由宣言》而将他们送上法庭。1688年6月王后诞下一子，天主教王朝似将延续；坊间谣传婴儿是用暖床炉偷运进宫的，实属无稽。就在主教们被宣判无罪的当天，七位要人联名邀请詹姆斯的外甥兼女婿奥兰治亲王威廉出兵干预。

威廉也有自己的打算：他希望借英格兰的力量对抗路易十四。一阵“新教之风”把他数百艘船的舰队送下英吉利海峡，绕过英国海军抵达托贝。约翰·丘吉尔等军官纷纷倒戈，詹姆斯的军队土崩瓦解。国王出逃，据说途中把国玺扔进了泰晤士河；他一度被截获，随后被有意放走，逃往法国。

协商议会宣布王位空缺，并于1689年2月将王位授予威廉和玛丽，同时附上《权利宣言》，即后来的《权利法案》。这场革命在英格兰几乎兵不血刃，但在苏格兰和爱尔兰却要靠基利克兰基战役和博因河战役才见分晓。

summary.en: When the childless Charles II of Spain left his empire to Louis XIV's grandson Philip of Anjou in 1700, England, the Dutch Republic and Austria went to war to prevent a union of French and Spanish power. Peace at Utrecht (1713) and Rastatt (1714) kept Philip V on the throne but cost Spain its Italian and Low Countries lands.
summary.zh: 1700年无嗣的西班牙国王卡洛斯二世去世，遗命将帝国传给路易十四之孙安茹公爵腓力。英格兰、荷兰共和国和奥地利哈布斯堡家族为阻止法西两国势力联合而开战。1713年《乌得勒支和约》与1714年《拉施塔特和约》保住了腓力五世的西班牙王位，但西班牙失去了在意大利和低地国家的领地。

sources.title: Britannica: War of the Spanish Succession
John A. Lynn, The Wars of Louis XIV, 1667–1714 (1999)
Henry Kamen, The War of Succession in Spain, 1700–15 (1969)

note: Marker at Blenheim (Blindheim, Bavaria), where Marlborough and Prince Eugene defeated the French and Bavarians on 13 August 1704. Fighting began in Italy in 1701; Britain gained Gibraltar and Minorca at Utrecht, and Barcelona fell to Philip V in September 1714.

summary.en: Edited by Denis Diderot and, until 1759, Jean le Rond d'Alembert, the Encyclopédie, or Reasoned Dictionary of the Sciences, Arts and Crafts appeared in Paris in 17 volumes of text (1751–1765) and 11 of plates (1762–1772). Its tens of thousands of articles, by Voltaire, Rousseau and many others, spread Enlightenment ideas despite repeated bans.
summary.zh: 《百科全书，或科学、艺术和工艺详解词典》由德尼·狄德罗主编，让·勒朗·达朗贝尔在1759年前任合编者，在巴黎出版正文17卷（1751—1765年）和图版11卷（1762—1772年）。伏尔泰、卢梭等众多作者撰写的数万条词条，冲破一再的查禁，传播了启蒙思想。

sources.title: Philipp Blom, Encyclopédie: The Triumph of Reason in an Unreasonable Age (2004)
ARTFL Encyclopédie Project, University of Chicago

note: Placed generically at Paris, where the publisher André Le Breton and his partners issued it. D'Alembert withdrew from the editorship in 1758–59. The last ten text volumes (1765) carried a false Neuchâtel imprint.

story.en:
The project began modestly in 1745, when the Paris bookseller André Le Breton commissioned a French translation of Ephraim Chambers's English Cyclopaedia. Diderot and the mathematician d'Alembert turned it into something far bigger: a survey of all knowledge, organised in d'Alembert's Preliminary Discourse (1751) around reason rather than revelation, and giving the mechanical arts the same dignity as theology.

Contributors included Voltaire, Rousseau, who wrote on music, Montesquieu and the economist Quesnay, but the tireless Chevalier de Jaucourt wrote roughly a quarter of all the articles. Cross-references slyly undercut orthodox entries. The authorities suspended it in 1752, and in 1759, after a scandal over another freethinking book, the royal licence was revoked and the pope placed it on the Index.

Diderot carried on in secret. In 1764 he discovered that Le Breton, fearing prosecution, had quietly cut passages from the final proofs, and he never forgave him. The remaining volumes came out together in 1765, the magnificent plates of workshops and machines by 1772. Reprints carried its ideas across Europe.
story.zh:
这项事业起初并不宏大：1745年，巴黎书商安德烈·勒布雷东委托人把伊弗雷姆·钱伯斯的英文《百科全书》译成法文。狄德罗和数学家达朗贝尔却把它变成了规模大得多的作品——一部包罗全部知识的总览。达朗贝尔在1751年的《序论》中以理性而非天启来组织知识体系，并赋予机械技艺与神学同等的尊严。

撰稿人包括伏尔泰、撰写音乐词条的卢梭、孟德斯鸠和经济学家魁奈，但不知疲倦的若古骑士一人就写了大约四分之一的词条。书中的交叉索引常常巧妙地拆解正统词条的说法。当局于1752年下令暂停出版；1759年另一部自由思想著作引发风波后，王室特许被撤销，教皇也将其列入禁书目录。

狄德罗转入地下继续编纂。1764年他发现勒布雷东因害怕被起诉，暗中删改了最后几卷的校样，对此始终耿耿于怀。其余各卷于1765年一并问世，描绘作坊与机器的精美图版到1772年出齐。各种翻印本把它的思想传遍了欧洲。

summary.en: James Watt's patent of January 1769 for a condenser separate from the cylinder stopped steam engines wasting heat by cooling the cylinder at every stroke, so that they burned far less coal than Thomas Newcomen's design. In partnership with Matthew Boulton he began supplying commercial engines in 1776, helping to power the Industrial Revolution.
summary.zh: 1769年1月，詹姆斯·瓦特为与汽缸分离的冷凝器申请了专利。这一设计避免了每一冲程都冷却汽缸所造成的热量浪费，使蒸汽机的耗煤量远低于纽科门式蒸汽机。他与马修·博尔顿合作，于1776年开始提供商用蒸汽机，为工业革命提供了动力。

sources.title: Richard L. Hills, James Watt, 3 vols. (2002–2006)
Jenny Uglow, The Lunar Men: The Friends Who Made the Future (2002)

note: Marker at the approximate site of Boulton and Watt's Soho Manufactory, Birmingham, where the partnership was based from 1774; the idea was conceived in Glasgow in 1765. The first two engines (1776) worked at Bloomfield Colliery, Tipton, and John Wilkinson's ironworks in Shropshire.

story.en:
Watt was a mathematical-instrument maker at the University of Glasgow when, in 1763–64, he was asked to repair a model Newcomen engine. He saw that most of its fuel went into reheating the cylinder after each cooling jet of water. By his own later recollection, the solution came to him in 1765 during a Sunday walk on Glasgow Green: condense the steam in a separate vessel and keep the cylinder hot.

Turning the idea into a working machine took a decade. His first backer, John Roebuck, went bankrupt, and his share passed to the Birmingham manufacturer Matthew Boulton. Watt moved south in 1774, Parliament extended his patent to 1800, and John Wilkinson's new cannon-boring technique finally produced cylinders accurate enough to hold the steam.

The first engines began work in 1776, pumping water from mines; customers paid royalties based on the coal they saved. When James Boswell visited Soho that year, Boulton told him that he sold what all the world desired: power. Rotary and double-acting versions followed in the 1780s and drove mills and factories.
story.zh:
瓦特原是格拉斯哥大学的数学仪器制造师。1763至1764年间，他受托修理一台纽科门蒸汽机模型，发现大部分燃料都耗费在每次喷冷水之后重新加热汽缸上。据他晚年回忆，1765年一个星期天他在格拉斯哥绿地散步时想到了办法：让蒸汽在另一个容器中冷凝，使汽缸始终保持高温。

把这一构想变成可用的机器花了十年。他最初的资助人约翰·罗巴克破产，股份转给了伯明翰制造商马修·博尔顿。1774年瓦特南迁，议会把他的专利延长至1800年，约翰·威尔金森新发明的炮管镗削技术终于造出了足够精密、不漏汽的汽缸。

1776年，首批蒸汽机开始为矿井抽水；用户按节省下来的煤炭支付专利费。那年詹姆斯·博斯韦尔参观索霍工厂时，博尔顿对他说，自己出售的正是全世界都想要的东西——动力。18世纪80年代，旋转式和双动式蒸汽机相继问世，开始驱动磨坊和工厂。

name.en: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen

summary.en: On 26 August 1789 France's National Constituent Assembly, sitting at Versailles, adopted a 17-article declaration proclaiming that men are born and remain free and equal in rights, that sovereignty resides in the nation and that law is the expression of the general will. It became the preamble to the constitution of 1791 and a model for later charters of rights.
summary.zh: 1789年8月26日，在凡尔赛开会的法国国民制宪议会通过了一份共17条的宣言，宣告人生来并始终自由、权利平等，主权属于国民，法律是公意的表达。它成为1791年宪法的序言，也成为后世各种权利宪章的范本。

sources.title: Britannica: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
Lynn Hunt, The French Revolution and Human Rights: A Brief Documentary History (1996)
Avalon Project (Yale Law School): Declaration of the Rights of Man, 1789

note: Placed at the Hôtel des Menus-Plaisirs, Versailles, where the Assembly sat until it followed the king to Paris in October 1789 (hence no Paris place link). Wikidata's 1790 inception is not the adoption date.

story.en:
The Declaration was written in the weeks after the fall of the Bastille, as the Assembly abolished feudal privileges on the night of 4 August. Lafayette, veteran of the American war, had presented a draft in July, discussed with Thomas Jefferson, then the American minister in Paris; deputies including Mounier and Sieyès argued over every clause.

The final text named liberty, property, security and resistance to oppression as natural rights. It established equality before the law, the presumption of innocence, freedom of opinion and of the press, and taxation by consent. Louis XVI hesitated to approve it and gave way only on 5 October, after the women's march on Versailles that brought the royal family to Paris.

Its universal language soon tested its limits. Olympe de Gouges replied in 1791 with a Declaration of the Rights of Woman and was guillotined two years later, and slavery in the colonies was abolished only in 1794, then restored by Napoleon. Yet the text echoed through later constitutions and the Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948, and it remains part of French constitutional law.
story.zh:
宣言起草于攻占巴士底狱后的几周里，其间议会在8月4日夜废除了封建特权。参加过美国独立战争的拉法耶特已在7月提交了一份草案，并曾与时任美国驻巴黎公使托马斯·杰斐逊商讨；穆尼埃、西耶斯等代表则对每一条款反复争论。

最终文本把自由、财产、安全和反抗压迫列为天赋权利，确立了法律面前人人平等、无罪推定、言论与出版自由，以及纳税须经同意等原则。路易十六迟迟不肯批准，直到10月5日巴黎妇女向凡尔赛进军、把王室带回巴黎之际才被迫让步。

宣言的普遍主义措辞很快就暴露出局限。奥兰普·德古热于1791年发表《女权和女公民权宣言》作为回应，两年后被送上断头台；殖民地的奴隶制直到1794年才被废除，后来又被拿破仑恢复。但这份文本在后世诸多宪法和1948年《世界人权宣言》中不断回响，至今仍是法国宪法的组成部分。

name.en: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
name.zh: 沃斯通克拉夫特《女权辩护》

summary.en: Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Woman, published in London by Joseph Johnson early in 1792, argued that women seem inferior only because they are denied a rational education, and demanded that they be educated as men's equals and able to earn their own living. It became a founding text of modern feminism.
summary.zh: 玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特的《女权辩护》于1792年初由约瑟夫·约翰逊在伦敦出版。书中指出，女性之所以显得低人一等，只是因为她们被剥夺了理性教育；她要求女性接受与男性平等的教育，并能自食其力。此书成为现代女性主义的奠基之作。

sources.title: Britannica: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman
Janet Todd, Mary Wollstonecraft: A Revolutionary Life (2000)
Wikipedia: A Vindication of the Rights of Woman

note: Placed at Joseph Johnson's shop in St Paul's Churchyard, London.

story.en:
Wollstonecraft had already answered Edmund Burke's attack on the French Revolution with A Vindication of the Rights of Men (1790). Her second Vindication, written in about six weeks, was dedicated to Talleyrand, whose 1791 report to the French Assembly proposed that girls be educated only for domestic life. She also took aim at Rousseau, whose ideal woman in Émile is trained simply to please.

Her case was that reason, not sex, is what makes a human being, and that a society which keeps women ignorant and dependent corrupts both women and men. She proposed national day schools where boys and girls would learn together, and she wanted women to be able to work, to be physicians or run businesses, and not to marry for support alone.

The book sold well and was soon translated into French and German. After her early death in 1797, days after giving birth to the future Mary Shelley, her husband William Godwin's candid memoir exposed her love affairs, and her reputation collapsed; Horace Walpole had already called her a hyena in petticoats. Later suffragists revived her, and Millicent Fawcett wrote the introduction to a new edition a century after the first.
story.zh:
此前，沃斯通克拉夫特已发表《人权辩护》（1790年），回击埃德蒙·伯克对法国大革命的抨击。她的第二部《辩护》大约用了六周写成，题献给塔列朗——后者在1791年向法国议会提交的报告中主张女孩只需接受持家方面的教育。她还把矛头指向卢梭，因为《爱弥儿》中的理想女性只被教导如何取悦男人。

她的论点是：使人成为人的是理性而非性别；一个让女性愚昧、依附于人的社会，会同时败坏女性和男性。她提议设立国家日间学校，让男孩和女孩一同学习；她希望女性能够工作，能当医生、经营生意，而不必仅为生计而结婚。

此书销路很好，不久便译成法文和德文。1797年她在生下日后的玛丽·雪莱几天后早逝，丈夫威廉·戈德温坦率的回忆录披露了她的情史，她的名声随之一落千丈；霍勒斯·沃波尔早先还骂她是“穿裙子的鬣狗”。后来的妇女选举权运动者重新发现了她，约一个世纪后，米莉森特·福西特为此书的新版撰写了导言。

name.zh: 拿破仑第一次意大利战役

summary.en: Given command of the ill-supplied French Army of Italy in March 1796, the 26-year-old Napoleon Bonaparte split the Piedmontese and Austrian armies, forced Piedmont out of the war, besieged Mantua and beat four Austrian relief attempts, the last at Rivoli. At Campo Formio in 1797 Austria ceded Belgium and recognised a French-dominated northern Italy, receiving Venice in exchange.
summary.zh: 1796年3月，26岁的拿破仑·波拿巴接掌给养匮乏的法国意大利方面军。他分割撒丁—皮埃蒙特军与奥军，迫使皮埃蒙特退出战争，围困曼托瓦，并四次击退奥军的解围行动，最后一次在里沃利。1797年《坎波福尔米奥和约》中，奥地利割让比利时，承认由法国主导的北意大利，并换得威尼斯。

label.en: Takes command of the Army of Italy at Nice
label.zh: 在尼斯接掌意大利方面军

label.en: Battle of the bridge of Lodi

sources.title: Martin Boycott-Brown, The Road to Rivoli: Napoleon's First Campaign (2001)
David G. Chandler, The Campaigns of Napoleon (1966)

note: Marker at Rivoli Veronese, the decisive battle (14–15 January 1797). Dates follow Wikidata (27 March 1796 to 17 October 1797).

story.en:
The Directory saw Italy as a sideshow to the main offensive in Germany. Bonaparte, newly married to Joséphine, found his troops unpaid and ragged at Nice and promised them the rich plains of Lombardy. Moving fast through the Ligurian hills, he beat the Austrians and Piedmontese separately at Montenotte and nearby battles, and on 28 April Piedmont signed an armistice.

On 10 May his troops stormed the bridge at Lodi; years later on St Helena he said it was there that he first saw himself as a man of destiny. He entered Milan on 15 May and laid siege to Mantua. Four Austrian armies tried to relieve it. At Arcole in November he seized a flag on the bridge, a scene later glorified by painters, and at Rivoli in January 1797 he broke the last attempt. Mantua surrendered on 2 February.

He then marched into the Alps toward Vienna and dictated preliminaries at Leoben, while shipping Italian art to Paris and creating sister republics. The ancient Republic of Venice fell in May, and at Campo Formio it was handed to Austria. The campaign made Bonaparte the most famous general in Europe.
story.zh:
督政府原本把意大利视为次要战场，主攻方向在德意志。新婚不久的波拿巴来到尼斯，发现部下欠饷多时、衣衫褴褛，便许诺带他们去富饶的伦巴第平原。他在利古里亚山地迅速穿插，在蒙特诺特及附近数战中把奥军和皮埃蒙特军各个击破，4月28日皮埃蒙特签订停战协定。

5月10日，法军强攻洛迪桥；多年后他在圣赫勒拿岛上说，正是在那里他第一次觉得自己负有天命。5月15日他进入米兰，随即围困曼托瓦。奥地利先后派出四支军队前来解围。11月的阿尔科莱战役中，他在桥头抓起一面军旗，这一幕后来被画家们大加渲染；1797年1月他在里沃利粉碎了奥军最后一次解围。2月2日曼托瓦投降。

他随后翻越阿尔卑斯山逼近维也纳，在莱奥本强定预备和约，同时把意大利的艺术品运往巴黎，并扶植起一批姊妹共和国。古老的威尼斯共和国于5月覆亡，《坎波福尔米奥和约》又把它交给了奥地利。这场战役使波拿巴成为全欧洲最负盛名的将领。

summary.en: On 21 October 1805 a British fleet of 27 ships of the line under Vice-Admiral Horatio Nelson attacked a Franco-Spanish fleet of 33 under Pierre-Charles Villeneuve off Cape Trafalgar, taking or destroying 22 without losing a ship. Nelson was killed in the battle, but Britain's command of the sea went unchallenged for the rest of the Napoleonic Wars.
summary.zh: 1805年10月21日，霍雷肖·纳尔逊中将率领由27艘战列舰组成的英国舰队，在特拉法加角外海攻击维尔纳夫指挥的33艘法西联合舰队，俘获或击毁敌舰22艘，自身无一损失。纳尔逊在战斗中阵亡，但此后整个拿破仑战争期间，英国的制海权再未受到挑战。

sources.title: Roy Adkins, Trafalgar: The Biography of a Battle (2004)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata (off Cape Trafalgar, south-east of Cádiz).

story.en:
Napoleon's plan to invade Britain depended on gathering enough warships to control the Channel. It collapsed when Villeneuve's combined fleet retreated to Cádiz, and by the time it sailed out on 19–20 October the Grande Armée had already marched east against Austria. Nelson had been waiting offshore with a plan to break the enemy line rather than fight it ship against ship.

Before the action he hoisted the signal "England expects that every man will do his duty." Two British columns, led by Nelson in HMS Victory and Cuthbert Collingwood in Royal Sovereign, sailed straight at the long Franco-Spanish line, cutting it into pieces that were overwhelmed in close combat. At about a quarter past one a musket ball fired from the French Redoutable struck Nelson; he died below decks some three hours later, after being told the battle was won.

A storm the next day wrecked many prizes. Nelson's body was brought home preserved in a cask of spirits and given a state funeral in St Paul's Cathedral. Napoleon turned to economic warfare against Britain, which kept command of the sea.
story.zh:
拿破仑入侵英国的计划取决于能否集结足够的战舰控制英吉利海峡。维尔纳夫的联合舰队退入加的斯后，这一计划便告破产；等到这支舰队于10月19日至20日出港时，大军团早已挥师东进对付奥地利。纳尔逊一直在外海守候，他的打算是切断敌方战列线，而不是逐舰对攻。

开战前，他升起了“英格兰期望人人恪尽其责”的旗号。英军分成两路纵队，分别由纳尔逊乘“胜利”号、科林伍德乘“君权”号率领，直插法西联合舰队绵长的战列线，将其截成数段，在近战中各个歼灭。约下午一点一刻，法舰“敬畏”号上射出的一颗枪弹击中纳尔逊；他被抬到下层甲板，约三小时后在得知胜利的消息后去世。

次日的风暴使许多战利舰沉没。纳尔逊的遗体浸在一桶烈酒中运回英国，在圣保罗大教堂举行了国葬。拿破仑转而对英国发动经济战，而英国则始终牢牢掌握着制海权。

summary.en: On 2 December 1805, the first anniversary of his coronation, Napoleon defeated a larger Russian and Austrian army under Tsar Alexander I and Emperor Francis II near Austerlitz (Slavkov u Brna) in Moravia. The "Battle of the Three Emperors" broke the Third Coalition: Austria made peace at Pressburg, and the Holy Roman Empire was dissolved in 1806.
summary.zh: 1805年12月2日，正值加冕一周年，拿破仑在摩拉维亚的奥斯特利茨（今斯拉夫科夫）附近击败了由沙皇亚历山大一世和皇帝弗朗茨二世率领、兵力占优的俄奥联军。这场“三皇会战”瓦解了第三次反法同盟：奥地利签订《普雷斯堡和约》，神圣罗马帝国于1806年解体。

sources.title: Robert Goetz, 1805: Austerlitz – Napoleon and the Destruction of the Third Coalition (2005)
David G. Chandler, The Campaigns of Napoleon (1966)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata (the Pratzen area east of Brno).

story.en:
After trapping an Austrian army at Ulm in October, Napoleon occupied Vienna and pushed into Moravia, far from his bases. Facing about 85,000 Russians and Austrians with some 73,000 men, he set a trap: he abandoned the commanding Pratzen Heights and left his right wing deliberately weak, while Marshal Davout's corps raced up from Vienna, covering over 100 kilometres in about two days.

At dawn the allies came down from the heights to turn the French right. Napoleon waited until their centre was thin, then sent Soult's divisions up the slopes out of the valley mist just as the sun broke through, the "sun of Austerlitz" his veterans later toasted. By midday the allied army had been cut in two. Fleeing troops crossed frozen ponds to the south; Napoleon's claim that thousands drowned there was a wild exaggeration.

The allies lost about a third of their army. Austria signed the Treaty of Pressburg on 26 December, and in 1806 Francis gave up the title of Holy Roman Emperor. In London, William Pitt is said to have asked for the map of Europe to be rolled up.
story.zh:
10月在乌尔姆围歼一支奥军后，拿破仑占领维也纳，继而深入摩拉维亚，远离了补给基地。面对约8.5万俄奥联军，他手中只有约7.3万人，于是设下圈套：主动放弃居高临下的普拉岑高地，并有意让右翼显得薄弱，同时命达武军从维也纳急行军赶来，两天左右走了一百多公里。

黎明时分，联军走下高地，企图迂回法军右翼。拿破仑等到联军中路空虚，才命苏尔特的各师从谷地晨雾中冲上山坡，恰在此时阳光破雾而出，这便是老兵们日后举杯称颂的“奥斯特利茨的太阳”。到中午，联军已被拦腰截断。溃兵向南越过结冰的池塘逃命；拿破仑声称数千人溺毙于此，实属严重夸大。

联军损失约三分之一兵力。奥地利于12月26日签订《普雷斯堡和约》，1806年弗朗茨放弃神圣罗马皇帝称号。据说在伦敦，威廉·皮特让人把欧洲地图卷起来，说今后用不着了。

summary.en: After occupying Portugal in 1807, Napoleon forced the Spanish Bourbons to abdicate and made his brother Joseph king of Spain, provoking a national uprising in 1808. Spanish armies and guerrillas, with British and Portuguese forces under Wellington, tied down hundreds of thousands of French troops until Wellington's victory at Vitoria in 1813 drove them back across the Pyrenees.
summary.zh: 1807年占领葡萄牙后，拿破仑迫使西班牙波旁王室退位，立其兄约瑟夫为西班牙国王，激起1808年的全国起义。西班牙正规军和游击队，连同威灵顿统率的英葡联军，牵制了数十万法军，直到1813年威灵顿在维多利亚获胜，把法军赶回比利牛斯山以北。

label.en: Dos de Mayo uprising in Madrid

sources.title: Charles Esdaile, The Peninsular War: A New History (2002)

note: The year follows the French invasion of Portugal (October–November 1807); Wikidata starts the war with the Madrid uprising of 2 May 1808, where the marker is placed, and ends it on 17 April 1814.

name.en: Opening of the Liverpool and Manchester Railway
name.zh: 利物浦—曼彻斯特铁路通车

summary.en: Opened on 15 September 1830, the Liverpool and Manchester Railway was the first inter-city line to run timetabled passenger and goods trains hauled entirely by steam locomotives. Engineered by George Stephenson, it showed that railways could pay and set off a railway boom; its opening day was marred by the death of the politician William Huskisson.
summary.zh: 利物浦—曼彻斯特铁路于1830年9月15日通车，是第一条完全以蒸汽机车牵引、按时刻表运行客货列车的城际铁路。它由乔治·斯蒂芬森主持修建，证明铁路有利可图，掀起了修建铁路的热潮。通车当天，政治家威廉·赫斯基森不幸遇难，给庆典蒙上阴影。

sources.title: Simon Garfield, The Last Journey of William Huskisson (2002)
Christian Wolmar, Fire and Steam: A New History of the Railways in Britain (2007)

note: Placed at the Manchester terminus, Liverpool Road station, which survives as part of the Science and Industry Museum. Wikidata's 1823 inception refers to the company.

story.en:
Liverpool merchants, tired of paying the canal companies' rates to move cotton to Manchester's mills, backed a railway between the two towns. George Stephenson's line needed bold engineering: a long cutting through rock at Olive Mount, a viaduct over the Sankey valley and a track floated across the bog of Chat Moss on rafts of brushwood and heather.

The directors were still unsure whether to use locomotives or stationary engines hauling cables, so in October 1829 they held trials at Rainhill. Rocket, built by George and his son Robert, was the only entrant to complete the test, reaching about 30 miles an hour.

The opening was a grand occasion attended by the prime minister, the Duke of Wellington. When the trains stopped to take water at Parkside, William Huskisson, MP for Liverpool, stepped down to greet Wellington and was struck by Rocket on the adjoining track. Stephenson rushed him to Eccles at record speed, but he died that night. Within weeks the line was carrying far more passengers than expected, and investors everywhere took note.
story.zh:
利物浦商人不愿再向运河公司支付高昂运费把棉花运往曼彻斯特的纺织厂，于是出资修建连接两城的铁路。乔治·斯蒂芬森设计的线路工程十分大胆：在奥利夫山开凿长长的岩石路堑，在桑基河谷架设高架桥，还在查特沼泽上用灌木枝和石南捆扎成的筏子把路基“浮”过泥沼。

董事们当时仍拿不准该用蒸汽机车还是用固定蒸汽机牵引钢缆，于是在1829年10月举办雷恩希尔机车大赛。乔治与儿子罗伯特制造的“火箭号”是唯一完成全部测试的参赛机车，时速约达30英里。

通车典礼十分隆重，首相威灵顿公爵亲临。列车在帕克赛德停车加水时，利物浦选出的议员威廉·赫斯基森下车去向威灵顿致意，被相邻轨道上驶来的“火箭号”撞倒。斯蒂芬森以创纪录的速度把他送往埃克尔斯，但他当晚仍不治身亡。通车后数周之内，客运量就远超预期，各地投资者都看在了眼里。

summary.en: Commissioned by the Communist League, a small society of mostly German émigré workers, and written by Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels in Brussels, the Manifesto of the Communist Party was printed in London in German in February 1848. It presented history as a story of class struggle and predicted that the proletariat would overthrow capitalism.
summary.zh: 《共产党宣言》受共产主义者同盟——一个以德国流亡工人为主的小团体——委托，由卡尔·马克思和弗里德里希·恩格斯在布鲁塞尔写成，1848年2月在伦敦以德文印行。它把历史描述为阶级斗争的历史，并预言无产阶级将推翻资本主义。

sources.title: Gareth Stedman Jones, introduction to The Communist Manifesto (Penguin Classics, 2002)

note: Placed at 46 Liverpool Street, Bishopsgate, where it was printed at the office of the German Workers' Educational Association. Exact publication day in February 1848 is uncertain, so no date is given.

story.en:
At its congress in London in late 1847, held in rooms above a Soho pub, the Communist League asked Marx and Engels to set out its principles. Engels had drafted a question-and-answer catechism, but Marx rewrote the whole thing as a manifesto in Brussels, so slowly that the League's leaders sent him an ultimatum in January 1848.

The pamphlet of 23 pages opens with the image of a spectre of communism haunting Europe and closes by calling on the workers of all countries to unite. In between it pays startling tribute to the bourgeoisie, which it says has transformed the world more than all previous generations, before arguing that capitalism creates its own gravediggers in the industrial working class.

It appeared within days of the revolution in Paris, but it had almost no influence on the upheavals of 1848. Its fame came later, with the growth of socialist parties after the 1870s and the English translation of 1888 edited by Engels. In the twentieth century it became one of the most widely read political texts ever written.
story.zh:
1847年底，共产主义者同盟在伦敦苏豪区一家酒馆楼上召开代表大会，委托马克思和恩格斯阐述同盟的原则。恩格斯先拟了一份问答体的纲领草稿，马克思却在布鲁塞尔把它全部改写成一篇宣言，进度之慢，以致同盟领导人在1848年1月向他下了最后通牒。

这本23页的小册子以“一个共产主义的幽灵在欧洲游荡”的意象开篇，以号召全世界无产者联合起来作结。其间它对资产阶级作出了惊人的赞颂，称其改变世界的力量超过以往一切世代的总和，进而论证资本主义在产业工人阶级中造就了自己的掘墓人。

宣言问世仅数日后巴黎便爆发革命，但它对1848年的动荡几乎毫无影响。它的盛名来得较晚：19世纪70年代以后社会主义政党兴起，1888年又出版了恩格斯审定的英译本。到20世纪，它已成为有史以来阅读最广的政治文本之一。

summary.en: In May 1860 Giuseppe Garibaldi sailed from near Genoa with about a thousand red-shirted volunteers to support a Sicilian revolt against the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies. Within five months they had taken Sicily and Naples; Garibaldi then handed his conquests to Victor Emmanuel II, opening the way to the Kingdom of Italy in 1861.
summary.zh: 1860年5月，朱塞佩·加里波第率领约一千名身穿红衫的志愿兵从热那亚附近出发，支援西西里人反抗波旁王朝两西西里王国的起义。五个月内，他们攻占了西西里和那不勒斯；随后加里波第把征服的土地交给维克托·伊曼纽尔二世，为1861年意大利王国的建立铺平了道路。

label.zh: 从热那亚附近的夸尔托出发

label.en: Crosses to the mainland at Melito
label.zh: 在梅利托渡海登陆本土

label.en: Meets Victor Emmanuel II near Teano
label.zh: 在泰阿诺附近会见维克托·伊曼纽尔二世

sources.title: Lucy Riall, Garibaldi: Invention of a Hero (2007)

note: Marker at Marsala, where the volunteers landed on 11 May 1860. The expedition sailed on the night of 5–6 May; the meeting near Teano was on 26 October.

story.en:
When Sicilians rose against their Bourbon king in April 1860, Garibaldi gathered volunteers at Genoa: students, artisans and veterans of 1848, most of them from the north. The Piedmontese prime minister, Cavour, neither stopped nor openly backed him. On the night of 5–6 May the volunteers seized two steamers at Quarto and slipped out to sea.

They landed at Marsala on 11 May and, outnumbered, won a hard fight at Calatafimi on 15 May, where Garibaldi is said to have told Nino Bixio that here they would make Italy or die. A popular rising helped them take Palermo, and by late July, after Milazzo, the island was theirs. Thousands of new recruits joined.

In August Garibaldi crossed the Strait of Messina. Naples fell almost without a fight, and he entered it by train on 7 September. After beating the Bourbon army on the Volturno, he met Victor Emmanuel near Teano on 26 October and greeted him as king of Italy. Refusing titles and rewards, he retired to his island farm on Caprera.
story.zh:
1860年4月西西里人起兵反抗波旁国王，加里波第在热那亚召集志愿兵，成员有学生、工匠和1848年革命的老兵，大多来自北方。皮埃蒙特首相加富尔对此既不阻止，也不公开支持。5月5日至6日夜，志愿兵在夸尔托夺取两艘轮船，悄然出海。

5月11日他们在马尔萨拉登陆，15日在卡拉塔菲米以寡敌众，苦战获胜；据说加里波第当时对尼诺·比克肖说，要么在这里缔造意大利，要么死在这里。在民众起义的配合下，他们攻下巴勒莫；7月下旬米拉佐一役后，全岛尽入其手，数以千计的新兵前来投奔。

8月，加里波第渡过墨西拿海峡。那不勒斯几乎不战而下，他于9月7日乘火车入城。在沃尔图诺河击败波旁军队后，他于10月26日在泰阿诺附近会见维克托·伊曼纽尔，尊其为意大利国王。他谢绝了一切封号和赏赐，回到卡普雷拉岛上的农庄隐居。

summary.en: After France's defeat by Prussia, Parisians resisted the national government's attempt to seize the National Guard's cannon on 18 March 1871 and elected a revolutionary Commune. It governed the city for about ten weeks, until government troops retook Paris during the "Bloody Week" of 21–28 May, killing thousands of Communards.
summary.zh: 普法战争中法国战败后，1871年3月18日巴黎民众抵制国民政府收缴国民自卫军大炮的行动，随后选举产生了革命性的公社。公社治理巴黎约十周，直至政府军在5月21日至28日的“流血周”中夺回巴黎，杀害了数以千计的公社社员。

sources.title: John Merriman, Massacre: The Life and Death of the Paris Commune (2014)

note: Placed at the Hôtel de Ville, seat of the Commune. The rising began on 18 March; the Commune was elected on 26 March. Death tolls for Bloody Week are disputed: older estimates of 10,000–20,000 or more, while Robert Tombs argues for roughly 6,000–7,500.

story.en:
Paris had endured a four-month Prussian siege and felt betrayed by the armistice. The new National Assembly, dominated by monarchists and led by Adolphe Thiers, ended the National Guard's pay and the moratorium on rents and debts. Before dawn on 18 March troops were sent to remove the Guard's cannon from Montmartre. Crowds surrounded them, soldiers refused to fire, and two generals were killed. Thiers withdrew the government to Versailles.

The Commune elected on 26 March separated church and state, banned night work in bakeries, suspended rent arrears and opened abandoned workshops to cooperatives. Women such as Louise Michel played prominent roles. On 16 May Communards pulled down the Vendôme Column as a monument to militarism.

The army broke in on 21 May. In a week of street fighting, troops shot prisoners in large numbers, while Communards executed hostages, including the archbishop of Paris, and set fire to the Tuileries and the Hôtel de Ville. The last fighters were shot against a wall in Père Lachaise cemetery. Marx hailed the Commune as the first workers' government, and it became a lasting legend of the left.
story.zh:
巴黎刚刚熬过普鲁士军队长达四个月的围困，民众认为停战是一种背叛。新选出的国民议会由君主派主导，以阿道夫·梯也尔为首，它停发国民自卫军的军饷，并取消了房租和债务的延期偿付。3月18日拂晓前，政府派兵去蒙马特高地收缴自卫军的大炮。民众团团围住军队，士兵拒绝开枪，两名将军被杀。梯也尔把政府撤往凡尔赛。

3月26日选出的公社宣布政教分离，禁止面包房夜间作业，暂停追缴拖欠的房租，并把业主弃置的作坊交给合作社经营。路易丝·米歇尔等女性发挥了突出作用。5月16日，公社社员推倒了旺多姆圆柱，视之为军国主义的象征。

5月21日政府军攻入城内。在一周的巷战中，军队大批枪杀俘虏；公社方面也处决了包括巴黎大主教在内的人质，并纵火焚烧杜伊勒里宫和市政厅。最后一批战士在拉雪兹神父公墓的一堵墙前被枪决。马克思称公社为第一个工人政府，它也成为左翼经久不衰的传奇。

name.zh: 爱因斯坦提出狭义相对论

summary.en: In "On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies", published in Annalen der Physik in September 1905, Albert Einstein, then a 26-year-old examiner at the Swiss patent office in Bern, showed that if the speed of light is the same for all observers, measurements of time and space depend on motion. A short follow-up paper that year derived E = mc².
summary.zh: 1905年9月，时年26岁、在伯尔尼瑞士专利局任审查员的阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦在《物理学年鉴》上发表《论动体的电动力学》。他证明，如果光速对所有观察者都相同，那么时间和空间的测量结果便取决于运动状态。同年稍后的一篇短文推导出了E=mc²。

sources.title: Albert Einstein, "Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper", Annalen der Physik 17 (1905): 891–921
Abraham Pais, 'Subtle is the Lord': The Science and the Life of Albert Einstein (1982)

note: Placed at Kramgasse 49, Bern, the flat where Einstein lived in 1903–1905 (now the Einsteinhaus). The paper was received by the journal on 30 June 1905 and published on 26 September.

story.en:
Physicists in 1905 believed light travelled through an invisible ether, yet experiments had failed to detect Earth's motion through it. Einstein cut the knot with two postulates: the laws of physics are the same for all observers moving uniformly, and the speed of light in a vacuum is the same for all of them. The ether, he wrote, was simply superfluous.

The consequences were startling. Events simultaneous for one observer are not for another; moving clocks run slow and moving rods shrink along their motion. Hendrik Lorentz and Henri Poincaré had found much of the mathematics, but Einstein reinterpreted it as a new account of space and time itself.

He worked this out in his spare time while examining patents in Bern, talking ideas over with his friend Michele Besso, the only person thanked in the paper, which cites no other literature. It was one of four papers of his "miraculous year". Max Planck took it up quickly; later experiments with fast-moving particles and precise clocks confirmed it, and in 1915 Einstein extended it into general relativity.
story.zh:
1905年的物理学家普遍相信光在一种看不见的“以太”中传播，然而实验始终测不出地球相对以太的运动。爱因斯坦用两条公设快刀斩乱麻：对一切匀速运动的观察者，物理定律都相同；真空中的光速对他们也都相同。他写道，以太根本是多余的。

由此得出的推论令人震惊：对一位观察者同时发生的事件，对另一位观察者却未必同时；运动的时钟走得更慢，运动的尺子沿运动方向缩短。洛伦兹和庞加莱已经得出了其中大部分数学形式，但爱因斯坦把它重新诠释为关于时间与空间本身的新理论。

这些都是他在伯尔尼审查专利之余推敲出来的，常与好友米歇尔·贝索讨论；贝索是论文中唯一被致谢的人，而论文没有引用任何文献。这是他“奇迹年”发表的四篇论文之一。马克斯·普朗克很快予以重视；后来对高速粒子和精密时钟的实验都证实了这一理论，1915年爱因斯坦又将其推广为广义相对论。

summary.en: The Parliament Act of 1906, confirmed by Nicholas II as Grand Duke of Finland on 20 July, replaced the four-estate Diet with a single chamber elected by all citizens aged 24 and over. Finnish women became the first in Europe to vote and, in March 1907, the first anywhere elected to a national parliament, winning 19 of 200 seats.
summary.zh: 1906年7月20日，尼古拉二世以芬兰大公身份批准《议会法》，以全体24岁以上公民选举产生的一院制议会取代原有的四等级议会。芬兰妇女由此成为欧洲最早享有选举权的女性；1907年3月，又成为世界上最早当选国家议会议员的女性，在200个议席中赢得19席。

sources.title: Parliament of Finland: Women's suffrage 110 years – Historical background
Library of Congress, In Custodia Legis: 115 Years of Women Being Members of Parliament in Finland (2022)
Irma Sulkunen, Seija-Leena Nevala-Nurmi and Pirjo Markkola (eds.), Suffrage, Gender and Citizenship: International Perspectives on Parliamentary Reforms (2009)

note: Finland was then an autonomous grand duchy of the Russian Empire (no separate polity id). Placed at the House of the Estates (Säätytalo), Helsinki, where the old Diet approved the reform on 1 June 1906; the date shown is the emperor's confirmation. New Zealand (1893) and Australia (1902) enfranchised women earlier, but Finland was the first to elect women MPs. The QID is the Finnish-language item "eduskuntauudistus 1906" (no English label).

story.en:
Finland had kept its own laws and Diet under Russian rule, but from 1899 the tsar's officials tried to Russify it. Russia's defeat by Japan and the revolution of 1905 gave Finns their chance: a general strike in the autumn of 1905 forced Nicholas II to restore Finnish autonomy and promise a new representative system.

Women's organisations, both middle-class associations and the growing working-class movement, had campaigned for the vote for years, and the Social Democrats insisted on it. The reform committee proposed universal and equal suffrage for men and women alike, including the right to stand for election. In 1906 the old Diet of four estates, nobility, clergy, burghers and peasants, voted itself out of existence.

The electorate grew roughly tenfold. In the election of 15–16 March 1907, 19 women won seats, most of them Social Democrats, among them the reformer Lucina Hagman and the former maid Miina Sillanpää, who later became Finland's first woman minister. Norway followed in 1913 and Denmark in 1915.
story.zh:
在俄国统治下，芬兰一直保有自己的法律和议会，但从1899年起，沙皇的官员试图推行俄罗斯化。俄国在日俄战争中失败以及1905年革命给了芬兰人机会：1905年秋的总罢工迫使尼古拉二世恢复芬兰自治，并承诺建立新的代议制度。

妇女团体——既有中产阶级协会，也有日益壮大的工人阶级妇女运动——多年来一直争取选举权，社会民主党也坚持这一要求。改革委员会提出男女一律享有普遍、平等的选举权和被选举权。1906年，由贵族、教士、市民和农民组成的旧四等级议会投票通过改革，结束了自己的历史。

选民人数增加了大约十倍。在1907年3月15日至16日的选举中，19名女性当选，大多来自社会民主党，其中有改革家露西娜·哈格曼，以及女仆出身、后来成为芬兰首位女部长的米娜·西兰帕。挪威于1913年、丹麦于1915年相继效仿。

summary.en: Between 6 and 12 September 1914 French and British forces counter-attacked German armies that had swept through Belgium to within about 50 km of Paris, exploiting a gap between the German First and Second Armies. The Germans fell back to the Aisne, their hope of quick victory in the west was lost, and the front settled into trenches.
summary.zh: 1914年9月6日至12日，英法军队向席卷比利时、推进到距巴黎约50公里处的德军发起反击，利用德军第一与第二集团军之间出现的缺口展开攻势。德军退至埃纳河一线，在西线速战速决的希望破灭，西线由此转入堑壕战。

sources.title: Britannica: First Battle of the Marne
Holger H. Herwig, The Marne, 1914: The Opening of World War I and the Battle That Changed the World (2009)
Wikipedia: First Battle of the Marne

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata. Wikidata gives 8–12 September; most accounts date the battle from 5–6 September, when fighting began on the Ourcq.

story.en:
Germany's war plan staked everything on swinging through Belgium and defeating France within weeks. By early September the French and the small British Expeditionary Force had retreated for almost two weeks, and the government had left Paris for Bordeaux. But General von Kluck's First Army, on the German right, turned south-east to chase the retreating French and passed east of Paris, exposing its flank.

General Gallieni, military governor of Paris, saw the chance, and the French commander-in-chief Joseph Joffre ordered a general counter-offensive, telling his men there must be no more retreat. Maunoury's Sixth Army struck Kluck on the Ourcq; famously, part of a division was rushed forward in several hundred Paris taxis, a gesture more symbolic than decisive. As Kluck turned to meet the threat, a gap opened between his army and Bülow's, and the British and French pushed into it.

On 9 September a staff officer, Lieutenant-Colonel Richard Hentsch, sanctioned a German withdrawal. The armies then tried to outflank each other northward in the "race to the sea", and by November trenches ran from the Channel to Switzerland.
story.zh:
德国的作战计划把一切押在取道比利时、数周内击败法国上。到9月初，法军和规模不大的英国远征军已连续后撤近两周，法国政府也从巴黎迁往波尔多。然而德军右翼克卢克将军的第一集团军为追击后撤的法军转向东南，从巴黎以东经过，把侧翼暴露了出来。

巴黎军事总督加利埃尼看到了战机，法军总司令霞飞随即下令全线反攻，告诫部下决不能再后退。莫努里的第六集团军在乌尔克河猛击克卢克的部队；广为传颂的是，部分援军乘坐数百辆巴黎出租车赶赴前线，但这更多是象征意义而非决定性因素。克卢克回师迎战，他与比洛的第二集团军之间随即出现缺口，英法军队乘虚而入。

9月9日，德军参谋军官里夏德·亨奇中校批准撤退。此后双方竞相向北迂回对方侧翼，形成“奔向大海”的竞赛；到11月，堑壕已从英吉利海峡一直延伸到瑞士边境。

summary.en: From 21 February to 18 December 1916 German and French armies fought around the fortress city of Verdun in the longest battle of the First World War. After ten months and about 700,000 casualties, including some 300,000 dead, the front line stood close to where it had begun, and Verdun became France's symbol of endurance.
summary.zh: 1916年2月21日至12月18日，德法两军围绕要塞城市凡尔登展开了第一次世界大战中历时最长的战役。十个月的鏖战造成约70万人伤亡，其中约30万人阵亡，战线却几乎回到了原点。凡尔登由此成为法国坚韧不屈的象征。

sources.title: Alistair Horne, The Price of Glory: Verdun 1916 (1962)
Paul Jankowski, Verdun: The Longest Battle of the Great War (2013)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata (the battlefield north-east of Verdun). Casualty figures vary by source.

story.en:
The German chief of staff, Erich von Falkenhayn, chose Verdun, a salient ringed by forts that France could not afford to lose. After the war he claimed he had meant to bleed the French army white there; historians doubt the memorandum he cited ever existed and suspect a justification after the fact. The attack opened on 21 February with a bombardment by more than a thousand guns, and on 25 February the great Fort Douaumont fell almost without a fight to a handful of German soldiers.

General Philippe Pétain took command and organised the defence. A single road from Bar-le-Duc, later called the Voie Sacrée, carried a constant stream of lorries with men and shells, and a rotation of divisions meant that most of the French army served at Verdun at some point. General Robert Nivelle's order of the day, "They shall not pass", became the battle's motto.

German pressure eased after the Somme offensive began in July, and French counter-attacks retook Douaumont in October. Nine villages destroyed in the fighting were never rebuilt. In 1984 President Mitterrand and Chancellor Kohl held hands at the Douaumont ossuary.
story.zh:
德军总参谋长埃里希·冯·法金汉选中了凡尔登——一个被要塞环绕、法国绝不能丢失的突出部。战后他声称，自己的意图是在那里让法军“流尽鲜血”；但历史学家怀疑他所引用的那份备忘录是否真的存在，认为那多半是事后的自我辩解。2月21日，德军以一千多门火炮的炮击发起进攻；2月25日，宏伟的杜奥蒙堡几乎未经抵抗就落入一小队德军之手。

菲利普·贝当将军接掌指挥，组织防御。一条从巴勒迪克通来的公路——后来被称为“圣路”——上满载兵员和炮弹的卡车川流不息；各师轮番上阵，使法军大部分部队都曾在凡尔登作战。罗贝尔·尼维勒将军在日令中写下的“他们休想通过”成了这场战役的口号。

7月索姆河攻势打响后，德军的压力有所减轻；10月法军反攻夺回杜奥蒙堡。战火中被毁的九个村庄再也没有重建。1984年，密特朗总统与科尔总理在杜奥蒙藏骨堂前手拉着手。

summary.en: Launched by British and French armies on 1 July 1916, partly to relieve Verdun, the Somme offensive cost the British Army 57,470 casualties, nearly 20,000 of them killed, on its first day, the worst in its history. By mid-November the Allies had advanced about 10 km, and total casualties on both sides exceeded one million.
summary.zh: 1916年7月1日，英法军队发起索姆河攻势，部分目的是为凡尔登解围。仅第一天英军就伤亡57470人，其中近两万人阵亡，是英军史上最惨痛的一天。到11月中旬，协约国军队仅推进约10公里，双方伤亡总数超过一百万。

sources.title: William Philpott, Bloody Victory: The Sacrifice on the Somme and the Making of the Twentieth Century (2009)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata. The offensive ended on 18 November (Britannica says 13 November); total casualty estimates are disputed.

story.en:
The offensive was planned as the main Allied blow of 1916, but Verdun drained French divisions and left the British, under Sir Douglas Haig, to carry most of the attack. For a week some 1.5 million shells were fired at the German lines, yet many were duds, and the bombardment neither cut the barbed wire nor destroyed the deep dugouts where German machine-gunners waited.

At 7.28 on the morning of 1 July huge mines, including the one at Lochnagar near La Boisselle, were blown, and two minutes later the infantry went over the top. Across much of the front they were cut down. Many units were "Pals" battalions of friends and neighbours who had enlisted together, so single towns lost a generation of young men in an afternoon. The French, attacking further south, did much better.

The battle ground on for four and a half months. On 15 September tanks went into action for the first time, at Flers-Courcelette. Historians still argue whether the Somme was futile slaughter or a costly lesson that wore down the German army; the Thiepval Memorial lists over 72,000 missing.
story.zh:
这次攻势原本计划作为协约国1916年的主要打击，但凡尔登战役消耗了大量法军师团，进攻重任大多落在道格拉斯·黑格爵士指挥的英军身上。整整一周，约150万发炮弹倾泻在德军阵地上，但其中许多是哑弹，炮击既没有切断铁丝网，也没能摧毁深藏地下的掩蔽部，德军机枪手就在那里等待。

7月1日早晨7时28分，包括拉布瓦塞勒附近洛赫纳加尔坑道在内的巨型地雷被引爆，两分钟后步兵跃出堑壕。在大部分战线上，他们成片倒下。许多部队是由朋友和邻居结伴参军组成的“伙伴营”，一个下午之间，一座小镇就可能失去整整一代青年。在南面进攻的法军则战果好得多。

战役又持续了四个半月。9月15日，坦克在弗莱尔—库尔瑟莱特首次投入实战。历史学家至今仍在争论，索姆河战役究竟是一场徒劳的屠杀，还是一次代价高昂却拖垮了德军的教训；蒂耶普瓦尔纪念碑上刻着七万二千多名失踪者的名字。

summary.en: Receiving royal assent on 6 February 1918, the Representation of the People Act gave the vote to almost all men over 21 and to women over 30 who met a property qualification, nearly tripling the electorate and enfranchising about 8.4 million women. Women won the vote on the same terms as men only with the Equal Franchise Act of 1928.
summary.zh: 《人民代表法》于1918年2月6日获御准，赋予几乎所有21岁以上男子以及符合财产条件的30岁以上女性选举权，使选民人数增加近两倍，约840万女性获得投票权。直到1928年《平等选举权法》通过，女性才获得与男性同等的选举权。

sources.title: UK Parliament, Living Heritage: Women and the vote
June Purvis, Emmeline Pankhurst: A Biography (2002)

note: Placed at the Palace of Westminster. A separate act of November 1918 let women stand for Parliament. The Equal Franchise Act (July 1928) passed weeks after Emmeline Pankhurst's death on 14 June 1928.

summary.en: In late October 1922 tens of thousands of Fascist Blackshirts converged on Rome. When King Victor Emmanuel III refused on 28 October to sign Prime Minister Luigi Facta's decree of martial law, the government collapsed, and on 30 October the king asked Benito Mussolini to form a government, opening two decades of Fascist rule.
summary.zh: 1922年10月下旬，数万名法西斯黑衫党徒向罗马集结。10月28日，国王维克托·伊曼纽尔三世拒绝签署首相路易吉·法克塔的戒严令，政府随即垮台；10月30日国王授命贝尼托·墨索里尼组阁，意大利由此开始了长达二十年的法西斯统治。

sources.title: Britannica: Benito Mussolini – Rise to power
Adrian Lyttelton, The Seizure of Power: Fascism in Italy, 1919–1929 (1973)

note: Placed at the Quirinal Palace, the royal residence. Mussolini waited in Milan and arrived by overnight train on 30 October; the Blackshirts paraded through Rome only after his appointment, on 31 October.

summary.en: On 30 January 1933 President Paul von Hindenburg appointed Adolf Hitler chancellor of a coalition cabinet that conservatives expected to control. Within months the Reichstag Fire Decree and the Enabling Act let the Nazis suspend civil liberties, ban other parties and rule by decree; by August 1934 Hitler was dictator as Führer.
summary.zh: 1933年1月30日，兴登堡总统任命阿道夫·希特勒为联合内阁总理，保守派原以为能够驾驭他。短短数月内，《国会纵火法令》和《授权法》使纳粹得以中止公民自由、取缔其他政党并以法令治国；到1934年8月，希特勒已作为“元首”成为独裁者。

sources.title: Richard J. Evans, The Coming of the Third Reich (2003)

note: Placed at the Reich Chancellery on Wilhelmstrasse, Berlin. The span ends with Hindenburg's death on 2 August 1934, when Hitler merged the offices of president and chancellor.

story.en:
The Nazis won 37 per cent of the vote in July 1932, then lost ground in November. Backroom intrigue, not an election, brought Hitler to power: the former chancellor Franz von Papen persuaded the aged Hindenburg to appoint him at the head of a cabinet in which only two other ministers were Nazis. Papen reportedly boasted that within months they would have Hitler cornered. That night SA men marched with torches through the Brandenburg Gate.

On 27 February the Reichstag burned, and a young Dutch communist, Marinus van der Lubbe, was arrested. The next day a decree suspended basic rights, and thousands of communists were rounded up. On 23 March, in the Kroll Opera House, the Reichstag passed the Enabling Act by 441 votes to 94, with SA men lining the hall; only the Social Democrats voted against.

Trade unions were abolished in May and all other parties dissolved by July; the first concentration camp opened at Dachau in March. In the Night of the Long Knives (30 June 1934) Hitler had SA leaders and other rivals murdered, and when Hindenburg died the army swore an oath to Hitler personally.
story.zh:
1932年7月，纳粹党以37%的得票率成为国会第一大党，11月的选举中又有所退步。把希特勒推上台的不是选举，而是幕后交易：前总理弗朗茨·冯·巴本说服年迈的兴登堡任命希特勒出任总理，内阁中除他之外只有两名纳粹部长。据说巴本夸口，几个月内就能把希特勒逼进死角。当晚，冲锋队员举着火把列队穿过勃兰登堡门。

2月27日国会大厦起火，年轻的荷兰共产党人马里纳斯·范德卢贝被捕。次日一道法令中止了基本权利，数以千计的共产党人遭到搜捕。3月23日，国会在克罗尔歌剧院以441票对94票通过《授权法》，会场四周站满了冲锋队员；只有社会民主党投了反对票。

5月工会被取缔，到7月其他政党全部解散；3月，第一座集中营已在达豪启用。1934年6月30日“长刀之夜”，希特勒下令杀害冲锋队首领和其他政敌；兴登堡去世后，军队向希特勒个人宣誓效忠。

summary.en: A military rising against Spain's elected Popular Front government in July 1936 split the country into Republican and Nationalist zones. Backed by Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy, General Francisco Franco's Nationalists defeated the Republic, which was aided by the Soviet Union and the International Brigades, in April 1939, after a war that killed perhaps half a million people.
summary.zh: 1936年7月，军队发动叛乱反对民选的人民阵线政府，西班牙分裂为共和派和国民派两大区域。在纳粹德国和法西斯意大利支持下，弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥将军率领的国民军于1939年4月击败了得到苏联和国际纵队援助的共和国。这场战争可能造成约50万人死亡。

label.zh: 梅利利亚（西属摩洛哥）军队起事

label.en: Army of Africa airlifted to Seville
label.zh: 非洲军团空运至塞维利亚

sources.title: Paul Preston, The Spanish Civil War: Reaction, Revolution and Revenge (2006)
Antony Beevor, The Battle for Spain: The Spanish Civil War 1936–1939 (2006)

note: Marker at Madrid, besieged from November 1936 until its fall in March 1939. The rising began in Melilla on 17 July 1936 (Wikidata gives 18 July, when it spread to the mainland). Death toll estimates vary widely.

story.en:
The generals who rose in July 1936 expected a quick coup. It failed in Madrid, Barcelona and much of the industrial north, where workers' militias took up arms, and Spain split in two. Franco's Army of Africa, the best troops in the country, was stranded in Morocco until German and Italian aircraft flew it across the Strait of Gibraltar, one of the first large military airlifts.
