By November the Nationalists reached Madrid. The city held, rallied by the communist Dolores Ibárruri's cry of "No pasarán" and helped by the first International Brigades, volunteers from dozens of countries. Britain and France stuck to non-intervention while Germany and Italy sent planes, tanks and troops and the Soviet Union supplied the Republic in return for its gold reserves. Behind both lines there were mass killings; the Republic was also torn by conflict between communists and anarchists, described by George Orwell in Homage to Catalonia.

The Republic's last great offensive, on the Ebro in 1938, was beaten back. Barcelona fell in January 1939, and hundreds of thousands of refugees fled into France. Franco declared the war over on 1 April, and repression continued for years.
story.zh:
1936年7月起事的将军们本以为一场速战速决的政变即可成功。然而政变在马德里、巴塞罗那和北方大部分工业区失败，那里的工人民兵拿起了武器，西班牙一分为二。佛朗哥的非洲军团是全国最精锐的部队，却被困在摩洛哥，直到德国和意大利的飞机把它运过直布罗陀海峡，这是最早的大规模军事空运之一。

11月国民军兵临马德里。共产党人多洛雷斯·伊巴露丽喊出“他们休想通过”，第一批国际纵队——来自数十个国家的志愿者——赶来增援，马德里守住了。英法坚持“不干涉”政策，德意则派出飞机、坦克和军队；苏联向共和国提供援助，换取了西班牙的黄金储备。双方后方都发生了大规模杀戮；共和国内部还因共产党人与无政府主义者的冲突而四分五裂，乔治·奥威尔在《向加泰罗尼亚致敬》中记录了这一切。

1938年共和国在埃布罗河发动的最后一次大攻势被击退。1939年1月巴塞罗那陷落，数十万难民逃往法国。4月1日佛朗哥宣布战争结束，此后的镇压又持续了多年。

summary.en: On the afternoon of 26 April 1937, a market day, aircraft of Germany's Condor Legion, with Italian support, bombed the Basque town of Guernica for Franco's Nationalists and destroyed much of it. Estimates of the dead range from under 300 to over 1,600. Picasso's painting made it a lasting symbol of the bombing of civilians.
summary.zh: 1937年4月26日下午，正值集市日，德国秃鹰军团的飞机在意大利空军配合下，为佛朗哥的国民军轰炸了巴斯克小镇格尔尼卡，镇子大半被毁。死亡人数的估计从不足300人到1600余人不等。毕加索的画作使它成为平民遭受轰炸的永恒象征。

sources.title: Ian Patterson, Guernica and Total War (2007)

note: Wikidata gives 27 April as the point in time; the raid took place on the afternoon and evening of 26 April 1937. The death toll is disputed: the Basque government reported 1,654 at the time, while most recent historians favour a few hundred (roughly 150–300).

summary.en: On 9–10 November 1938 Nazi Party members, SA and SS men and others attacked Jews across Germany, annexed Austria and the Sudetenland, burning hundreds of synagogues, wrecking some 7,500 Jewish shops and killing at least 91 people. About 30,000 Jewish men were sent to concentration camps, marking a turn to open, organised violence.
summary.zh: 1938年11月9日至10日，纳粹党员、冲锋队、党卫队成员和其他人在德国全境以及刚被吞并的奥地利和苏台德地区袭击犹太人，焚毁数百座犹太会堂，捣毁约7500家犹太商店，至少91人遇害。约三万名犹太男子被送进集中营，标志着迫害转向公开、有组织的暴力。

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Holocaust Encyclopedia: Kristallnacht

note: Placed at the New Synagogue on Oranienburger Strasse, Berlin. The pogrom was set off from Munich. Figures follow standard references (Heydrich's first report listed 267 synagogues destroyed; later research puts the number of synagogues and prayer rooms attacked far higher, and the death toll including suicides and deaths in the camps in the hundreds).

story.en:
In late October 1938 Germany expelled thousands of Polish-born Jews across the border. Among them were the parents of Herschel Grynszpan, a 17-year-old living in Paris, who on 7 November shot the German diplomat Ernst vom Rath. Vom Rath died on 9 November, as Nazi leaders gathered in Munich for the anniversary of the 1923 putsch. With Hitler's approval, Joseph Goebbels gave a speech that party leaders understood as the signal for "spontaneous" revenge.

Orders went out by telephone through the night. Police were told not to interfere, and fire brigades to protect only neighbouring non-Jewish buildings. Synagogues were set alight, homes and shops smashed and men beaten and arrested. In Berlin, a local police chief, Wilhelm Krützfeld, is credited with driving arsonists away from the New Synagogue and calling the fire brigade.

Afterwards the regime made the victims pay: Jews were fined one billion Reichsmarks, their insurance claims were confiscated and they were driven from economic life. The name, after the shattered glass that littered the streets, is now often replaced in Germany by "November pogroms". Desperate emigration followed, including the Kindertransport that took about 10,000 children to Britain.
story.zh:
1938年10月下旬，德国把数千名出生于波兰的犹太人驱逐出境。其中有一对夫妇的儿子赫舍尔·格林斯潘时年17岁，住在巴黎；11月7日，他开枪打伤了德国外交官恩斯特·冯·拉特。11月9日冯·拉特身亡，此时纳粹领导人正聚集在慕尼黑纪念1923年啤酒馆政变。经希特勒同意，约瑟夫·戈培尔发表讲话，党内头目都把它理解为发动“自发”报复的信号。

命令连夜通过电话层层下达。警察奉命不得干预，消防队只负责保护相邻的非犹太人建筑。犹太会堂被纵火焚烧，住宅和商店被砸毁，男人们遭到殴打和逮捕。在柏林，一位名叫威廉·克吕茨费尔德的辖区警长据信赶走了在新犹太会堂纵火的人，并叫来了消防队。

事后，当局反而要受害者买单：犹太人被罚款十亿帝国马克，保险赔偿被没收，并被彻底逐出经济生活。“水晶之夜”之名来自满街碎玻璃，如今德国人多改称“十一月大迫害”。随后出现了绝望的移民潮，其中包括把约一万名儿童送往英国的“儿童转移”行动。

summary.en: Between 26 May and 4 June 1940 Operation Dynamo evacuated about 338,000 British, French and Belgian troops from the harbour and beaches of Dunkirk as German armies closed in. Destroyers carried most of them, helped by hundreds of small civilian boats. The army's escape let Britain fight on, though almost all its heavy equipment was lost.
summary.zh: 1940年5月26日至6月4日，在德军步步紧逼之际，“发电机行动”从敦刻尔克港口和海滩撤出了约33.8万名英、法、比军人。大部分官兵由驱逐舰运走，数百艘民用小船也参与了接运。军队得以脱险，英国才能继续作战，但几乎所有重装备都丢弃在了法国。

sources.title: Hugh Sebag-Montefiore, Dunkirk: Fight to the Last Man (2006)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata (Dunkirk harbour and beaches). Totals usually cited are about 338,000 (roughly 198,000 British and 140,000 French and Belgian).

story.en:
German armour broke through the Ardennes at Sedan in mid-May 1940 and raced to the Channel, trapping the British Expeditionary Force and much of the French army in a shrinking pocket around Dunkirk. On 24 May Hitler approved an order halting the tanks for about three days, a decision still debated; Göring had promised that the Luftwaffe could finish the job.

From tunnels beneath Dover Castle, Vice-Admiral Bertram Ramsay ran the rescue. The Admiralty hoped to save perhaps 45,000 men. Most were taken off from the long East Mole of the harbour by destroyers and other large ships, while yachts, ferries, fishing boats and pleasure craft, the "little ships", ferried soldiers from the shallow beaches. French troops held the perimeter to the end, and tens of thousands of them were captured when it fell on 4 June.

That day Churchill told the Commons that the nation would fight on the beaches and never surrender, but warned that wars are not won by evacuations. The "Dunkirk spirit" entered British folklore.
story.zh:
1940年5月中旬，德军装甲部队在色当突破阿登山区，直扑英吉利海峡，把英国远征军和大部分法军困在敦刻尔克周围日益缩小的包围圈里。5月24日，希特勒批准坦克部队停止前进约三天，这一决定至今仍有争论；戈林曾保证空军就能完成歼灭任务。

伯特伦·拉姆齐海军中将在多佛城堡地下的隧道里指挥这次营救。海军部原本只希望救出大约4.5万人。大多数官兵由驱逐舰和其他大型船只从港口长长的东防波堤上接走，而游艇、渡轮、渔船和游船——即所谓“小船”——则把士兵从浅滩上摆渡出去。法军坚守防线直到最后，6月4日防线失守时，数以万计的法军被俘。

当天，丘吉尔在下院宣布，英国将在海滩上战斗、决不投降，但他也提醒说，战争不是靠撤退打赢的。“敦刻尔克精神”从此成为英国民间传奇。

summary.en: From July to October 1940 the Luftwaffe tried to win air superiority over southern England as a prelude to invasion. RAF Fighter Command, guided by radar and a ground-control network, held out, and in September Hitler postponed the invasion indefinitely. Germany turned to night bombing of cities, the Blitz, which killed over 40,000 civilians by May 1941.
summary.zh: 1940年7月至10月，德国空军试图夺取英格兰南部上空的制空权，为入侵作准备。英国皇家空军战斗机司令部依靠雷达和地面指挥网络顽强坚守；9月，希特勒无限期推迟了入侵计划。德国转而对城市实施夜间轰炸，即“闪电空袭”，到1941年5月已造成四万多名平民死亡。

sources.title: Richard Overy, The Battle of Britain: The Myth and the Reality (2000)

note: Placed at Bentley Priory, north-west London, headquarters of RAF Fighter Command (Wikidata gives only a generic point in Britain). Dates follow the official British span of 10 July–31 October 1940; the Blitz lasted from 7 September 1940 to May 1941.

story.en:
After France fell, Hitler ordered preparations for Operation Sea Lion, a landing in southern England that would be possible only if the RAF was beaten first. The Luftwaffe attacked Channel convoys in July and then, from mid-August, airfields and radar stations. Britain had slightly more than 600 front-line fighters, but its Chain Home radar stations, the Observer Corps and the control rooms of Air Chief Marshal Hugh Dowding's system let it send Hurricanes and Spitfires exactly where they were needed. Pilots came from across the Commonwealth and occupied Europe; the Polish 303 Squadron was among the highest scoring.

On 20 August Churchill told Parliament that never had so much been owed by so many to so few. By early September Fighter Command was badly stretched, but on 7 September the Germans switched to bombing London. Their great daylight raids of 15 September were beaten off, and two days later the invasion was postponed.

The Blitz continued by night. London was bombed on 57 consecutive nights, Coventry was devastated in November, and in the raid of 29 December St Paul's Cathedral survived amid the flames. Londoners sheltered in Underground stations until the raids eased in May 1941.
story.zh:
法国沦陷后，希特勒下令筹备“海狮行动”，即在英格兰南部登陆，而这只有在先击败皇家空军之后才有可能。7月德国空军袭击英吉利海峡的护航船队，8月中旬起又转而轰炸机场和雷达站。英国的一线战斗机只有六百余架，但凭借“本土链”雷达站、皇家观察队以及休·道丁空军上将所建体系中的指挥室，它能把“飓风”和“喷火”战斗机准确派往最需要的地方。飞行员来自英联邦各地和被占领的欧洲国家，波兰第303中队是战绩最高的中队之一。

8月20日，丘吉尔在议会说，在人类战争史上，从未有过这么多人对这么少的人欠下如此深重的恩情。到9月初，战斗机司令部已疲于应付，但9月7日德军转而轰炸伦敦。9月15日德军的大规模昼间空袭被击退，两天后入侵计划被推迟。

夜间的闪电空袭仍在继续。伦敦连续57个夜晚遭到轰炸，考文垂在11月被夷为废墟；12月29日的空袭中，圣保罗大教堂在火海中屹立不倒。伦敦市民躲进地铁站避难，直到1941年5月空袭才逐渐减少。

summary.en: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murdered about six million European Jews, two-thirds of Europe's prewar Jewish population, along with Roma, disabled people, Soviet prisoners of war and others. Persecution began in 1933; systematic mass murder began with shootings in the occupied Soviet Union in 1941 and extended to death camps such as Auschwitz-Birkenau.
summary.zh: 纳粹德国及其合作者杀害了约六百万欧洲犹太人，占战前欧洲犹太人口的三分之二，同时遇害的还有罗姆人、残疾人、苏军战俘等群体。迫害始于1933年；1941年在被占领的苏联境内开始大规模枪杀，有计划的屠杀随后扩展到奥斯威辛—比克瑙等灭绝营。

sources.title: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum, Holocaust Encyclopedia: Introduction to the Holocaust
Raul Hilberg, The Destruction of the European Jews (3rd ed., 2003)
Saul Friedländer, The Years of Extermination: Nazi Germany and the Jews, 1939–1945 (2007)

note: Persecution of Jews in Germany began in 1933 (Wikidata dates the Holocaust 1933–1945); this record's 1941–1945 span covers the systematic mass murder. Marker at Auschwitz II-Birkenau, the largest killing centre, where about 1.1 million people, about a million of them Jews, were murdered.

story.en:
From 1933 the Nazi regime drove Jews out of public life, stripped them of citizenship under the Nuremberg Laws of 1935 and unleashed the Kristallnacht pogrom in 1938. After the conquest of Poland in 1939, Jews were forced into ghettos, and a secret "euthanasia" programme killed tens of thousands of disabled people, developing the gassing methods later used in the camps.

The invasion of the Soviet Union in June 1941 turned persecution into genocide. Mobile killing units and police battalions shot Jewish men, women and children by the hundreds of thousands; at Babi Yar outside Kyiv more than 33,000 were killed in two days. Gassing began at Chełmno in December. On 20 January 1942, at a villa by the Wannsee lake in Berlin, Reinhard Heydrich met senior officials to coordinate the deportation of all Europe's Jews. Bełżec, Sobibór and Treblinka killed about 1.7 million people, and Auschwitz-Birkenau became the largest killing centre.

Among the victims was Anne Frank, who hid with her family in Amsterdam from 1942, was betrayed in 1944 and died at Bergen-Belsen in early 1945. Soviet troops reached Auschwitz on 27 January 1945, now International Holocaust Remembrance Day.
story.zh:
从1933年起，纳粹政权把犹太人逐出公共生活，1935年又以《纽伦堡法》剥夺其公民权，1938年更发动了“水晶之夜”大迫害。1939年征服波兰后，犹太人被强行关进隔离区；一项秘密的“安乐死”计划杀害了数以万计的残疾人，并发展出后来在集中营中使用的毒气杀人方法。

1941年6月入侵苏联，使迫害演变为种族灭绝。流动屠杀部队和警察营枪杀了数十万犹太男女老幼；在基辅城外的娘子谷，两天之内就有三万三千多人遇害。12月，海乌姆诺开始使用毒气杀人。1942年1月20日，莱因哈德·海德里希在柏林万湖畔的一座别墅里召集高级官员，协调把全欧洲犹太人押送东方的行动。贝乌热茨、索比堡和特雷布林卡三座灭绝营杀害了约170万人，奥斯威辛—比克瑙则成为规模最大的屠杀中心。

受害者中有安妮·弗兰克。她从1942年起与家人藏身阿姆斯特丹，1944年遭人告发被捕，1945年初死于贝尔根—贝尔森集中营。1945年1月27日苏军抵达奥斯威辛，这一天如今是国际大屠杀纪念日。

summary.en: As Allied armies broke out of Normandy, the Resistance in Paris rose on 19 August 1944. General Leclerc's French 2nd Armoured Division entered on 24–25 August, and the German commander, Dietrich von Choltitz, surrendered on the 25th. That evening Charles de Gaulle spoke at the Hôtel de Ville, and next day he led a victory walk down the Champs-Élysées.
summary.zh: 盟军从诺曼底突破之际，巴黎抵抗力量于1944年8月19日起义。勒克莱尔将军的法国第2装甲师于8月24日至25日开进巴黎，德军城防司令迪特里希·冯·肖尔蒂茨将军于25日投降。当晚夏尔·戴高乐在市政厅发表讲话，26日又率众沿香榭丽舍大街徒步游行庆祝胜利。

sources.title: Matthew Cobb, Eleven Days in August: The Liberation of Paris in 1944 (2013)
Antony Beevor and Artemis Cooper, Paris After the Liberation, 1944–1949 (1994)

note: Placed at the Hôtel de Ville, where the first Free French troops arrived on the night of 24 August and de Gaulle spoke on the 25th (Wikidata's coordinates are near the Étoile). The uprising began on 19 August; the date shown is the German surrender.

story.en:
General Eisenhower meant to bypass Paris, sparing fuel and avoiding a costly fight for a city of millions. Parisians forced the issue. The police went on strike on 15 August, and on the 19th Resistance fighters seized the prefecture of police and other buildings and threw up barricades. De Gaulle, anxious that the Communist-led resistance or chaos might fill the vacuum, pressed Eisenhower to send in French troops.

On the evening of 24 August a small column of Leclerc's division under Captain Raymond Dronne reached the Hôtel de Ville; many of its men were exiled Spanish Republicans of the company known as La Nueve. Church bells rang across the city. Hitler had ordered that Paris be left only as a field of ruins, but Choltitz did not carry out large-scale demolitions, though historians doubt his later claim to have saved the city on purpose.

At the Hôtel de Ville de Gaulle declared Paris liberated by its own people, with the help of the armies of France, barely mentioning the Allies. Shots rang out during the thanksgiving at Notre-Dame on the 26th, and a harsh settling of scores with collaborators followed.
story.zh:
艾森豪威尔将军原打算绕过巴黎，以节省燃料，避免为一座数百万人口的城市付出高昂代价。巴黎人却迫使局势改变。8月15日警察罢工；19日，抵抗战士占领警察局等建筑并筑起街垒。戴高乐担心由共产党领导的抵抗力量或混乱局面会填补权力真空，于是力促艾森豪威尔派法军进城。

8月24日傍晚，勒克莱尔师由雷蒙·德龙上尉率领的一支小部队抵达市政厅，其中许多人是流亡的西班牙共和派，所属连队被称为“第九连”。全城教堂钟声齐鸣。希特勒曾下令巴黎要么守住，要么只留下一片废墟，但肖尔蒂茨没有实施大规模爆破；不过，对于他后来声称自己是有意保全巴黎，历史学家多有怀疑。

戴高乐在市政厅宣告，巴黎是由它自己的人民在法国军队的帮助下解放的，几乎只字未提盟军。26日巴黎圣母院举行感恩仪式时响起枪声，随后便是对通敌者的严厉清算。

summary.en: From 20 November 1945 to 1 October 1946 an International Military Tribunal of the United States, Britain, the Soviet Union and France tried 22 leading Nazis in Nuremberg's Palace of Justice for conspiracy, crimes against peace, war crimes and crimes against humanity. Twelve were sentenced to death, seven imprisoned and three acquitted; the trial laid foundations of international criminal law.
summary.zh: 1945年11月20日至1946年10月1日，由美、英、苏、法四国组成的国际军事法庭在纽伦堡司法宫审判了22名纳粹首要人物，罪名为共谋罪、破坏和平罪、战争罪和反人类罪。其中12人被判死刑，7人被判监禁，3人无罪释放。这次审判为国际刑法奠定了基础。

sources.title: Ann Tusa and John Tusa, The Nuremberg Trial (1983)

note: Coordinates follow Wikidata (Palace of Justice, Courtroom 600). The dates cover the main trial before the International Military Tribunal; twelve later trials were held there by US military courts until 1949.

story.en:
The Allies set the rules in the London Charter of August 1945. Nuremberg was chosen partly because its Palace of Justice had survived the bombing and had a prison attached, and partly because the city had hosted the Nazi party rallies. Twenty-four men were indicted; the labour leader Robert Ley killed himself before the trial, the industrialist Gustav Krupp was found unfit, and Martin Bormann was tried in absentia.

In the dock sat Hermann Göring, Rudolf Hess, Joachim von Ribbentrop, Albert Speer and others. The chief American prosecutor, Robert H. Jackson, built the case largely on the regime's own documents, and the court watched film shot in the liberated camps. The tribunal rejected the defence that the accused were only obeying orders, and established that individuals, not just states, could be held responsible for such crimes.

Göring took poison hours before he was due to hang; ten others were executed on 16 October 1946. Critics called it victors' justice, noting that Soviet prosecutors tried to blame Germany for the Katyn massacre. Its principles nonetheless shaped the Genocide Convention of 1948 and, decades later, the International Criminal Court.
story.zh:
盟国在1945年8月的《伦敦宪章》中确定了审判规则。选择纽伦堡，一是因为那里的司法宫躲过了轰炸，还附设监狱；二是因为这座城市曾是纳粹党代会的举办地。共有24人被起诉：劳工阵线头目罗伯特·莱伊在开庭前自杀，工业家古斯塔夫·克虏伯被认定无行为能力，马丁·鲍曼则被缺席审判。

被告席上坐着赫尔曼·戈林、鲁道夫·赫斯、约阿希姆·冯·里宾特洛甫、阿尔贝特·施佩尔等人。美国首席检察官罗伯特·H. 杰克逊主要依靠纳粹政权自己的档案定案，法庭还放映了在解放后的集中营里拍摄的影片。法庭驳回了被告“只是奉命行事”的辩护，确立了个人而不仅是国家须为此类罪行承担责任的原则。

戈林在行刑前几小时服毒自杀；另外十人于1946年10月16日被处以绞刑。批评者称之为“胜利者的正义”，并指出苏联检察官曾试图把卡廷惨案嫁祸给德国。尽管如此，审判所确立的原则影响了1948年的《防止及惩治灭绝种族罪公约》，并在数十年后促成了国际刑事法院的建立。

summary.en: On 24 June 1948, after the Western powers introduced the Deutsche Mark, the Soviet Union cut road, rail and water links to West Berlin. American and British aircraft flew in food and coal for more than two million people for almost a year, some 2.3 million tons in all, until Stalin lifted the blockade on 12 May 1949.
summary.zh: 1948年6月24日，西方国家推行德国马克之后，苏联切断了通往西柏林的公路、铁路和水路。美英飞机为两百多万居民空运食品和煤炭近一年，总计约230万吨，直到1949年5月12日斯大林解除封锁。

sources.title: Daniel F. Harrington, Berlin on the Brink: The Blockade, the Airlift, and the Early Cold War (2012)

note: Placed at Tempelhof airport, main terminus of the airlift. Flights continued until 30 September 1949 to build up stocks. Tonnage figures vary by source (Britannica says nearly two million tons; about 2.3 million is the usual official total).

story.en:
By 1948 the Western Allies were preparing a West German state, and on 20 June they replaced the worthless Reichsmark in their zones with the Deutsche Mark. Moscow answered by closing every land route to the western sectors of Berlin, which lay some 160 km inside the Soviet zone. Only three air corridors, guaranteed by agreement, remained open.

The American military governor, General Lucius Clay, and the British government decided to supply the city by air, something many experts thought impossible. Under General William Tunner the airlift became a conveyor belt, with aircraft landing every few minutes at Tempelhof and Gatow and, from November, at a new airfield at Tegel built by Berliners, many of them women, in about three months. On 9 September 1948 Mayor Ernst Reuter told a vast crowd at the Reichstag that the peoples of the world should look upon this city. An American pilot, Gail Halvorsen, won hearts by dropping sweets on tiny parachutes to children. Dozens of airmen died in crashes.

On the "Easter Parade" of 16 April 1949 nearly 13,000 tons were landed in a day. Stalin gave up in May. The crisis hastened the founding of NATO and of the Federal Republic.
story.zh:
到1948年，西方盟国已在筹建西德国家；6月20日，它们在各自占领区以德国马克取代形同废纸的帝国马克。莫斯科的回应是封锁通往柏林西区的全部陆路——西柏林地处苏占区腹地约160公里处，只剩下协议保障的三条空中走廊仍然开放。

美国军事总督卢修斯·克莱将军和英国政府决定以空运为全城供给，许多专家都认为这不可能做到。在威廉·坦纳将军指挥下，空运成了一条传送带：飞机每隔几分钟就在滕珀尔霍夫和加图机场降落一架；从11月起又启用了泰格尔新机场，这座机场由柏林市民（其中许多是妇女）用大约三个月建成。1948年9月9日，市长恩斯特·罗伊特在国会大厦前向人山人海的群众呼吁：世界各国人民，请看看这座城市！美国飞行员盖尔·哈尔沃森用小降落伞给孩子们空投糖果，赢得了人心。数十名飞行人员在事故中丧生。

1949年4月16日的“复活节大游行”中，一天之内运抵近1.3万吨物资。斯大林于5月放弃封锁。这场危机加速了北约和联邦德国的成立。

summary.en: On 9 May 1950 French foreign minister Robert Schuman proposed placing French and West German coal and steel production under a common High Authority open to other European countries, so that war between them would become materially impossible. Drafted by Jean Monnet, it led to the six-nation European Coal and Steel Community (1951–52); 9 May is now Europe Day.
summary.zh: 1950年5月9日，法国外长罗贝尔·舒曼提议把法国和西德的煤钢生产置于一个对其他欧洲国家开放的共同高级机构管理之下，使两国之间的战争在物质上变得不可能。这一由让·莫内起草的计划促成了1951至1952年六国欧洲煤钢共同体的建立；5月9日如今是“欧洲日”。

sources.title: European Union: The Schuman Declaration, 9 May 1950 (official text)
John Gillingham, Coal, Steel, and the Rebirth of Europe, 1945–1955 (1991)

note: Placed at the French foreign ministry on the Quai d'Orsay, where Schuman read the declaration in the Salon de l'Horloge. The Treaty of Paris creating the ECSC was signed on 18 April 1951 and took effect in July 1952. The Fourth French Republic has no polity id.

story.en:
Five years after the war, France faced a dilemma. The United States wanted West Germany's industry revived, and the French feared that a rearmed Ruhr would again threaten them. Jean Monnet, head of France's planning office, proposed a way out: instead of controlling Germany, share sovereignty with it over the very industries that made war possible.

Monnet's small team drafted the text in secret. Schuman, born in Luxembourg and raised in German-ruled Lorraine, was well placed to champion it. On the morning of 9 May he obtained Chancellor Konrad Adenauer's agreement by private letter, got it through the French cabinet, and that evening read it to the press in the Salon de l'Horloge. Europe, it said, would not be built all at once, but through concrete achievements that first create real solidarity.

France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg signed the Treaty of Paris in April 1951; Britain stayed out. The High Authority, with Monnet as its first president, began work in Luxembourg in 1952. The community was the seed of the European Economic Community and today's European Union.
story.zh:
战后五年，法国陷入两难：美国希望复兴西德工业，法国人却担心重新武装起来的鲁尔区会再次威胁自己。法国计划总署署长让·莫内提出了出路：与其控制德国，不如在恰恰能够支撑战争的那些产业上与德国分享主权。

莫内的小团队秘密起草了宣言文本。舒曼生于卢森堡，在德国统治下的洛林长大，由他来倡导此事再合适不过。5月9日上午，他通过私人信件取得联邦总理康拉德·阿登纳的同意，随后在法国内阁获得通过，当晚在“时钟厅”向记者宣读。宣言说，欧洲不会一蹴而就，而要通过具体的成就，首先建立起真正的团结。

1951年4月，法国、西德、意大利、比利时、荷兰和卢森堡签署《巴黎条约》，英国未参加。以莫内为首任主席的高级机构于1952年在卢森堡开始运作。这个共同体正是欧洲经济共同体和今日欧洲联盟的萌芽。

name.en: Discovery of the DNA double helix

summary.en: In a one-page letter in Nature on 25 April 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick of the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge proposed that DNA is a double helix of two complementary strands. Their model drew on X-ray data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins at King's College London, whose papers appeared alongside it, and suggested how genes are copied.
summary.zh: 1953年4月25日，剑桥卡文迪许实验室的詹姆斯·沃森和弗朗西斯·克里克在《自然》杂志上发表了一页篇幅的短文，提出DNA是由两条互补链构成的双螺旋。他们的模型借鉴了伦敦国王学院罗莎琳德·富兰克林和莫里斯·威尔金斯的X射线衍射数据（两人的论文刊于同期），并揭示了基因如何复制。

sources.title: J. D. Watson and F. H. C. Crick, "Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids: A Structure for Deoxyribose Nucleic Acid", Nature 171 (1953): 737–738
Brenda Maddox, Rosalind Franklin: The Dark Lady of DNA (2002)

note: The QID is the 1953 Nature paper. Placed at the old Cavendish Laboratory on Free School Lane, Cambridge. Watson, Crick, Franklin and Wilkins have no person ids.

story.en:
By 1951 several laboratories were racing to work out the structure of DNA, recently shown to carry genetic information. At Cambridge the young American James Watson and the British physicist Francis Crick built models rather than doing experiments. Their first attempt, a three-stranded helix, collapsed when Rosalind Franklin pointed out that it ignored basic facts about water content.

At King's College London Franklin and her student Raymond Gosling produced the sharpest X-ray pictures of DNA yet, including the image later called Photograph 51. In January 1953 Maurice Wilkins showed it to Watson without her knowledge, and an unpublished research report containing her measurements reached Crick through Max Perutz. With these clues and Erwin Chargaff's ratios of the bases, Watson and Crick realised that adenine pairs with thymine and guanine with cytosine, holding two strands together like the rungs of a twisted ladder. Watson later wrote that Crick announced in the Eagle pub that they had found the secret of life; Crick said he did not remember it.

Their paper noted, with famous understatement, that the pairing immediately suggested a copying mechanism. Watson, Crick and Wilkins shared the 1962 Nobel Prize; Franklin had died of cancer in 1958, aged 37.
story.zh:
到1951年，DNA刚被证明携带遗传信息，几个实验室正竞相破解它的结构。在剑桥，年轻的美国人詹姆斯·沃森和英国物理学家弗朗西斯·克里克不做实验，而是搭建模型。他们的第一个模型是三链螺旋，罗莎琳德·富兰克林指出它忽视了含水量等基本事实，模型随即被推翻。

在伦敦国王学院，富兰克林和她的学生雷蒙德·戈斯林拍出了当时最清晰的DNA X射线照片，包括后来被称为“51号照片”的那一张。1953年1月，莫里斯·威尔金斯在富兰克林不知情的情况下把照片给沃森看了；一份载有她测量数据的未发表研究报告也经马克斯·佩鲁茨之手到了克里克那里。凭借这些线索和埃尔文·查加夫关于碱基比例的规律，沃森和克里克意识到腺嘌呤与胸腺嘧啶配对、鸟嘌呤与胞嘧啶配对，像扭曲梯子的横档一样把两条链连在一起。沃森后来写道，克里克在老鹰酒吧宣布他们找到了生命的秘密；克里克则说自己不记得有这回事。

他们的论文以著名的轻描淡写指出，这种配对方式立即提示了一种复制机制。1962年，沃森、克里克和威尔金斯分享了诺贝尔奖；富兰克林已于1958年因癌症去世，年仅37岁。

summary.en: In the early hours of 13 August 1961 East German police and soldiers sealed the border between East and West Berlin with barbed wire, soon replaced by concrete. Approved by Khrushchev, the barrier stopped the flight of millions of East Germans to the West. It divided the city for 28 years, and at least 140 people died at it.
summary.zh: 1961年8月13日凌晨，东德警察和士兵用铁丝网封锁了东西柏林之间的边界，不久又代之以混凝土墙。这道经赫鲁晓夫批准的屏障阻断了数百万东德人向西方的出逃。它把柏林分隔了28年，至少有140人死于柏林墙下。

sources.title: Frederick Taylor, The Berlin Wall: A World Divided, 1961–1989 (2006)
Berlin Wall Memorial (Gedenkstätte Berliner Mauer), Bernauer Strasse

note: Placed at the Berlin Wall Memorial on Bernauer Strasse. Wikidata's English description says 3 August, but its point in time is 13 August, which is correct. About 2.5 million people had fled East Germany between 1949 and 1961 (Britannica).

story.en:
Through the 1950s East Germans voted with their feet, and the open sector border in Berlin was the easiest way out. By the summer of 1961 tens of thousands were leaving every month, many of them young and skilled. In June the East German leader Walter Ulbricht told journalists that no one intended to build a wall. In August, with Moscow's consent, the operation began, organised by the security chief Erich Honecker.

Overnight on 12–13 August streets were torn up and wire strung across them; trains and underground lines were cut. On Bernauer Strasse, where the buildings stood in the East but the pavement belonged to the West, residents jumped from their windows into firemen's nets, and some died. On 15 August a young border guard, Conrad Schumann, leapt over the wire, a moment caught in a famous photograph.

The Western powers protested but did not act, and President Kennedy reportedly remarked that a wall was better than a war. In October American and Soviet tanks faced each other at Checkpoint Charlie. The wall grew into a death strip of concrete, fences and watchtowers until it was opened on 9 November 1989.
story.zh:
整个50年代，东德人用脚投票，柏林开放的区界是最便捷的出逃通道。到1961年夏，每月出走的人数达数万，其中许多是年轻的技术人才。6月，东德领导人瓦尔特·乌布利希对记者说，没有人打算修建一道墙。8月，在莫斯科同意下，由安全事务负责人埃里希·昂纳克组织的行动开始了。

8月12日至13日夜间，街道被挖断，铁丝网横贯其上；火车和地铁线路也被切断。在贝尔瑙尔大街，房屋属于东区，人行道却属于西区，居民们从窗口跳进消防员张开的救生网，有人因此丧生。8月15日，年轻的边防士兵康拉德·舒曼纵身跃过铁丝网，这一瞬间被拍成了一张著名照片。

西方大国提出抗议，却没有采取行动；据说肯尼迪总统私下表示，一堵墙总比一场战争好。10月，美苏坦克在查理检查站对峙。此后柏林墙逐步扩建成由混凝土墙、铁丝网和瞭望塔组成的“死亡地带”，直到1989年11月9日才被打开。

summary.en: Student protests that began at Nanterre and spread to the Sorbonne in May 1968 turned into nights of street fighting in the Latin Quarter and then France's largest general strike, with perhaps seven to ten million workers out. Shaken, de Gaulle dissolved the National Assembly; his supporters won a landslide in June, but he resigned the following year.
summary.zh: 1968年5月，始于南泰尔、蔓延至索邦的学生抗议，演变为拉丁区连续数夜的街头冲突，进而发展为法国史上规模最大的总罢工，罢工工人可能多达七百万至一千万。受到震动的戴高乐解散国民议会；6月他的支持者在选举中大胜，但他本人于次年辞职。

sources.title: Kristin Ross, May '68 and Its Afterlives (2002)
Michael Seidman, The Imaginary Revolution: Parisian Students and Workers in 1968 (2004)

note: Placed at the Sorbonne, whose police evacuation on 3 May set off the Paris protests. Striker numbers are estimates. De Gaulle resigned in April 1969 after losing a referendum.

summary.en: On 25 April 1974 junior officers of the Armed Forces Movement overthrew Portugal's Estado Novo dictatorship, founded by António de Oliveira Salazar, in a nearly bloodless coup cheered by crowds in Lisbon who put carnations in the soldiers' rifles. The revolution ended the colonial wars, led to independence for Portugal's African colonies in 1974–75 and opened the way to democracy.
summary.zh: 1974年4月25日，“武装部队运动”的中下级军官推翻了萨拉查创立的葡萄牙“新国家”独裁政权。这场几乎未流血的政变受到里斯本民众欢呼，人们把康乃馨插进士兵的枪管。革命结束了殖民战争，使葡属非洲殖民地在1974至1975年间相继独立，并为民主开辟了道路。

sources.title: Kenneth Maxwell, The Making of Portuguese Democracy (1995)

note: Placed at the Largo do Carmo, Lisbon, where Marcelo Caetano surrendered at the Carmo barracks of the Republican National Guard. The Estado Novo has no polity id.

story.en:
For nearly half a century Portugal was ruled by the Estado Novo of Salazar and, from 1968, his successor Marcelo Caetano. From 1961 the regime fought wars against independence movements in Angola, Mozambique and Guinea-Bissau that consumed much of the budget and a generation of conscripts. In February 1974 General António de Spínola published a book arguing that the wars could not be won by force.

The young officers of the Armed Forces Movement used the radio for their signals. Late on 24 April a station played Portugal's Eurovision song "E depois do adeus"; just after midnight another broadcast "Grândola, Vila Morena", a banned song by Zeca Afonso, and the troops moved. Captain Salgueiro Maia's column surrounded the Carmo barracks, where Caetano had taken refuge, and in the evening he handed power to Spínola. A restaurant worker, Celeste Caeiro, is remembered for giving carnations to soldiers, and the flowers spread through the crowds. Four people died when secret police agents fired from their headquarters.

After two turbulent years, a democratic constitution was adopted in 1976. The colonies became independent, and 25 April is now Freedom Day.
story.zh:
近半个世纪里，葡萄牙一直处于萨拉查及其1968年起的继任者马塞洛·卡埃塔诺的“新国家”统治之下。从1961年起，政权在安哥拉、莫桑比克和几内亚比绍与独立运动作战，战争耗去大量预算，也耗去了一代应征青年。1974年2月，安东尼奥·德斯皮诺拉将军出书，认为这些战争无法以武力取胜。

“武装部队运动”的青年军官们用电台传递信号。4月24日深夜，一家电台播放了葡萄牙的欧洲歌唱大赛参赛曲《告别之后》；午夜刚过，另一家电台播出了何塞·阿方索的禁歌《格朗多拉，黝黑的小镇》，部队随即出动。萨尔盖鲁·马亚上尉的部队包围了卡埃塔诺藏身的卡尔莫兵营，当晚卡埃塔诺把权力交给了斯皮诺拉。人们记得一位名叫塞莱斯特·凯罗的餐馆女工把康乃馨送给士兵，鲜花随即在人群中传开。秘密警察特工从总部开枪，造成四人死亡。

经过两年的动荡，葡萄牙于1976年通过了民主宪法。各殖民地相继独立，4月25日如今是葡萄牙的“自由日”。

summary.en: After Francisco Franco died on 20 November 1975, King Juan Carlos I and his prime minister Adolfo Suárez dismantled the dictatorship from within: the Francoist Cortes voted for political reform in 1976, parties including the Communists were legalised, free elections were held in June 1977, and a democratic constitution was approved by referendum on 6 December 1978.
summary.zh: 1975年11月20日佛朗哥去世后，国王胡安·卡洛斯一世与首相阿道弗·苏亚雷斯从体制内部拆解了独裁：1976年佛朗哥时代的议会投票通过政治改革，包括共产党在内的各政党获得合法地位，1977年6月举行自由选举，1978年12月6日民主宪法经全民公决通过。

sources.title: Paul Preston, The Triumph of Democracy in Spain (1986)
Charles Powell, Juan Carlos of Spain: Self-Made Monarch (1996)

note: Placed at the Congress of Deputies, Madrid. The end point is debated: this record ends with the 1978 constitution; Wikidata ends the transition in 1983, and many historians extend it to the failed coup of February 1981 or the Socialist election victory of October 1982.

summary.en: On 3 October 1990, less than a year after the Berlin Wall opened, the German Democratic Republic acceded to the Federal Republic, creating a united Germany within NATO and the European Community. East Germany's first free election in March, a currency union in July and the Two Plus Four Treaty with the wartime Allies in September cleared the way.
summary.zh: 1990年10月3日，柏林墙开放还不到一年，德意志民主共和国加入联邦德国，一个留在北约和欧洲共同体之内的统一德国由此诞生。此前，东德在3月举行了首次自由选举，7月实现货币联盟，9月又与四个战时盟国签订了《二加四条约》，为统一扫清了道路。

sources.title: Britannica: Germany – The era of partition
Mary Elise Sarotte, 1989: The Struggle to Create Post–Cold War Europe (2009)
Konrad H. Jarausch, The Rush to German Unity (1994)

note: Placed at the Reichstag building, Berlin, scene of the celebrations on the night of 2–3 October. Wikidata's start date (9 November 1989) is the opening of the Wall.

story.en:
When the Wall opened in November 1989, few expected unity within a year. But East Germans kept leaving, and the chant at demonstrations shifted from "We are the people" to "We are one people". Chancellor Helmut Kohl seized the moment with a ten-point plan, and in the Volkskammer election of 18 March 1990 a coalition backed by his Christian Democrats won decisively on a promise of rapid unification.

On 1 July the Deutsche Mark replaced the East German mark, mostly at one to one for wages and savings, a generous rate that made East German industry uncompetitive overnight. The external obstacles were harder. Britain and France were wary, and the Soviet Union still had some 380,000 troops in the East. In July Mikhail Gorbachev accepted that a united Germany could stay in NATO, in return for limits on German forces and West German money for the Soviet withdrawal. The Two Plus Four Treaty, signed in Moscow on 12 September, ended the Allies' occupation rights and confirmed the Oder–Neisse border with Poland.

At midnight on 2–3 October the federal flag was raised before the Reichstag. Five new states joined the Federal Republic, and years of costly reconstruction followed.
story.zh:
1989年11月柏林墙开放时，几乎没人料到一年之内就会统一。但东德人持续出走，示威者的口号从“我们是人民”变成了“我们是一个民族”。联邦总理赫尔穆特·科尔抓住时机提出“十点计划”；在1990年3月18日的人民议院选举中，由他领导的基督教民主联盟支持的竞选联盟凭借尽快统一的承诺大获全胜。

7月1日，德国马克取代东德马克，工资和储蓄大多按一比一兑换。这一优厚的比率使东德工业一夜之间丧失了竞争力。外部障碍更加棘手：英法心存疑虑，苏联在东德还驻有38万军队。7月，米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫同意统一后的德国留在北约，条件是限制德国兵力，并由西德出资支持苏军撤离。9月12日在莫斯科签署的《二加四条约》结束了盟国的占领权，并确认了德波之间的奥得河—尼斯河边界。

10月2日至3日午夜，联邦国旗在国会大厦前升起。五个新的州加入联邦共和国，此后是多年代价高昂的重建。

summary.en: Signed in Maastricht on 7 February 1992 by the twelve members of the European Community, the Treaty on European Union created the EU, introduced EU citizenship and common foreign, security and justice policies, and set a timetable and criteria for economic and monetary union. After hard-fought ratifications, above all in Denmark, it entered into force on 1 November 1993.
summary.zh: 1992年2月7日，欧洲共同体十二个成员国在马斯特里赫特签署《欧洲联盟条约》。条约创建了欧盟，设立欧盟公民身份以及共同外交、安全和司法政策，并为经济与货币联盟规定了时间表和趋同标准。经过一番艰难的批准过程（尤以丹麦为甚），条约于1993年11月1日生效。

sources.title: Desmond Dinan, Ever Closer Union: An Introduction to European Integration (4th ed., 2010)

note: Placed at the Gouvernement aan de Maas, the provincial government building in Maastricht where it was signed. The text was agreed at the European Council there in December 1991.

story.en:
The end of the Cold War and the reunification of Germany gave new urgency to plans for deeper integration. Helmut Kohl and François Mitterrand saw a common currency and closer political union as a way to anchor a larger Germany firmly in Europe, building on Jacques Delors's 1989 report on monetary union.

Agreed at a summit in Maastricht in December 1991, the treaty set up a European Union resting on three pillars: the existing communities, a common foreign and security policy, and cooperation in justice and home affairs. It created citizenship of the Union and laid down convergence criteria for joining the single currency, including limits on inflation, budget deficits of no more than 3 per cent of output and public debt of 60 per cent. Britain negotiated opt-outs from the currency and the social chapter.

Ratification proved fraught. Danish voters rejected the treaty in June 1992 and approved it the next year only after opt-outs were granted; French voters accepted it by a hair in September, in the same month that currency turmoil forced sterling and the lira out of the exchange-rate mechanism. The euro followed in 1999.
story.zh:
冷战结束和德国统一，使深化一体化的计划变得更加紧迫。赫尔穆特·科尔和弗朗索瓦·密特朗认为，在雅克·德洛尔1989年关于货币联盟的报告基础上推进单一货币和更紧密的政治联盟，可以把扩大后的德国牢牢系在欧洲之中。

条约于1991年12月在马斯特里赫特峰会上达成，建立了以三大支柱为基础的欧洲联盟：原有的各共同体、共同外交与安全政策，以及司法与内政合作。它创设了联盟公民身份，并为加入单一货币规定了趋同标准，包括限制通货膨胀、财政赤字不超过国内生产总值的3%、公共债务不超过60%。英国争取到了不参加单一货币和社会章程的豁免。

批准过程一波三折。1992年6月丹麦选民否决了条约，次年在获得若干豁免后才予以通过；同年9月法国选民以微弱多数批准，同月的货币风暴迫使英镑和里拉退出欧洲汇率机制。1999年欧元随之诞生。

name.zh: 《贝尔法斯特协议》（耶稣受难日协议）

summary.en: Signed in Belfast on Good Friday, 10 April 1998, by the British and Irish governments and most Northern Ireland parties, the agreement created a power-sharing assembly and executive and cross-border bodies, and established that Northern Ireland's status could change only with majority consent. Approved by referendums north and south, it largely ended the Troubles, in which about 3,500 people died.
summary.zh: 1998年4月10日耶稣受难日，英国和爱尔兰两国政府与北爱尔兰大多数政党在贝尔法斯特签署协议，设立分权共治的议会和行政机构以及跨境机构，并确立北爱尔兰的地位只有经多数人同意才能改变。协议经南北两地全民公决通过，基本结束了造成约3500人死亡的北爱尔兰问题动乱。

note: Placed at Castle Buildings on the Stormont estate, Belfast, where the final talks took place. The referendums of 22 May 1998 approved it by 71 per cent in Northern Ireland and 94 per cent in the Republic. The Republic of Ireland has no polity id.

story.en:
After the IRA and loyalist ceasefires of the mid-1990s, multi-party talks opened under the chairmanship of the former US senator George Mitchell. Sinn Féin joined in 1997 after the IRA renewed its ceasefire, while Ian Paisley's Democratic Unionists walked out. Mitchell set a deadline of Easter 1998. Arriving in Belfast for the last days, Tony Blair said he felt the hand of history on his shoulder; he and the Irish taoiseach, Bertie Ahern, stayed through the final all-night session.

The agreement balanced the two traditions. Northern Ireland would stay in the United Kingdom as long as a majority wished, and the Republic amended its constitution to drop its territorial claim; in return nationalists gained power-sharing, cross-border institutions and the right for people to be Irish, British or both. Prisoner releases, police reform and the decommissioning of paramilitary weapons were included.

The unionist David Trimble and the nationalist John Hume won the Nobel Peace Prize that year. Peace remained fragile: the Omagh bombing in August killed 29 people, and the institutions were suspended several times before the DUP and Sinn Féin agreed to share power in 2007.
story.zh:
20世纪90年代中期爱尔兰共和军和亲英派武装相继停火后，由美国前参议员乔治·米切尔主持的多党会谈开始举行。1997年爱尔兰共和军恢复停火后，新芬党加入会谈，伊恩·佩斯利的民主统一党则退出。米切尔把最后期限定在1998年复活节。托尼·布莱尔在最后几天抵达贝尔法斯特时说，他感到历史之手搭在了自己肩上；他与爱尔兰总理伯蒂·埃亨一起熬过了最后通宵达旦的谈判。

协议在两种传统之间取得平衡：只要多数人愿意，北爱尔兰就留在英国，爱尔兰共和国则修改宪法、放弃领土主张；作为交换，民族主义者获得了分权共治、跨境机构，以及民众可以选择做爱尔兰人、英国人或两者兼是的权利。协议还涵盖释放囚犯、警察改革和准军事组织解除武装等内容。

统一党人戴维·特林布尔和民族主义者约翰·休姆当年获得诺贝尔和平奖。和平依然脆弱：同年8月的奥马爆炸案造成29人死亡，自治机构也几度中止，直到2007年民主统一党与新芬党才同意共同执政。

summary.en: On 1 January 1999 eleven EU countries irrevocably fixed their exchange rates and adopted the euro, managed by the European Central Bank in Frankfurt, for non-cash transactions. Euro banknotes and coins followed on 1 January 2002 in twelve countries, the largest cash changeover in history, replacing currencies such as the Deutsche Mark, the franc and the lira.
summary.zh: 1999年1月1日，十一个欧盟国家不可撤销地锁定汇率，在非现金交易中采用由法兰克福欧洲中央银行管理的欧元。2002年1月1日，欧元纸币和硬币在十二个国家投入流通，取代了德国马克、法郎、里拉等货币，这是史上规模最大的现金更换。

sources.title: David Marsh, The Euro: The Politics of the New Global Currency (2009)
European Central Bank: history of the euro

note: Year 1999 (launch as a currency) is chosen, with endYear 2002 for the cash changeover; Wikidata dates the currency from 2002. Placed at the Eurotower in Frankfurt, the ECB's seat from 1998. The QID is the currency itself; Wikidata has no separate item for its introduction. Greece joined in 2001, making twelve.

summary.en: In a referendum on 23 June 2016 the United Kingdom voted by 51.9 to 48.1 per cent to leave the European Union. After years of parliamentary deadlock over the terms and two changes of prime minister, the UK left on 31 January 2020; the transition period ended on 31 December 2020 with a limited trade agreement.
summary.zh: 2016年6月23日，英国全民公投以51.9%对48.1%决定退出欧盟。此后议会围绕脱欧条件僵持数年，首相两度易人，英国最终于2020年1月31日正式脱欧；过渡期于2020年12月31日结束，双方达成了一项范围有限的贸易协定。

sources.title: Tim Shipman, All Out War: The Full Story of How Brexit Sank Britain's Political Class (2016)

note: Placed at the Palace of Westminster. Wikidata's point in time is the withdrawal date (31 January 2020); the record starts with the referendum. Article 50 was triggered on 29 March 2017.
